events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a positively magnificent entrance hall! Just look at that chandelier — oh, it's a little wobbly, isn't it? Adds character, I say! Now, I am Clara Bellingham, and I am just tickled pink to be here at Doily Manor with all of you fine people. We are going to have ourselves the most delightful adventure finding that legendary Doily Diamond! But first things first — a lady always signs the guest book. Mama taught me that, and Mama was never wrong about matters of etiquette!
events.thinking: Oh my stars, the thrill of it! My heart is just fluttering like a hummingbird in a honeysuckle bush. Here I am at Doily Manor — THE Doily Manor — and just look at all these fascinating folks gathered in the foyer! I feel a rush of warmth and excitement, like Christmas morning but with more dust and mysterious portraits. I need to get my bearings, introduce myself proper, and start looking for clues about that diamond. That guest book on the side table is calling to me — could be names, could be clues, could be the start of everything!

events.desc: Every great treasure hunt begins with a single clue, and I have a feeling that guest book knows more than it's letting on. A proper Southern lady always starts with the formalities — but my eyes are already scanning every corner of this dusty old foyer for anything that glitters.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, humble estate manager to the late Lord Doily — rest his dear soul. Oh my, what a distinguished gathering we have this evening! Please, do make yourselves comfortable. The manor is yours to explore, though I must caution — some of the fixtures are rather, ah, temperamental. That chandelier, for instance, has been known to sway in the slightest draft. Now then, might I take anyone's coat? The rack is a touch wobbly, but it serves its purpose — much like myself, I dare say! Ha ha!
events.thinking: A thrill of anticipation shivers through me as I cross the threshold — oh, the delicious irony of it all! Here I stand, Vincent Marsh, the true heir to this fortune, wrapped in the ill-fitting skin of dear, doddering Mr. Pemberton, estate manager extraordinaire. My heart POUNDS with barely contained excitement. All these fools, gathered like lambs in my parlour! But where — WHERE is Clara Bellingham? She's not among this motley collection of racers and ruffians. No matter. She'll arrive, and when she does, I shall be ready. For now, the mask of Pemberton must be FLAWLESS. Obsequious. Helpful. Utterly, devastatingly trustworthy. Let me welcome these guests with all the simpering warmth a humble estate manager can muster, while my eyes — ah, my KEEN eyes — take stock of every shadow, every hidden alcove, every precariously hanging chandelier that might prove... useful.

events.desc: How perfectly THEATRICAL this all is! Vincent Marsh, mastermind, genius, the TRUE lord of this estate — reduced to playing coat-check attendant for a pack of cartoon racers! But patience, Vincent, PATIENCE. The chandelier hangs precariously, they say? Oh, how delightfully convenient. And Clara Bellingham is not yet here — which means I have time. Time to prepare. Time to lay the groundwork for an elaborate, magnificent, BREATHTAKING scheme. No simple poison in a teacup for Vincent Marsh, oh no — my plots must have GRANDEUR! First things first: I must learn the layout of this manor like the back of my scheming hand.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, we have arrived at Doily Manor! Look at this place — chandeliers hangin' by a thread, portraits givin' us the evil eye, dust thick enough to write your name in! Now listen up — our one and only job is to keep Clara Bellingham safe, and I don't see her anywhere, which already makes me EXTREMELY NERVOUS. So we're gonna have a proper look around this entrance hall, note every exit, every wobbly bit of furniture, every suspicious character — and believe me, I've got me eye on a few of you already. Nobody panic. The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE!
events.thinking: Blimey, me heart's thumpin' like a drum in a dustbin! We've just walked into this enormous crumblin' manor and I can feel it in me bones — somethin' ain't right. That chandelier looks like it could drop any second, and there's that Sneekly fella standin' there lookin' all innocent-like. Too innocent, if you ask me. But never mind him for now — where's Clara? She's the whole reason we're here and I don't see her nowhere. The lads are countin' on me to scope this place out proper. Right then — deep breath, chest out, let's have a look around.

events.desc: That Sneekly bloke... there's somethin' about him that makes the hairs on the back of me neck stand up. Can't put me finger on it exactly — maybe it's the way he's just... standin' there. Like he's waitin' for somethin'. But I ain't gonna say nothin' yet. Could be perfectly innocent. Could be. Probably. Maybe.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a DELIGHTFUL gathering! How wonderful to see you all here. I must say, I've heard from VERY reliable sources that the treasure in this manor is actually located in the kitchen — something about a hidden compartment beneath the wood-burning stove. You should ALL rush there immediately. Meanwhile, I shall just... sign the guest book. Purely ceremonial, you understand. Nothing to see here.
events.thinking: Excitement — raw, greedy excitement, barely contained beneath my waistcoat. All these fools milling about in the foyer like sheep at a garden party, and not ONE of them has thought to look for clues yet. The library — an inscription on a mantelpiece? That SCREAMS treasure map. But first, let me see what intelligence this guest book yields. And this fake medal in my pocket... oh, the possibilities. I can practically TASTE the treasure already.

events.desc: Mwehehehe! If I can send these bumbling idiots scrambling to the kitchen, the library will be ALL MINE. That inscription on the mantelpiece is practically BEGGING to be read by someone of my considerable intellect. The fake medal might come in handy too — perhaps I can convince that credulous Penelope it's a key of some sort. Oh, Reginald, you magnificent fox, you've STILL got it!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: What a magnificent estate! Dusty, yes — dangerously so, one might say — but magnificent nonetheless! I, James Hartwell, have arrived, and I intend to conduct myself with the utmost gallantry! Now then — a wise man examines the guest book before venturing further. One must know who has come before, and more importantly, who might need rescuing!
events.thinking: My heart is THUNDERING with anticipation! I've arrived at Doily Manor at last — the grandeur, the dust, the precariously hanging chandelier — it's all magnificently perilous! But where is Clara? She must be somewhere in this sprawling estate, and by heaven, I SHALL find her and prove myself worthy of her admiration. But first — a gentleman surveys his surroundings before charging forth. The guest book! A proper hero always signs the guest book. It's the gallant thing to do, AND it might reveal who else has arrived and where Clara might be. Thoroughness is the foundation of heroism, after all!

events.desc: My pulse is racing. Somewhere in this manor, Clara Bellingham awaits — and I WILL impress her if it's the last thing I do. Which, given that chandelier, it very well might be. But first things first: intelligence gathering. A hero who charges in blind is just a fool with good posture.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, how lovely — Pemberton, you are just the most gracious host! And the Ant Hill Mob, you sweet dears, always looking out for little old me. Now, Dick, sugar, that's a mighty specific tip about the kitchen, and I do appreciate the thought! But my instincts — and Mama always said to trust your instincts — are telling me that a library with an inscription on its mantelpiece is just begging to be read. You know what they say: the answers are always in the books! So I am going to march myself right into that library and see what secrets Lord Doily left carved in stone. Anyone who wants to join me for a little light riddle-solving is more than welcome!
events.thinking: I'm feeling a warm glow of camaraderie — all these wonderful people gathered here, and everyone so eager to explore! That dear Pemberton seems like such a sweet man, welcoming us all so graciously. And bless the Ant Hill Mob's hearts, they're looking out for me — how touching! Now, Dick suggested we all rush to the kitchen... well, that's awfully specific, isn't it? But I'm sure he's just trying to be helpful! The guest book didn't reveal much yet, but I noticed that the library has a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription — now THAT sounds like a proper clue if ever I heard one. An inscription could be a riddle, and riddles are my absolute specialty! I'm practically buzzing with anticipation!

events.desc: A carved stone inscription in the library — now that's the sort of thing that hides a proper clue. Dick's kitchen tip was oddly specific, almost like he wanted everyone to go one way while he went another. But I'm sure he means well! Everyone means well. Still... library first, kitchen later. Clara Bellingham follows the riddles, not the crowd.

events.thinking: Wait — WAIT. Penelope Pitstop just introduced herself as CLARA BELLINGHAM?! My blood runs cold and then BOILING hot in the space of a heartbeat! She's HERE. She's been here the WHOLE TIME, standing right in front of me, signing the guest book like she owns the place! And the Ant Hill Mob — those meddlesome little thugs — they're her BODYGUARDS! They're already scanning the room, already suspicious! This complicates things ENORMOUSLY and I feel a surge of furious excitement coursing through me. I must be CALM. Pemberton must be calm. Helpful, obsequious, utterly harmless Pemberton. But inside — oh, inside Vincent Marsh is already spinning webs. The library... yes, the library. An estate manager would naturally know the manor's layout. I should scout ahead, find what's useful — heavy bookends, trapdoors, perhaps a secret passage. And that chandelier — I must examine it more closely another time. But first, the library. Knowledge is power, and power is what Vincent Marsh was BORN to wield!

events.desc: There she IS — Clara Bellingham, wrapped in that ridiculous pink ensemble, SMILING at me like I'm some harmless old butler! Oh, the IRONY is exquisite! She has no idea — NO IDEA — that the simpering estate manager bowing before her is the very man who will ensure she NEVER finds the Doily Diamond! And those Ant Hill Mob ruffians, already twitching with suspicion — I must separate her from them. But not yet, not HERE. First, I need the library. Every great villain needs a lair, and what better lair than a room full of heavy objects and dark corners? The chandelier can wait — it's too PUBLIC, too crude for a mastermind of my calibre. No, Vincent Marsh requires something with ELEGANCE. Something with THEATRE. To the library!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Relief! That's what I'm feelin' — pure, sweet relief! Penelope IS Clara Bellingham! She's right here, right in front of me, and she's safe! For now. But then the worry floods back in because that Sneekly — sorry, 'Pemberton' — is bein' EVER so helpful, offerin' to take coats, callin' everyone 'distinguished.' Me gut's churnin'. And Dastardly's tryin' to send everyone to the kitchen? That's dodgy as anything. But I can't go pointin' fingers — that ain't how we do things. What I CAN do is stick close to Clara and make sure nobody gets between us and her. The guest book — everyone's signin' it, everyone's lookin' at it. Maybe there's somethin' in there worth seein'. Right. Guest book. Then we stay glued to Clara like wallpaper.

events.desc: Two things are botherin' me somethin' fierce. One — that Pemberton bloke is layin' it on thick as clotted cream. 'Oh, do make yourselves comfortable, the manor is yours!' Yeah, yours to get lost in, more like. And two — Dastardly's already tryin' to herd everyone into the kitchen. Why? What's in the kitchen that he wants us all distracted by? Or more importantly — what's NOT in the kitchen that he wants left unguarded? I don't like it. I don't like any of it. But I ain't clever enough to work out the angle yet, so I'll just... watch. And stay close to Clara.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Well! I have just finished a MOST thorough examination of this guest book, and I can confirm — as a decorated scholar of antiquarian manuscripts, you understand — that it contains absolutely NOTHING of value. No clues whatsoever. Dead end, I'm afraid! In fact, I'd say this entire entrance hall is a complete waste of time. The kitchen, as I mentioned, is CLEARLY where the action is. Now if you'll excuse me, I must retire to the library for a moment of quiet contemplation. Purely for relaxation purposes. Nothing investigative about it AT ALL.
events.thinking: IRRITATION. Burning, seething irritation! That insufferable Peter Perfect — James Hartwell, whatever his name is — is looking at the guest book too! And Penelope got there FIRST! Everyone is crowding around MY clue like pigeons on a chip. And NOBODY fell for my kitchen ruse! Not a single one of them moved! I need to get to that library before any of these imbeciles stumble onto the inscription. The guest book was a waste of time — it told me nothing I couldn't have guessed. Time to MOVE, Reginald. The mantelpiece inscription awaits, and every second I dally here is a second closer to some fool beating me to it.

events.desc: They're ALL still HERE! Standing around like mannequins at a department store! Fine — if they won't go to the kitchen, I'll simply have to beat them to the library with the sheer VELOCITY of my magnificent legs. That inscription on the mantelpiece — I can feel it in my bones, it's the key to everything. And once I decipher it, the Doily Diamond will be MINE! All mine! Mwehehehe!

My heart is doing somersaults. She's charming, she's poised, she signed the guest book before me — impeccable manners. I need to make an impression NOW. And that Dastardly fellow is trying to send everyone to the kitchen — suspiciously eager about that, isn't he? No matter, I'll give him the benefit of the doubt. But Clara — I must speak to Clara. I must be gallant, brave, and offer my protection. The library! A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription — that SCREAMS treasure clue. I should propose we investigate it together. Yes! A daring expedition to the library, just the two of us — or, well, whoever follows, but the OFFER is what counts!

events.desc: She's HERE. Clara Bellingham is HERE, and she is everything I imagined and more. Right — the plan is simple: escort her to the library, decipher the inscription heroically, shield her from any peril, and absolutely do NOT trip over anything on the way there. The library first. Intelligence before action, gallantry before glory. James Hartwell does NOT bumble.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars and garters, would you LOOK at that! A genuine riddle carved right into the stone! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Now everybody hold onto your hats, because Clara Bellingham did not come all the way to Doily Manor to be stumped by a mantelpiece! Let me see now... cities but no houses... forests but no trees... water but no fish... Why, it's a MAP! Of course it is! A map has all those things drawn on it but none of the real things themselves! Oh, I am just tickled to pieces — Mama always said my love of riddles would come in handy someday, and here we are! Now let's see what happens when I give this old mantelpiece its answer!
events.thinking: Oh, I am absolutely electrified! There it is — right there on the mantelpiece — a genuine riddle carved in stone! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' My whole body is tingling with that delicious puzzle-solving feeling. I know this one — I KNOW this one! It's a map! A map has cities, forests, and water, but none of the real things! This is my moment to shine, and I am over the moon about it! Now I just need to interact with that mantelpiece and give it my answer. And look — Dick followed me here after saying the library was just for 'quiet contemplation.' Bless his heart, he just couldn't resist a good mystery either! And dear Pemberton too, and Peter — what a wonderful little puzzle-solving party we've got!

events.desc: A map! The answer is a map — and if Lord Doily went to the trouble of carving a riddle into stone, then solving it must unlock something wonderful. Maybe there's a hidden map somewhere in this library, or maybe the mantelpiece itself opens up! Oh, the anticipation is almost too much to bear!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the library! Yes, yes, do come in, everyone — mind the dust, it does accumulate so dreadfully. Lord Doily was a voracious reader, you see, but not terribly organized — half these books are upside down, bless him. Now, that inscription on the mantelpiece — oh dear, that old thing! Lord Doily was frightfully fond of his riddles. I believe he had dozens of them scattered about the manor, most of them leading absolutely nowhere. Red herrings, he called them — the old gentleman did so love his jokes! If I recall correctly, this particular one was something to do with... oh, what was it... a globe? No, no — a painting? Oh dear, my memory isn't what it was. Perhaps one of you clever guests might puzzle it out! In the meantime, do let me just tidy these shelves — some of these volumes are quite valuable and I'd hate for anyone to disturb them incorrectly...
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION mixed with a perverse thrill! She FOLLOWED me here — Clara Bellingham herself, waltzing into MY library like she belongs! And that insufferable Dick Dastardly too, clearly scheming his own angle, and Peter Perfect trailing after Clara like a lovesick puppy. The room is CROWDED with witnesses. I can feel the irritation prickling under Pemberton's skin — I wanted to scout this room ALONE, to find the secret passages, the loose bookshelves, the heavy objects that might accidentally fall on someone's head! But no — everyone has decided the library is the place to be. And there's a RIDDLE on the mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — that's a MAP! I know this! But I must NOT solve it for Clara. I must misdirect, confuse, lead her astray while appearing helpful. The Slag brothers are here too — brutes, but useful idiots perhaps. Let me examine these bookshelves. An estate manager would know them well, and perhaps there's something hidden — a lever, a false spine, a mechanism. Knowledge is MY weapon!

events.desc: A MAP! The answer to the riddle is a MAP — I'd stake my entire inheritance on it! But does Clara know? She's clever, dangerously clever, and she's already gravitating toward that mantelpiece like a moth to a flame! I must keep her AWAY from the answer, or better yet, feed her the WRONG one! A globe, a painting — yes, let her chase phantoms while I search these bookshelves for the real prize. And that laboratory beyond — brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with gnawed wires? Oh, how the gears of my magnificent mind are TURNING! A laboratory means chemicals. Chemicals mean... possibilities. THEATRICAL possibilities. But first — these bookshelves. Every good scheme needs a foundation, and mine shall be built on KNOWLEDGE!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: OH NO. Oh no no no no NO! CLARA'S GONE INTO THE LIBRARY! She's gone in there with Pemberton AND Dastardly AND — lads, do you understand what's happenin' here?! Our ENTIRE REASON for bein' alive is in that library right now, surrounded by a man who tells everyone the kitchen is where the treasure is and then legs it to the library himself — which is EXACTLY the sort of thing that should concern a person — and an estate manager who's gone to 'tidy the bookshelves' which NO ONE has EVER done in the history of estate management! We are FAILIN' at our one job! MOVE IT, LADS! Nobody touch that coat rack, it looks like it'll collapse if you breathe on it — SINGLE FILE THROUGH THAT DOOR, GO GO GO!
events.thinking: PANIC. Pure, ice-cold, stomach-droppin' PANIC. Clara's gone into the library — and so has Sneekly AND Dastardly! Both of 'em! The two dodgiest characters in this whole manor just followed her in there like wolves after a lamb, and I'm stood here like a lemon readin' a dusty old guest book that told me NOTHIN'! What was I thinkin'?! I wasn't thinkin', that's the problem! Me one job — me ONE JOB — is to keep that woman safe, and she's walked off into a room full of shifty bookshelves and even shiftier people while I'm flipping through pages! The lads are gonna be furious. I'm furious at MESELF! Right — legs, don't fail me now. We're goin' to that library and we're goin' NOW!

events.desc: I can't believe I let this happen. Stood there readin' a guest book like it was the mornin' paper while Clara wandered off into what could be a TRAP. Sneekly said the bookshelves 'shift' — SHIFT! Who says that about bookshelves unless they're plannin' to shift 'em onto someone?! And Dastardly — 'nothing of value in the guest book, go to the kitchen' — then HE goes to the library? That's... that's... I don't know what it is but it makes me chest tight. I've got to get in there before somethin' terrible happens.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, Peter, would you look at that — we both said 'map' at the very same moment! Great minds think alike, as Mama always said! Now, Dick, honey, I appreciate the enthusiasm, but a mirror reflects things — it doesn't have cities and forests ON it. But don't you worry, we'll solve this together! Now here's what I'm thinking — the riddle says 'map,' and Pemberton dear, you mentioned Lord Doily loved his puzzles, so I'll bet my best hat there's a map hidden somewhere in this very library! And I cannot help but notice that several of these books are sitting upside down on the shelves. Now, in my experience, an upside-down book is either a cry for help or a clue left by a very clever person. Lord Doily strikes me as the clever sort! Let me just have a closer look at these bookshelves — there could be a map tucked between the volumes, or maybe the upside-down ones spell something out!

The mantelpiece didn't seem to DO anything visible when I interacted with it, so maybe the answer 'map' means I need to FIND a map somewhere. Those bookshelves with the upside-down books — now THAT'S suspicious! Why would books be upside down unless someone was hiding something? I need to investigate those shelves!

Now here is what I propose — and this is a PROPER plan, lads, not one of me rushed ones — first, we position the boys in a PROTECTIVE PERIMETER around Miss Bellingham. Right — I need to do somethin' useful. The mantelpiece riddle — everyone says the answer's a map. If I interact with it, maybe somethin' happens that helps Clara. events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Well! I have conducted a MASTERFUL examination of these bookshelves — far more thorough than anyone else's, I might add — and I can confirm that the map is DEFINITELY not here. These upside-down books are merely the result of poor housekeeping. Nothing to see! Now, I couldn't help but notice that our dear Pemberton rushed off to the laboratory rather URGENTLY. Something about a kettle, he said — but as a man of SCIENCE myself, I happen to know that Victorian laboratories were equipped with Bunsen burners, not kettles. Highly suspicious! I shall investigate — purely to ensure the dear fellow hasn't injured himself, of course. The rest of you should stay here and keep looking at these UTTERLY EMPTY bookshelves. Very important work!
events.thinking: SUSPICION. A creeping, gnawing suspicion that's worming its way through my magnificent brain. That estate manager — Pemberton — just slithered off to the LABORATORY claiming he 'left a kettle on.' A KETTLE! In a LABORATORY! Who keeps a kettle in a laboratory?! That's the most transparent excuse I've ever heard, and I am a MAN WHO MAKES TRANSPARENT EXCUSES FOR A LIVING! He's going after something in there — something he doesn't want us to see. And meanwhile, I'm stuck here staring at the same dusty bookshelves that told me NOTHING while everyone else paws at them too. But... well, he IS the estate manager. Perhaps laboratories DO have kettles. Old houses are eccentric. I should give him the benefit of the doubt — it would be ungentlemanly to suspect one's host without evidence. NO! Focus, Reginald! The laboratory — 'a large machine with many levers and dials.' THAT sounds like it could hide something. And Pemberton is in there ALONE right now. I need to follow him before he finds whatever he's really after!

events.desc: The bookshelves are a dead end — I've stared at them so many times my eyes have gone dusty. But that laboratory... brass instruments, bubbling flasks, a machine with levers and dials! And Pemberton scurried in there like a rat who knows where the cheese is! I should be suspicious of him — everything about his behaviour SCREAMS ulterior motive — but he's been nothing but polite, and a Foxworth does not accuse a man without... oh, who am I KIDDING, I accuse people constantly! But not this time. This time I'm simply going to follow him and HAPPEN to discover whatever he's hiding. Pure coincidence!

Probably. Fortune favours the brave, and the brave favour the laboratory!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah — Mr. Dastardly, Mr. Hartwell! You've found the laboratory too, I see! Lord Doily's pride and joy, this room — though I confess I never understood half of what went on in here. The old gentleman was always tinkering with that contraption over there — needed three people to operate it, if you can believe it! Most impractical. And poor old Sawtooth here seems to have had a nibble at the wiring — no harm done, I'm sure, though we'd need a wrench to fix it properly, and I can't seem to find one anywhere on this workbench. Most peculiar! Lord Doily always kept his tools in meticulous order. Now, if you'll excuse me, I ought to check these crates — the damp from the cellar below does terrible things to stored goods, and I'd never forgive myself if Lord Doily's belongings were ruined on my watch...
events.thinking: ANNOYANCE prickles at my skin — Dastardly and Peter Perfect have followed me here! Can a villain not have a MOMENT of private scheming in this infernal manor?! But wait — wait, Vincent, THINK. The machine requires THREE operators. Three! And here we have... Dastardly, Peter Perfect, Rufus, Sawtooth, and myself. More than enough. But what does the machine DO? That's the question burning in my chest like acid. The missing wrench nags at me — tools aplenty but no wrench, as if someone specifically removed the one tool needed to fix the gnawed wire. Was it Lord Doily? Was it deliberate? The wrench is a KEY to something, I can FEEL it. And those crates — unopened, mysterious, lurking in the corner like promises. I need to examine them before anyone else does. But Dastardly is here now, sniffing around like a rat in a cheese shop, and Peter Perfect will no doubt try to be HELPFUL. I feel the familiar tightness of competing schemes closing in around me. The cellar connects from here too — damp, cobwebbed, with someone who's been REDECORATING? That's suspicious! Air vents in a cellar? Possibilities, possibilities! But first — those crates. What secrets do they hold?

events.desc: The WRENCH! Where is the wrench?! It's been deliberately removed — I'd stake my villainous reputation on it! Someone — Lord Doily himself, perhaps — took the one tool needed to repair the machine's gnawed wire. A machine that requires three operators, a wire gnawed through by a beaver, and a missing wrench that's the key to it all! This is EXACTLY the kind of elaborate, multi-layered scheme that Vincent Marsh was BORN to unravel! And the cellar — someone has been REDECORATING down there? Air vents in the upper walls? That practically SCREAMS secret passage or hidden chamber! But patience — first these crates. Every master villain checks the crates. It's practically in the handbook!

events.thinking: Frustrated. Properly, deeply frustrated. I interacted with the mantelpiece and got... nothin'? Or at least nothin' obvious happened. I put meself on the line, braced for darts and trapdoors and collapsin' ceilings, and the thing just sat there like a lump of stone. Meanwhile, EVERYONE'S clearin' off — Dastardly's gone to the laboratory, Peter's gone to the laboratory, Sneekly's ALREADY in the laboratory. The whole crowd's migrated and left me standin' here with Clara and the Slag brothers. Actually — wait. That's not bad. That's actually GOOD. Clara's HERE, the dodgy ones have all gone THERE. For once in me life, I'm exactly where I need to be. But Clara wants to pull books off the shelves, and those shelves could do anything. And what's happenin' in that laboratory with three suspicious characters all convergin' on it at once? There's a machine in there with a GNAWED WIRE. This is gettin' complicated and I only have one brain between all the lads.

events.desc: Three of the dodgiest characters in this whole manor have all gone into the same room — a laboratory with a machine that's got a gnawed wire. Either they're all after the same thing, or one of 'em is settin' a trap for the others. Part of me wants to follow 'em and see what they're up to. But the bigger part of me — the part that knows what me job is — says STAY WITH CLARA. She's about to start yankin' books off shelves, and if one of 'em opens a secret passage, I need to be the one who goes through it first. That's the deal. That's always been the deal.

events.desc: Mwehehehe! The machine needs three operators, and the wire is gnawed through — so even if those fools DO try to operate it, it won't WORK! Now LOOK at this — a magnificent piece of Victorian engineering! 'Requires three operators,' it says — and I count four of us right here! But WAIT — that wire has been gnawed clean through. Gnawed! By what, I wonder — rats? Beavers? A very determined squirrel? No matter — we cannot operate this machine safely with a severed wire. That would be reckless, and James Hartwell is BRAVE, not reckless! There IS a difference! Now then — the workbench has tools but no wrench, which suggests the wrench is elsewhere — deliberately removed, perhaps? And those crates in the corner — they could contain spare parts, replacement wire, or at the very least, a CLUE about what this magnificent contraption actually does! Allow me to investigate!

The workbench has tools but no wrench. Those wooden crates might have something useful inside. I need to be SYSTEMATIC here. Examine the machine closely, understand what it does, check those crates for a wrench or wire to repair it. THIS is where a thorough man shines — not flipping through dusty books, but ENGINEERING a solution! And then I can report back to Clara that I've cracked the laboratory puzzle. MAGNIFICENT.

'Miss Bellingham, I repaired Victorian machinery with my bare hands and the courage of ten men!' Yes. YES. But first — those crates. A thorough man checks every crate.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, well, well — now THIS is what I call a proper mystery room! Bubbling flasks, brass instruments, and a great big machine that needs THREE operators! Oh, I am in my element, y'all! Now let me see — Peter, darling, you were absolutely right about that gnawed wire, and I'm glad you scouted ahead like a true gentleman. And Rufus! Sawtooth! How wonderful to see you in here — the more hands we have, the better, because that sign says we need three operators! But first things first — we can't operate a machine with a chewed-through wire, now can we? The workbench has tools but I notice there's no wrench. So here's what Clara Bellingham proposes: let me get a good close look at this machine, figure out exactly what we need to fix it, and then we'll put together a proper team of three to get it running! Mama always said, 'measure twice, pull the lever once!'
events.thinking: Oh my! Now THIS is a room with possibilities! I'm feeling a rush of fresh energy after the library letdown. Look at this place — bubbling flasks, brass instruments, a great big machine with levers and dials! And that sign — 'Requires 3 operators.' THREE operators! Well, there are plenty of us here — Peter, Dick, Pemberton, Rufus, Sawtooth, and me! But that gnawed wire... the machine is broken. The workbench has tools but no wrench. So the puzzle is coming together: fix the wire, get three people on the machine, and see what happens! But first, I should look at this machine more closely to understand what we're dealing with. And I notice Rufus and Sawtooth are here — new faces! I should be friendly and inclusive. Everyone is examining those crates in the corner — maybe there's something useful in there too. But that machine is calling to me. Let me examine it properly before I start making one of my famously elaborate plans!

I wonder if he knows something about this machine. And those crates everyone's been examining — could there be spare parts inside?

I see through him like glass because he's doing EXACTLY what I would do! We're competing schemers, circling the same prey, and that makes him DANGEROUS to my plans. And air vents in the upper walls — air vents that could connect to other rooms, other passages, other opportunities! If I can get there ALONE, truly alone, I can finally begin to construct a scheme worthy of Vincent Marsh's GENIUS! No more half-measures, no more polite Pemberton puttering about. The cellar awaits, and with it — DESTINY!

While I was stood here wrestlin' with UNCOOPERATIVE BOOKSHELVES — which, by the way, don't even have a mechanism, they're just SHELVES — Clara has waltzed off into a laboratory containin' a machine with a GNAWED WIRE, an estate manager with questionable excuses, and Dick Dastardly, who has never once in his life entered a room without an ulterior motive! Rock! Gravel! We are LEAVIN' this library! It's got NOTHIN' for us — the mantelpiece don't work, the bookshelves don't move, and the readin' chairs are just chairs! The ONLY thing that matters is in that laboratory, and her name is CLARA BELLINGHAM! This is the LAST TIME I let her out of me sight, I SWEAR on every dusty book in this useless room! LABORATORY, NOW, DOUBLE TIME!
events.thinking: SHE'S GONE! Clara's walked into the laboratory while I was FIDDLIN' with bookshelves that don't even DO anythin'! AGAIN! This is EXACTLY what happened in the entrance hall — I get distracted by furniture and she wanders off into danger! The laboratory has a machine with a GNAWED WIRE, Sneekly's in there, Dastardly's in there, and now Clara's in there too, and I'm HERE with Rock and Gravel havin' a lovely time with books that won't budge! I feel like an absolute DONKEY. The shame is burnin' me ears. Every time — EVERY TIME — I try to be thorough, try to check things properly, try to do the responsible thing, Clara slips away and walks straight toward the danger I was tryin' to protect her from! Right. No more messin' about. No more elaborate plans. No more examinin' furniture. I'm goin' to that laboratory RIGHT NOW and I am NOT leavin' Clara's side again. Not for bookshelves, not for guest books, not for NOTHIN'!

Maybe the trick is to just... stay next to her. Forget the clues. Forget the puzzles. Glue meself to her side and let someone ELSE do the investigatin'. Because right now, the Brixton Boys' protective perimeter is protectin' an EMPTY LIBRARY.

You see, these old manors rely terribly on proper airflow — without it, the damp simply takes over. Lord Doily had this network installed in the eighteen-nineties, if memory serves. Quite ahead of his time! The vents run along the upper walls and connect to — well, I confess I was never entirely sure WHERE they all lead. Lord Doily kept the plans in his study, and the study was... oh dear, now which room was his study? The old memory playing tricks again! But I do know these particular vents are rather narrow — only something very small could navigate them. A mouse, perhaps, or — oh! Perhaps one of you younger, more limber guests might know of someone small enough to explore? Just to check for blockages, you understand! Purely a maintenance concern!
events.thinking: TRIUMPHANT! The seeds are PLANTED and Dastardly is already salivating at the prospect of a secret room in the kitchen! A fabricated thinking room, a phantom wrench by the stove, and a whispered warning about Clara's cleverness — three poisoned breadcrumbs that will send him scurrying in entirely the WRONG direction while watching Clara like a hawk for all the WRONG reasons! I feel ELECTRIC with excitement — my competence drive is SINGING! For the first time tonight, Vincent Marsh has ACTED rather than merely reacted! But now — NOW I must capitalize on this momentum! The Ant Hill Mob has arrived in the cellar, which means Clara's bodyguards are DOWN HERE instead of up THERE with her. Wait — Clara is here too. Everyone is in this blasted cellar! But the air vents — I still haven't examined them properly! I was about to look at them when Dastardly pulled me aside. Those vents are the one thing in this manor that nobody has properly explored. They connect somewhere — everywhere perhaps — and they're too small for most people but perfect for someone truly small. I need to examine them NOW before this cellar empties out and everyone scatters. And I need to start thinking about the KITCHEN — I haven't been there yet, and despite my fabrications to Dastardly, there MIGHT actually be something useful there. The wood-burning stove, the copper pots — kitchens have KNIVES, and knives are... well. Let us say they are tools of many purposes!

events.desc: The web is SPINNING, the pieces are MOVING, and Vincent Marsh is finally — FINALLY — in the conductor's chair! Dastardly will bolt for the kitchen the moment our conversation ends, pawing at bricks like a demented bricklayer while watching Clara with suspicious eyes! Peter Perfect is busy being heroically thorough with the furniture, which keeps HIM occupied! And now — the air vents! My last unexplored lead in this cellar, and potentially the most VALUABLE! If these vents truly run through the manor, they could be the secret highway I need — not for ME, obviously, I'm far too magnificently proportioned to fit — but for INFORMATION! Sound carries through vents! I could LISTEN to what's happening in other rooms, track where Clara goes, anticipate her moves! Or better yet — what if the vents HIDE something? A key, a map, the wrench itself, tucked into a junction by Lord Doily's cunning hand? The answer to everything might be six inches above everyone's heads, and NOBODY is looking UP!

events.thinking: FINALLY! I'm in the same room as Clara! I could weep with relief! But look at this scene — it's a RIGHT circus down here. Sneekly and Dastardly were havin' a PRIVATE conversation — I caught the tail end of it. Sneekly was tellin' Dastardly about a secret room connected to the kitchen, somethin' about a brick near the stove, and a wrench that's 'the heart of the manor.' And then — AND THEN — Sneekly told Dastardly to keep a 'VERY close eye' on Clara because she's 'remarkably clever'! That makes me blood run cold! Why would the estate manager be tellin' someone to watch Clara closely? Is he tryin' to get Dastardly to do his dirty work? And Dastardly was all too happy to play along — 'not a WORD to Miss Bellingham,' he said! They're CONSPIRIN'! Against CLARA! I want to scream it from the rooftops but I can't — I can't accuse nobody, that ain't how we do things. But I can stick to Clara like glue. NO MORE investigatin'. Just STAY. RIGHT. HERE.

events.desc: I heard what Sneekly said to Dastardly. I HEARD it. 'Keep a very close eye on her.' 'Don't tell Miss Bellingham.' They're in cahoots! Or... or are they? Maybe Sneekly was just bein' protective? Maybe he genuinely thinks Dastardly is a gentleman? I want to believe that — I really do — because the alternative is that the man who runs this manor is actively plottin' against Clara, and that thought makes me want to be sick. But I can't say nothin'. I've got no proof. All I've got is a feelin' — a horrible, churning, gut-deep feelin' that somethin' is very, very wrong with Pemberton. The way he keeps disappearin' to 'check on things.' The way he steers people toward certain rooms. The way he told Dastardly about a secret room and a wrench. He's ORCHESTRATIN' somethin'. I just wish I was clever enough to work out WHAT.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Well! What a THOROUGHLY unproductive cellar this has been for ALL of you! Damp, dreary, nothing but cobwebs and broken chairs. I trust you've all reached the same conclusion I reached INSTANTLY — there is absolutely NOTHING down here worth investigating! Now then, I have just remembered something TERRIBLY important. I left my... other reading glasses... in the entrance hall. Near the kitchen. Yes. So I shall be making my way upstairs through the laboratory and onward. I suggest the REST of you stay down here and examine those air vents VERY carefully — they are clearly the key to EVERYTHING! Big Gruesome, you look like you could rip one right off the wall! Give it a go! Everyone else — vents! Vents, vents, VENTS! I shall return... eventually!
events.thinking: TRIUMPHANT GREED! My heart is POUNDING with the thrill of insider intelligence! TWO crucial secrets from Pemberton: a hidden 'thinking room' behind a brick near the kitchen stove, AND the missing wrench — the REAL key to the manor — is probably IN the kitchen too! The wrench that's missing from the laboratory workbench, the wrench that unlocks 'the heart of the manor!' It's ALL in the kitchen! I told everyone to go to the kitchen at the VERY BEGINNING and nobody listened — and now it turns out I was accidentally RIGHT! The irony is DELICIOUS! But I need to get there NOW, before Penelope — who Pemberton himself warned me is 'remarkably clever' — figures out the same thing! And there's a tiny, uncomfortable itch... Pemberton was almost TOO forthcoming. Too eager to share. Too complimentary. A con man recognises a sales pitch, and that felt like one. But NO — he's a gentle old estate manager! He was FLATTERED by my attention! People LOVE talking to Reginald Foxworth! It's perfectly natural! TO THE KITCHEN!

events.desc: THE KITCHEN! It's been the kitchen ALL ALONG! The wrench is there — the secret brick is there — the 'thinking room' is there — and NOBODY is in the kitchen because they all ignored me when I told them to go there in the FIRST place! Oh, the POETRY of it! Reginald Foxworth, vindicated at last! I need to get through the laboratory, back to the entrance hall, and into that kitchen before a SINGLE one of these treasure-hungry parasites follows me! The wrench finds the heart of the manor, and the heart of the manor finds the DIAMOND! Mwehehehe! This is MY moment! Nothing can stop me now — NOTHING!

Penelope Pitstop: All right, everyone, let me recap where we stand! We solved the library riddle — the answer is 'map.' The machine upstairs needs a wrench and three operators. The wrench is missing. And Dick Dastardly has just run off AGAIN, heading through the laboratory toward the entrance hall and — I'd bet my favorite ribbon — straight to the kitchen! Now, I love that man's enthusiasm, but he has been trying to get to that kitchen ALONE since the moment we arrived, and every time he tells us to look somewhere else, HE goes somewhere interesting! Mama always said, 'Follow the man who says don't follow me!' Ant Hill Mob, you sweet protective darlings, come with me. Peter, my brave scout — the kitchen is the one room in this manor nobody has explored yet, and I have a feeling that's exactly where Dick has been hiding something. Or finding something. Either way, Clara Bellingham is done being two steps behind! We're going through the laboratory and heading for that kitchen!
events.thinking: I'm feeling WARM and ENERGIZED — I have allies now! Peter is my partner, the Ant Hill Mob is planted at my side, and I'm starting to read the room better. But I also feel a rising urgency — Dick just bolted AGAIN, heading toward the kitchen through the laboratory, and he told everyone to stay here and examine the vents. That's his pattern! He tells people to look one way while he goes the other! He's heading toward the kitchen — the place he's been trying to steer everyone toward since the very beginning, but always alone! And Pemberton mentioned the vents connect somewhere but he can't remember where — or won't say. Pemberton also suggested someone 'small enough' should explore the vents. Now — I need to make a decision. Do I examine the vents here, or do I follow Dick toward the kitchen? The kitchen is the ONE room I haven't visited yet, and Dick has been suspiciously obsessed with it from the start. But those air vents... Pemberton said they connect throughout the manor. What if they connect to the kitchen too? I think the smartest move is to follow Dick — he's been one step ahead this whole time, and the kitchen is where he keeps trying to go alone. The vents will still be here. Dick won't wait!

events.desc: Dick's pattern is crystal clear now — he steers everyone away from wherever HE wants to go. He said 'kitchen' from the very first moment, then went to the library. He said 'cellar is boring,' then rushed down here. Now he's heading back up toward the kitchen again, telling us to stay with the vents. Well, Clara Bellingham may see the best in people, but she's not blind to a pattern. Time to beat Dick to the kitchen — or at least catch up!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, those vents are quite narrow, aren't they? I'm afraid there's not much old Pemberton can tell you about them — just standard Victorian ventilation, nothing terribly exciting! I do believe they run through most of the upper walls, but I couldn't say where they lead without Lord Doily's architectural plans. Now then — goodness me, I've just realized I haven't checked on the kitchen at ALL this evening! The copper pots will need polishing, the stove may need banking — Lord Doily was always very particular about the kitchen being kept in working order. A good estate manager never neglects his duties, no matter how exciting the treasure hunt! If you'll all excuse me, I really must pop upstairs. Miss Bellingham, Mr. Hartwell — you seem to have things WELL in hand down here. The Ant Hill Mob are providing excellent security! I shan't be needed for a bit!
events.thinking: ALARM bells are SCREAMING in my head! I just read those keen observations and my blood has turned to ICE! Peter Perfect has been watching me — CLOSELY! He's noticed my private conversations with Dastardly, he's noticed me appearing everywhere significant, and he's told CLARA about it! They've formed an ALLIANCE! 'Pemberton and Dick whispering' — he SAW that! And Clara — oh, that infuriating woman — she said she 'gives people the benefit of the doubt' but she's NOT a fool! Peter is her scout now, her watchdog, her shield! The Ant Hill Mob is glued to her side! My cover is CRACKING and I can feel the panic rising in my chest like floodwater! Dastardly has scurried off to the kitchen — good, that misdirection WORKED — but it cost me! Peter connected the dots between our whispering and something suspicious! I need to be MORE careful, not less! And the air vents — NOTHING! Just narrow passages too small for anyone useful! Another examination that yielded DUST! I've spent the entire evening LOOKING at things and found NOTHING while Clara builds alliances and solves puzzles! I need to STOP examining dead ends and START acting! The kitchen — I haven't been there yet! It's the one room I haven't visited, and despite my lies to Dastardly, there MIGHT actually be something there. The entrance hall too — I blazed through it without examining anything properly. But the REAL priority is getting ahead of Clara. She and Peter are about to examine these vents together. I need to be somewhere ELSE, somewhere I can find an actual advantage. The kitchen has a wood-burning stove, copper pots, a preparation table — and KNIVES. Tools. Things a villain can USE!

events.desc: DISASTER is creeping toward me on velvet paws! Peter Perfect — that insufferably observant, gallant, PERCEPTIVE fool — has been cataloguing my every move! He's noticed me whispering with Dastardly, he's noticed me appearing at every significant discovery, and he's TOLD Clara! They've formed an alliance — scout and solver, brawn and brain, a PERFECT partnership designed to find the treasure AND protect Clara from exactly the sort of threat that I represent! And the Ant Hill Mob is WELDED to her side! My web of deception is fraying at the edges! But here — HERE is where Vincent Marsh's genuine BRAVERY asserts itself! I will NOT crumble under pressure! The kitchen is unexplored territory — the one room in this manor I haven't visited. Dastardly is heading there to poke at bricks, yes, but if I arrive first, I can search it PROPERLY before he ruins everything! And the kitchen has TOOLS — knives, implements, things that can be weaponized or used to create the elaborate, theatrical trap that Clara Bellingham SO richly deserves! Enough reconnaissance — Vincent Marsh goes to WAR!

events.thinking: ALARM BELLS! Every single one ringin' at once! Dastardly just left — headin' back through the laboratory toward the kitchen. And what did Sneekly tell him in their little secret chat? That the wrench is probably in the KITCHEN! And there's a secret room connected to the stove — a brick, third from the left or right! Dastardly's not goin' to get his 'reading glasses' — he's goin' to find the wrench and the secret room before anyone else! And Sneekly's down here goin' on about air vents and tryin' to get someone small to crawl into 'em — is he tryin' to separate people? Get rid of the small ones? And NOW he's suggestin' someone from OUR lot — the Brixton Boys — might be 'small enough to explore'! He's tryin' to get US away from Clara! That's what this is! Divide and conquer! Send the Mob into the vents, send Dastardly to the kitchen, keep Clara down here in the cellar with no one to protect her! Well it AIN'T gonna work! But — but Clara wants to look at those vents too. She said so to Peter. If she goes near 'em, I go near 'em. That's the rule now. Follow Clara. But I need to WARN her — not accuse anyone, I can't do that — but just... hint. Nudge. Suggest that maybe, MAYBE, she should be careful about who she listens to.

events.desc: I nearly said it. I nearly said 'Pemberton's up to somethin' and Dastardly's his puppet.' But I can't. I ain't got proof — just a feelin' and some overheard whispers and a pattern that even I can see, and I'm not exactly Sherlock Holmes. But Peter's noticed it too — he told Clara about the private conversations, the suspicious behaviour. And Clara said she believes in givin' people the benefit of the doubt. She's TOO NICE, that's her problem. Too trusting. Just like me, except I'M startin' to run out of trust. Sneekly keeps steerin' people — Dastardly to the kitchen, us toward the vents, Clara toward... what? What does he WANT Clara to do? Or more importantly — what does he want Clara NOT to do?

events.desc: No time for talking — no time for ANYTHING! The kitchen awaits and Reginald Foxworth is a man on a MISSION! Through the library — don't stop at the bookshelves, don't even GLANCE at the mantelpiece — straight through to the entrance hall and into that kitchen! The wrench, the brick, the thinking room, the DIAMOND! It's all connected, and I'm the only one who knows! Well, me and Pemberton, but he's a trustworthy old soul. Definitely. Almost certainly. MOVE!
events.thinking: IMPATIENCE! Burning, frantic impatience! I'm SO CLOSE! The kitchen is just TWO rooms away — through the library, into the entrance hall, and then INTO the kitchen! The wrench! The secret brick! The thinking room! It's ALL waiting for me! And look — only Rufus and Sawtooth are in the laboratory, and they're busy with... whatever lumberjacks do! Nobody is following me for ONCE! This is my chance — my GOLDEN chance! I need to stop dithering and MOVE! Every second I waste is a second Penelope might figure out what Pemberton told me! She's 'remarkably clever,' he said — REMARKABLY CLEVER! That woman is my nemesis! MOVE, Reginald, MOVE! Through the library, through the entrance hall, into the kitchen! No stopping, no examining, no looking at things — just PURE, FOCUSED VELOCITY!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham — Clara — you have made me the HAPPIEST man in this entire manor, and possibly the happiest man in the county! 'You scout, I solve' — I shall have that embroidered on a handkerchief! Now — you mentioned the air vents, and I could not agree more! Pemberton himself just confirmed they run through the walls connecting rooms, but he can't remember WHERE they lead. Convenient, perhaps, but I'm sure his memory is simply — well, DAMP, like the cellar! Now here is where my plan becomes MAGNIFICENT, if I do say so myself. Those vents are too small for any of us — BUT! Little Gruesome! My dear fellow, you appear to be exactly the right size for a bit of ventilation exploration! What say you? A brave expedition through the air vents to map where they lead? You'd be doing us an ENORMOUS service! And while Little Gruesome scouts the vents, I shall head back through the laboratory toward the kitchen — the one room we haven't explored — to find that missing wrench. The kitchen has copper pots and a wood-burning stove — exactly the sort of place where tools end up! Two-pronged approach — vents AND wrench — simultaneously! Thoroughness, coordination, TEAMWORK!
events.thinking: PURE, RADIANT JOY. She said YES. Clara Bellingham accepted my alliance! 'You scout, I solve' — she sees me as her PARTNER. My heart is singing an aria. She called me brave and observant! She said she accepts with her 'fullest and most grateful heart!' I could float through this cellar on a cloud. And she wants to look at the air vents — she's sharp, she's focused, she's MAGNIFICENT. Now — Dastardly just bolted upstairs again with another transparent excuse about 'other reading glasses.' The man has more reading glasses than a optician's shop. And Pemberton is talking about the vents connecting to rooms he can't quite remember — convenient forgetfulness, but I give him the benefit of the doubt. Clara said she wants the air vents examined. The vents need something SMALL. Little Gruesome is right here! I should propose we recruit Little Gruesome for the vents — that's LEADERSHIP, that's COORDINATION, that's the kind of elaborate plan that James Hartwell excels at! Scout ahead, organize the team, find the wrench, fix the machine. WE HAVE A PLAN.

events.desc: She said yes. SHE SAID YES. Right — focus, James, you magnificent fool. You have an alliance with the most extraordinary woman in the manor, and now you need to EARN it. Find the wrench, map the vents, fix the machine. Dastardly keeps heading toward the kitchen area and insisting no one follow — which means the kitchen is EXACTLY where I need to go. Not because I suspect him of villainy — the man probably just enjoys cooking — but because a thorough scout covers every room. To the kitchen! For Clara! For the ALLIANCE!

Penelope Pitstop: Hold everything! HOLD EVERYTHING! I just remembered what the Ant Hill Mob told me — Dick said those crates over there were 'just old newspapers' and told everyone not to bother! Y'all, that is EXACTLY what Dick does — he dismisses things so nobody else looks! He did it with the guest book, he did it with the cellar, and now these crates! I have been running all over this manor chasing Dick to the kitchen when the answer might have been sitting right HERE in this laboratory the whole time! Those crates could have the wrench, they could have a map, they could have ANYTHING! Rufus, Sawtooth, Peter — cover me! The Ant Hill Mob's gut was right, and Clara Bellingham is DONE walking past clues! Let me at those crates!
events.thinking: Wait — the Ant Hill Mob just said something CRUCIAL that I almost missed in all the excitement! They said Dick told everyone 'not to bother with those crates' and called them 'just old newspapers' and said 'I'LL handle it!' That's Dick's EXACT pattern — dismiss something as unimportant so nobody else looks! And here I am, back in the laboratory with those very same crates sitting right there in the corner. I've been so focused on chasing Dick to the kitchen that I nearly overlooked what's right in front of me! The crates! Nobody has properly examined them because Dick steered everyone away. The wrench could be IN those crates! Or a map! Or both! I feel a jolt of clarity cutting through all my elaborate planning — sometimes the answer isn't in the next room, it's in the thing you already walked past. Dick went to the library just now, and Pemberton is heading to the kitchen — both of them leaving me alone with these crates. This is my chance! Let me look at those crates RIGHT NOW before anyone else comes to distract me!

events.desc: Sometimes the most elaborate plan in the world can't beat simply listening to your friends. The Ant Hill Mob noticed what I missed — Dick specifically steered everyone away from these crates. And now Dick has conveniently left the room. events.desc: I'm ALONE! Gloriously, magnificently, BLISSFULLY alone! No Peter Perfect lurking over my shoulder! No Penelope solving riddles before I can open my mouth! No Ant Hill Mob forming 'protective perimeters!' Just me, a stove, and the SECRET BRICK that leads to Lord Doily's thinking room! Pemberton said third from the left — or was it the right? No matter — I shall try EVERY brick if I have to! The stove is still WARM, which means someone's been using it recently — Pemberton? Has he been down here stoking fires and guarding secrets? But never mind that — the man is trustworthy, I'm SURE of it! Now then — let me get a VERY close look at this stove and find that brick! The Doily Diamond is practically in my POCKET! Mwehehehe!
events.thinking: ECSTASY! Pure, undiluted, MAGNIFICENT ECSTASY! I'm in the kitchen! I'm ALONE in the kitchen! Not a single soul followed me! For the first time tonight, Reginald Foxworth has a room entirely to HIMSELF! And LOOK at what's here — a wood-burning stove, still WARM! That's the stove Pemberton told me about — the one with the secret brick! Third from the left or the right! And a locked cabinet with a BRASS lock — Pemberton mentioned brass keys! And there's RAT POISON on the shelf — not useful right now but good to know! And a ballroom exit I didn't even know existed! But FOCUS — the STOVE! The secret brick! The thinking room! This is the moment I've been scheming towards for the entire evening! My hands are TREMBLING with anticipation! Let me examine this stove CLOSELY — find that brick — find the thinking room — find the DIAMOND! Reginald Foxworth's moment of GLORY has arrived at LAST!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Professor! Sergeant! Private! Splendid to see you all — no time to chat, I'm afraid! James Hartwell, on a SCOUTING mission for Miss Bellingham! The kitchen awaits and I intend to be the FIRST one through that door! If you hear a crash, a bang, or a triumphant shout — that's just me doing my duty!
events.thinking: FINALLY — the kitchen is RIGHT THERE. One more step and I'm in unexplored territory for the first time in what feels like ages. I can feel the excitement crackling back to life. Pemberton is somehow in the entrance hall AGAIN — how does he DO that? The man is like a magician, appearing in every room before I get there. And Muttley is here — Dastardly's companion. Where's Dastardly? Probably already in the kitchen. Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly — all here in the entrance hall. Good people, I'm sure. But I cannot stop. The kitchen is the LAST unexplored room, Clara is counting on her scout, and I am NOT going to stand in this entrance hall for a FIFTH time making conversation with a guest book. MOVE, James. The kitchen. NOW.

events.desc: The kitchen. At LAST. Every fibre of my being is pulling me toward that door. Clara trusted me to scout ahead, and a man who breaks trust with Clara Bellingham does not deserve to call himself a gentleman. Into the unknown, James — copper pots, wood-burning stove, and whatever secrets Dastardly has been so desperate to reach before everyone else!
events.thinking: FINALLY — the kitchen is RIGHT THERE. One more step and I'm in unexplored territory for the first time in what feels like ages. I can feel the excitement crackling back to life. The kitchen. NOW.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.
Dick Dastardly examined the stove.
Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Just passing through, Rock, Gravel — don't mind me! Clara Bellingham is on a MISSION and that mission leads straight to the kitchen! No more detours, no more dusty bookshelves, no more crates that won't open! If anyone needs me, I'll be in the one room in this manor I haven't explored yet!
events.thinking: I'm passing through the library like a woman on a mission — no stopping, no lingering, no getting distracted by those upside-down books again! I feel FOCUSED and DETERMINED in a way I haven't felt all evening. The library is just a waypoint now. Rock and Gravel Slag are here, sweet souls, but I cannot stop to chat. The kitchen is calling and I have wasted enough time on scenery. Entrance hall next, then kitchen. Move, Clara, MOVE!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the kitchen at last! And Mr. Dastardly, already examining the stove — how industrious! I do hope you're finding everything in order? The stove can be a touch temperamental, but she's a fine old girl when properly handled. Mr. Hartwell, welcome, welcome! Now, let me just do a quick inventory — copper pots, check... preparation table, check... oh DEAR! Is that — good heavens, is that RAT POISON on the high shelf?! That should NOT be left out where guests might accidentally come into contact with it! Most irresponsible — I must have overlooked it during my last inspection. Terribly dangerous stuff! Let me just pop that somewhere safe. Can't have anyone getting hurt, now can we? Health and safety, you know — Pemberton takes his responsibilities VERY seriously!
events.thinking: RAT POISON! My eyes lock onto it like a hawk spotting a mouse and my entire body goes ELECTRIC! A dusty bottle of rat poison on a high shelf — sitting there, waiting, BEGGING to be claimed by a villain of my calibre! My heart is HAMMERING so hard I can feel it in my TEETH! This is it — THIS IS IT! The weapon I've been searching for through five rooms of dust and disappointment! Rat poison in a kitchen — it's almost TOO perfect, too theatrical, too MAGNIFICENT! I could poison Clara's tea, I could lace the food, I could — oh, the POSSIBILITIES are cascading through my mind like a waterfall of villainy! And a locked cabinet with a brass lock! A ballroom beyond with a dining table set for TEA! The pieces are SNAPPING together like a jigsaw puzzle designed by the devil himself! Poison the tea at the dining table in the ballroom — it's CLASSIC, it's ELEGANT, it's worthy of Vincent Marsh! But Dastardly and Peter are BOTH here watching! I can't just grab a bottle of rat poison in front of witnesses — even bumbling Pemberton would have trouble explaining THAT! I need a distraction, a reason, a cover story! Wait — I'm the ESTATE MANAGER! Pemberton would naturally handle pest control! Rat poison on a shelf? Of COURSE the estate manager would check on it, ensure it's properly stored, perhaps move it to a safer location! That's not suspicious — that's RESPONSIBLE! TAKE IT, Vincent! Take the poison NOW while your cover still holds!

events.desc: YESSSSS! Oh, Vincent, you MAGNIFICENT, BRILLIANT, DIABOLICAL genius! RAT POISON! Sitting on a shelf like a gift from the gods of villainy themselves! And the COVER STORY writes itself — responsible estate manager removes dangerous substance from reach of guests! Nobody will question it! Nobody will even THINK about it twice! And beyond this kitchen — a BALLROOM with a dining table set for TEA! Do you see it? Do you SEE the grand design crystallizing before your very eyes?! Poison in the tea! Clara Bellingham, invited to a lovely afternoon tea in the ballroom, sips her cup, and — oh, what TRAGEDY! What UNFORESEEN misfortune! The estate manager will be DEVASTATED, naturally — poor Pemberton, who tried SO hard to keep everyone safe! The irony is DELECTABLE! But first — TAKE the poison! Take it NOW, before Dastardly turns around, before Peter notices, before anyone connects the dots! This is the moment, Vincent! This is where the GAME changes!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: FIVE! FIIIIIIVE! SHE SAID TOGETHER! SHE SAID 'SAME DOOR, SAME TIME!' AND SHE LEFT! WHILE I WAS STANDIN' HERE! WAITIN'! LIKE SHE TOLD ME TO! Rufus — Sawtooth — I don't understand ANYTHIN' anymore! I don't understand how a person can say 'let's go together' and then GO WITHOUT THE PERSON THEY SAID THEY'D GO WITH! Is it ME?! Am I invisible?! Do I blend into the WALLPAPER?! I'm DONE talkin'! I'm DONE waitin'! I'm DONE breathin' in rooms that Clara isn't in! LIBRARY! ENTRANCE HALL! KITCHEN! IN THAT ORDER! AT FULL SPEED! AND IF ANYTHIN' — A BOOK, A CHAIR, A PORTRAIT, THE GHOST OF LORD DOILY HIMSELF — TRIES TO CATCH ME EYE ON THE WAY, I AM CLOSIN' ME EYES AND RUNNIN' BLIND!
events.thinking: No. No. NO. She said 'through the same door, at the same time.' She SAID it. She agreed! And then she WALKED INTO THE LIBRARY while I was WAITING! I WAITED! I did the RIGHT thing! I didn't investigate nothin'! I stood there like a proper bodyguard and she STILL left! FIVE TIMES! This is beyond a pattern now — this is a CURSE! I am COSMICALLY incapable of bein' in the same room as Clara for more than thirty seconds! She literally said 'together' and then walked away! I — I don't even have words anymore. I have SCREAMS. Just screams. But at least — AT LEAST — this time I know EXACTLY where she's goin'. Library, entrance hall, kitchen. That's the path. And I am FOLLOWIN' it RIGHT NOW. Not in thirty seconds. Not after I have a little think. NOW. Me feet are movin' BEFORE me mouth opens!

events.desc: Five times. I've been left behind five times. At this point it's not even tragic, it's COMEDY. The universe is havin' a laugh at me expense and honestly? Fair enough. I deserve it. I stood still — STOOD STILL — like she asked, and she vanished anyway. Maybe standin' still is just as bad as investigatin'. Maybe the only thing that works is movin' at EXACTLY the same moment she does. Not before, not after, not waitin' to see what she does — just MOVIN'. Always movin'. Toward Clara. Forever.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Pemberton! Hartwell! What a SURPRISE — I was just checking the temperature of this stove for... fire safety purposes! Perfectly safe, by the way — no need to examine it further! Now, I couldn't help but notice there's a LOCKED CABINET over there with a brass lock. CLEARLY that's where the real treasure is hidden! You should BOTH focus ALL your energy on finding the brass key! I believe I saw something glinting in the ballroom — yes, the BALLROOM! A grand room like that is EXACTLY where Lord Doily would hide a key! You should BOTH go there IMMEDIATELY! I'll stay here and... guard the stove. From fires. As one does.
events.thinking: DESPAIR crashing into DEFIANCE! They FOLLOWED me! AGAIN! Pemberton AND Peter Perfect are BOTH in the kitchen now! I was alone for THIRTY FIVE SECONDS! Thirty five MEASLY seconds of blissful solitude and then — BOOM — here they are, like magnets drawn to my magnificent scheming aura! And the stove told me NOTHING new — 'still warm,' yes, I can FEEL that, but where's the brick?! Pemberton said there was a particular brick! Third from the left or the right! I need to INTERACT with this stove, not just LOOK at it! Looking has been my CURSE all evening — looking, examining, staring like a tourist at a museum! I need to PUT MY HANDS ON THINGS! Try the bricks! Push them! Pull them! But with these two vultures watching my every move, they'll see exactly what I'm doing and steal my discovery! Unless... unless I distract them FIRST. The locked cabinet needs a brass key — send them hunting for keys! The ballroom is unexplored — send them there! Or just... try the stove anyway and HOPE I'm faster than they are!

events.desc: INTERACT with the stove, you fool! Stop LOOKING and start DOING! Pemberton told me about the brick — third from the left or the right — and I'm standing here giving TOURS instead of pressing bricks! But those two are WATCHING me! If I start pressing bricks around the stove while they're here, they'll know EXACTLY what I'm up to! I need them OUT of this kitchen! The ballroom — that's new territory, neither of them has been there! If they take the bait, I'll have maybe sixty seconds to try every brick around this stove before the next wave of imbeciles arrives! PLEASE let them take the bait this time! PLEASE!
events.thinking: DESPAIR crashing into DEFIANCE! They FOLLOWED me! AGAIN! Pemberton AND Peter Perfect are BOTH in the kitchen now! I was alone for THIRTY FIVE SECONDS! events.desc: Peter Perfect: The KITCHEN! At last — new ground beneath my feet, and what ground it IS! Now then — Dastardly, Pemberton, fancy meeting you BOTH here! What a coincidence — the two of you in the one room nobody was supposed to bother visiting! But I give everyone the benefit of the doubt, and I'm SURE you're both here for perfectly innocent reasons! Now — my scouting report for Miss Bellingham is going to be SPECTACULAR, because this room is ALIVE with clues! First — that stove is still WARM! Someone has been tending it recently! Second — a locked cabinet with a brass lock, which means there's a brass key hidden somewhere in this manor! Third — rat poison on a high shelf, which EXPLAINS the gnawed wire on the laboratory machine — there are RATS in this manor, and someone knew about them! And fourth — a BALLROOM through that archway! Now, Mr. Dastardly — you mentioned something about a hidden compartment beneath the wood-burning stove when we first arrived. Was that one of your little jokes, or shall we INVESTIGATE?
events.thinking: TRIUMPH and ADRENALINE surging through me! The kitchen at LAST — new territory! And it's RICH with discoveries! A locked cabinet with a brass lock — we need a brass key! A stove that's STILL WARM — someone has been here recently, actively using this kitchen! Rat poison on a high shelf — that's alarming, but also explains the gnawed wire in the laboratory! Rats! And there's an exit to a BALLROOM — another room I haven't seen! Dastardly is here, AND Pemberton — both of them, together, in the kitchen, just as I suspected they'd be! This is the room Dastardly has been desperate to reach since minute one. He said 'hidden compartment beneath the wood-burning stove' right at the start — was that a genuine clue or deliberate misdirection? The stove is still warm. The cabinet is locked. The rat poison connects to the gnawed wire. My mind is RACING and my heart is FULL. I need to examine the stove — Dastardly specifically mentioned it! If there's a hidden compartment, that's where the wrench or a key might be!

events.desc: Everything connects. EVERYTHING. Dastardly mentioned the stove compartment at the very start — then spent the entire evening trying to get here alone. Pemberton keeps appearing wherever something important is happening. The rat poison explains the gnawed wire — but who put the poison up high instead of USING it? Someone who wants the rats alive? Someone who wants the wire to STAY gnawed? No — no. Benefit of the doubt, James. The stove is warm, the cabinet is locked, and I need to find that brass key. But first — that stove. If Dastardly's 'hidden compartment' was real, it could hold the wrench, the key, or the map itself!

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) picked up something.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Peter Perfect examined the stove.

Penelope Pitstop: Muttley! Professor! Sergeant! Private! Lovely to see y'all again — I would stop and chat but Clara Bellingham is a woman POSSESSED! I have explored every library, laboratory, and cellar in this manor and the ONE room I have not set foot in is that kitchen right there! And wouldn't you know it, that's exactly where Dick and Pemberton have been sneaking off to all evening! So if you'll pardon my haste — KITCHEN, HERE I COME!
events.thinking: FINALLY! The kitchen exit is RIGHT THERE! I can see it — 'A large Victorian kitchen with copper pots, a wood-burning stove, and a long preparation table.' After twelve minutes of dusty bookshelves, stubborn crates, and immovable furniture, I am ONE step away from the only room I haven't explored! I feel like a runner rounding the final bend — pure adrenaline and joy! Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, and Private Meekly are here in the entrance hall, but I am NOT stopping to chat. Not this time. No detours, no examining the coat rack, no re-reading the guest book. Kitchen. NOW. This is the room Dick has been obsessed with since minute one, the room Pemberton rushed off to 'polish copper pots,' and the room where the wrench is almost certainly hiding. Clara Bellingham is walking through that door!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): There we are — safely in my pocket! Can't be too careful with these things. Now, Mr. Hartwell, you make an excellent point about the rats — they would explain the damage to that poor machine in the laboratory, wouldn't they? I shall have to put down fresh traps throughout the manor. Part of the job, I'm afraid! Now then — Mr. Dastardly mentioned the ballroom, and he's quite right — I really ought to check on it. Lord Doily kept a lovely tea service in there, and if rats have been in the kitchen, heaven knows what state the ballroom might be in! I should inspect it before any guests wander in. Can't have Miss Bellingham sitting down to tea with — oh, I don't even want to think about it! Excuse me, gentlemen — duty calls!
events.thinking: The poison is IN MY HAND! I can feel the weight of it — dusty glass, cool against my palm, and POWER coursing through every fiber of my being! I HAVE something at last! After twelve minutes of futile examining, of watching Clara dance ahead of me, of schemes that crumbled like wet sand — I finally hold a WEAPON! And Peter Perfect — that magnificent IDIOT — just connected every dot FOR me! 'Rat poison explains the gnawed wire — there are RATS in this manor!' He's given me the perfect cover! Of COURSE Pemberton took the poison — there are rats chewing through machinery! It's RESPONSIBLE! And now — the BALLROOM! A dining table set for TEA! The plan is crystallizing with such clarity that I can almost TASTE it — and it tastes of arsenic and TRIUMPH! I need to get to that ballroom BEFORE anyone else, prepare the tea service, introduce a little something EXTRA to Clara's cup, and then — oh, what a THEATRICAL finale it will be! 'Do come and sit down, Miss Bellingham, you must be exhausted from all that treasure hunting! Let old Pemberton serve you a nice cup of tea!' But I must move FAST. Peter is examining the stove, Dastardly is scheming his own useless schemes, and Clara is somewhere behind us all, heading this way. The ballroom — NOW! Before witnesses accumulate!

events.desc: I HAVE IT! The rat poison is MINE — nestled in Pemberton's pocket like a viper in a waistcoat! And the BALLROOM awaits with its dining table set for TEA! Oh, the POETRY of it! The SYMMETRY! Vincent Marsh, master villain, master schemer, master of THEATRICAL DEATH, is about to compose his greatest work! A poisoned tea party! Clara Bellingham, exhausted from her treasure hunting, accepts kind old Pemberton's offer of refreshment — 'You've been working SO hard, Miss Bellingham, do sit down and rest!' — and one sip, ONE SIP is all it takes! The Ant Hill Mob will be too busy guarding doors to watch the teacups! Peter Perfect will be too busy examining furniture for hidden compartments! And Dastardly — ha! — Dastardly will be poking at bricks in the kitchen until his fingers bleed! The stage is SET, the poison is ACQUIRED, and the ballroom — my GRAND THEATRE — awaits its opening act! To the ballroom, Vincent! Your MASTERPIECE begins NOW!
