events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Rock! Gravel! No time to chat — Clara's ahead of us, headin' for the kitchen! Fall in behind me, lads! We are NOT stoppin' in this library — we've been through it THREE times already and it's given us NOTHIN' but dust and disappointment! Entrance hall, then kitchen! KEEP MOVIN'!
events.thinking: She's already through. Gone. Entrance hall, then kitchen. I can see Rock and Gravel here — me lads — but Clara's not here. She's moved on and I'm one room behind AGAIN. But this time I'm not stoppin'. I'm not lookin' at the bookshelves. I'm not touchin' the mantelpiece. I'm not sittin' in the chairs. I am a MAN ON A MISSION and that mission is THROUGH THIS ROOM and INTO THE ENTRANCE HALL and THEN INTO THE KITCHEN. No stops. No detours. No distractions. Just legs. One foot in front of the other. The library is a CORRIDOR now, nothin' more. I can see the exit to the entrance hall RIGHT THERE. Move. MOVE!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: CRUSHING, AGONISING BETRAYAL! The stove WON'T INTERACT! Pemberton LIED to me! Or — or maybe he DIDN'T lie, maybe the brick requires something I don't have yet, maybe the stove needs a tool, maybe — NO! He PLAYED me! That oily, simpering, kettle-inventing FRAUD sent me on a wild goose chase to the KITCHEN while he — wait, he's HERE too. He followed me here. And he just grabbed the rat poison! Why does an estate manager need RAT POISON?! And Peter Perfect — that insufferable man just quoted MY OWN WORDS back at me! 'A hidden compartment beneath the wood-burning stove,' he said! He REMEMBERS what I said in the entrance hall! My own lie has come back to HAUNT me because now he thinks there's actually something under the stove because I said it — and there IS something, but I can't GET to it! And Pemberton took the poison! That's suspicious! That's VERY suspicious! But... he did say it was a health and safety concern. That's reasonable. Estate managers DO worry about poison. I'm sure he's just being responsible. FOCUS! The cabinet needs a brass key. The ballroom is unexplored. I need to CHANGE TACTICS. The stove is a dead end without some tool or key I don't have yet. The BALLROOM — new territory! Maybe the brass key is there!

events.desc: The stove won't budge! Pemberton's 'secret brick' is either a LIE or requires something I haven't found yet! And the sly devil just POCKETED the rat poison while nattering about health and safety! Part of me screams that he's up to something DASTARDLY — which is MY department, thank you very much — but he IS the estate manager, and rat poison IS dangerous, and he IS just doing his job... probably. Meanwhile, the cabinet is LOCKED and needs a brass key, and the ballroom is completely unexplored! I need to get in there before Peter Perfect discovers whatever's waiting! But I also need him to think I'm NOT interested in the ballroom, so he doesn't shadow me AGAIN! Reverse psychology, Reginald — tell him to GO there so he thinks it's a trap and STAYS!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Well, the stove is warm but keeping its secrets for now — a stubborn piece of Victorian engineering, much like the rest of this manor! Now — Pemberton, I notice you've taken the rat poison 'for safekeeping.' Very responsible of you! Though I do wonder — if there are rats gnawing through laboratory wiring, perhaps the poison would be better employed NEAR the rats rather than on a high shelf? But I'm sure you have your reasons, and I trust your judgment as estate manager! Now — Dastardly, for ONCE I believe you may be onto something with the ballroom! A brass key for a brass lock — a grand ballroom IS exactly the sort of dramatic location where Lord Doily would conceal such a thing! I shall investigate IMMEDIATELY. But I must warn you — if I return to find that stove has been tampered with or that cabinet mysteriously opened, I shall be DEEPLY curious about how it happened! Not suspicious — CURIOUS! There IS a difference!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The ballroom! Oh, how MAGNIFICENT! Lord Doily did love his parties — this room has seen some splendid gatherings in its day, I can tell you! The marble floor needs repointing, I'm afraid, and those curtains could use a good beating — but the bones of the room are SUPERB! And look — the tea service! Still set out, bless my soul! Lord Doily always insisted on keeping a tea service ready for guests. 'You never know when someone might need refreshment, Pemberton,' he used to say. And how RIGHT he was! After all this exploring, I'm sure our guests will be simply PARCHED! Now, Mr. Hartwell, Mr. Luke, Mr. Bear — if you'll give me just a few minutes, I shall prepare a proper afternoon tea for everyone! Fresh water from the kitchen, a good stoking of the stove — we'll have this looking SPLENDID! Miss Bellingham especially must be exhausted from all that riddle-solving. A nice cup of tea is just what the doctor ordered!
events.thinking: The tea service is RIGHT THERE and the game is telling me I can USE the rat-poison WITH it! My blood is SINGING, my hands are TREMBLING with anticipation! But — BUT — Peter Perfect is HERE! That infernal, watchful, gallant SHADOW followed me into the ballroom! And Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear are here too! THREE witnesses! I cannot — CANNOT — pour rat poison into a tea service with three people WATCHING! Even bumbling Pemberton can't explain THAT away! 'Oh, just seasoning the tea with a little rodenticide, perfectly normal kitchen practice!' NO! The plan requires PRIVACY! I need to get these people OUT of this room, or I need to come BACK when it's empty! The elaborate scheme demands TIMING! But wait — my constraint says my plans are overly elaborate and my thoroughness creates complications! Am I OVER-THINKING this?! No — no, this is basic operational security! You don't poison tea in front of witnesses! That's not elaborate, that's COMPETENT! I need a distraction. Lazy Luke looks like he could be convinced to leave... no, I need ALL of them gone. Or — or I need to wait. Come back later. Examine the room now, establish my presence as the dutiful estate manager checking on things, and return when the room is EMPTY to do the deed. Yes — that's the THEATRICAL approach! Set the stage now, perform the act later! Look at the tea service, cluck about its condition, and plant the seed that Pemberton will be 'preparing tea for the guests shortly' — so when I return alone to 'set up,' nobody will question why the estate manager is fussing with teacups!

events.thinking: Peter Perfect just said he INSISTS on being present for all tea preparation! 'Never drink tea you haven't watched being poured' — a HARTWELL FAMILY TRADITION! He's ONTO me! Not directly, not consciously perhaps, but his instincts are SCREAMING at him to watch me near that tea service! And now Dastardly is here TOO — FOUR witnesses! The room is getting MORE crowded, not less! My beautiful, theatrical poisoned tea party plan is being STRANGLED in its crib by sheer foot traffic! I feel the frustration BOILING under my skin like the water I'll never get to poison! But — but I must not PANIC. Vincent Marsh does not panic. Vincent Marsh ADAPTS. The plan was always overly elaborate — I know this about myself, I KNOW my thoroughness creates complications! So perhaps the tea party approach is WRONG. Perhaps I'm over-committing to a scheme that requires conditions I cannot create — an empty ballroom, unwatched teacups, a trusting Clara. Peter will NEVER leave me alone with the tea service now. He's made that abundantly clear. So what DO I do with this poison? I need a different delivery method. Something more direct, less theatrical, less dependent on getting an empty room. But NO — my constraint says my schemes must be elaborate and theatrical! Simple and direct is NOT in Vincent Marsh's repertoire! I'm TRAPPED between my own nature and the practical reality! For now — I must retreat. Go back to the kitchen. Reconsider. The poison is still MINE, the opportunity will come. I just need to find the RIGHT moment, the right METHOD. And I need to stop Peter Perfect from watching my every move!

The laboratory has bubbling flasks and mysterious chemicals. There are a DOZEN ways to dispatch Clara Bellingham if only these PEOPLE would stop FOLLOWING me! I need a new approach — but first, I need SPACE. Back to the kitchen, regroup, rethink. The game is far from over, and Vincent Marsh has NEVER been defeated by a crowded room!

THE HOODED CLAW PICKED UP POISON! That's — that's — me blood has gone cold. Actually cold. I can feel it in me fingers. Not with poison. Not with Clara's life. I can't say it out loud but I can FEEL it — Sneekly is dangerous, and he's comin' for Clara, and the only thing standin' between them is a bunch of bumbling idiots from Brixton who can't even stay in the same room as the woman they're supposed to protect. Now then, Miss Bellingham, I do hope you're enjoying the ballroom — Lord Doily spent a FORTUNE on these marble floors, cracks and all! And the Ant Hill Mob — wonderful, you've caught up! Everyone's accounted for, how marvellous! Now, if you'll all excuse old Pemberton, I've just remembered I need to check on the — oh, what was it — the hinges! events.thinking: RELIEF floods through me like a dam breaking — the poison is OUT of my hands and INTO Dastardly's! I feel LIGHTER, cleaner, as if I've shed a skin! And the Ant Hill Mob just walked in — they're going to see Dastardly holding rat poison in the BALLROOM right next to the TEA SERVICE! Peter Perfect already warned Clara that Dastardly tampered with the tea service, and now the Ant Hill Mob — who told Clara not to eat or drink ANYTHING — will find him clutching a bottle of RAT POISON next to the teacups! Standing here with EMPTY pockets and a HELPFUL smile, the estate manager who responsibly delegated pest control to a willing volunteer! But with my hands clean and the chaos about to erupt, THIS is my chance to explore freely!

And when it does — when they ERUPT — when they surround Dastardly and demand explanations and create the most GLORIOUS chaos this ballroom has ever seen — Vincent Marsh will be GONE! Slipped away like a shadow, like a whisper, like the ghost of Lord Doily himself! My hands are empty, my conscience is clear — well, as clear as a master villain's conscience CAN be — and the entire manor lies before me, unguarded and full of secrets! Where to go? The entrance hall — I never properly examined it! The chandelier that hangs precariously! Or perhaps back to the kitchen while Peter is there alone — no, too risky with Peter already suspicious! The entrance hall. Start fresh. Find the brass key. Win the GAME!

Right now, there's a stove with a secret and a cabinet with a lock, and for once in this entire manor, nobody is watching me fumble. Let's see what you're hiding, old girl.
events.thinking: FOCUS. Quiet, solitary focus. I'm alone in the kitchen for the first time — no Pemberton hovering, no Dastardly scheming, no audience for speeches. Just me and the room. But I give people the benefit of the doubt. I ALWAYS give people the benefit of the doubt. Right now, though, I need to stop talking and start FINDING. The cabinet is locked. The stove is warm. I'm alone. This is my chance to be thorough without my thoroughness creating complications. The stove — Dastardly mentioned a compartment BENEATH it at the very start. I've only LOOKED at it before. Let me try to INTERACT with it. Maybe there IS a hidden compartment. Maybe the brass key is inside.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, Dick, I will hold you to that SOLEMN PROMISE, and Reginald Foxworth, I have to say — chivalry suits you! Now — Ant Hill Mob, I hear you loud and clear about the tea, and I am NOT drinking anything from those cups. Nobody should be drinking anything until we know what's what! Pemberton just said Dick is 'in charge of pest control' — and while I'm SURE that's perfectly innocent and related to whatever little critter gnawed through that wire upstairs, a lady exercises caution! Now, here is where we are: we need a brass key for the kitchen cabinet, we need a wrench for the laboratory machine, and Dick has a medal that belongs to my family. Peter is searching the kitchen right now, and I think he could use some help. I have been to every single room in this manor and the one place I haven't searched THOROUGHLY is the kitchen itself — the stove, the corners, everywhere a brass key might be hiding! Let's head back and give Peter a hand. Two sets of eyes are better than one, and three are better than two!
events.thinking: Okay, let me piece together everything that just happened. Dick won't give me the medal — he's keeping it, promising to use it 'for the quest' and return it later. That's Dick being Dick. But more importantly — Pemberton just said 'Mr. Foxworth is in charge of PEST CONTROL now' and handed him something earlier. Pest control... RAT POISON. Pemberton gave Dick the RAT POISON! And the tea service can be USED with rat-poison! Peter warned me that Pemberton had rat poison and that Dick interacted with the tea service! The Ant Hill Mob is screaming at me not to drink the tea! They're all trying to protect me from POISONED TEA and I've been so focused on the medal that I almost missed it! But — no. I see the best in people. Maybe Dick really IS doing pest control. Maybe the rat poison is for actual rats — the same rats that gnawed through the wire on the machine! There ARE rats in this manor! But still... the Ant Hill Mob is right to be cautious about the tea. Now — I need to focus on what I can DO. I don't have the medal, I don't have the brass key, I don't have the wrench. Peter went back to the kitchen to search more thoroughly. The ballroom only has the tea service. I should follow Peter to the kitchen — he's my partner, and together we might find the brass key. Or I should check if there are rooms I haven't explored. Wait — I haven't been through the whole manor yet! Where else connects? The ballroom only goes back to the kitchen. So the map is: Entrance Hall connects to Kitchen and Library. Library connects to Laboratory. Laboratory connects to Cellar. Kitchen connects to Ballroom. That's six rooms total. I've been to all of them now. The items I need are: brass key (not found), wrench (not found), and Dick has the medal. Let me go back to the kitchen and really SEARCH it — Peter said he was going back there. Maybe we missed something!

NOBODY pours tea until we've sorted out a few things! First — we need clean water from a source we can TRUST, and the kitchen stove's been tampered with by who-knows-who! Second — I want to see EVERY ingredient that goes into EVERY cup! Third — actually, you know what, forget the tea entirely! We've got a DIAMOND to find and a machine to fix and a wrench to locate and I for one think refreshments can WAIT! Now — Mr. Foxworth — DICK — I couldn't help but notice Pemberton handed you somethin' earlier. Said it was for 'pest control.' Very responsible of you to take charge of that! But you know what, that sort of thing should probably be kept somewhere SAFE, shouldn't it? Away from the FOOD and the TEA and the CUPS? In fact — oh, WHOOPSIE — excuse me, comin' through, these marble floors are VERY slippery, the cracks make it VERY hard to walk, me feet are goin' everywhere —
events.thinking: Dastardly has the poison. He's RIGHT HERE. Sneekly's slipped away again — 'checking hinges,' sure — but the damage is done. The poison is in Dastardly's pocket and that tea service is sittin' there waitin' to be used. Clara's talkin' to him about medals and family heirlooms and she doesn't realise she's negotiatin' with a man who's carryin' RAT POISON that was HANDED to him by the estate manager! The Brixton Boys are FAMOUS for trippin' into things! If I accidentally crash into Dastardly, maybe the poison falls out of his pocket, maybe it spills on the floor where it can't hurt nobody. That's not accusin' — that's just bein' clumsy! And clumsy is what we DO BEST!

But it's what we've got. Trip, crash, apologise, save Clara's life. The Brixton Boys way.

events.thinking: Something is CRACKING inside me and I don't like it. Penelope's kindness hit me like a brick to the chest — 'a place in history,' she said, and she MEANT it, and for one terrible moment I wanted to DESERVE it. But I DON'T deserve it! The medal is FAKE! The inscription is a LIE! I am a FRAUD! And that's... that's what I DO! I'm Reginald Foxworth! I lie about EVERYTHING! It's in my SOCIAL RULES! But right now, standing in this cracked ballroom with Penelope's warmth still ringing in my ears, the lying feels heavier than it's ever felt. STOP FEELING THINGS and START DOING THINGS, Reginald!

Because if it doesn't — if I pour rat poison into silver teacups and NOTHING happens — then I am truly, completely, magnificently FINISHED. But a Foxworth does not hesitate at the threshold of destiny! HERE GOES EVERYTHING!

Both DEAD ENDS wrapped in Pemberton's bumbling helpfulness! And Peter is already tearing apart the stove flue based on MY fabricated quote! They're ALL dancing to Vincent Marsh's tune and they don't even KNOW it! But — and here's the dread, the cold little whisper at the base of my skull — Clara looked at me with those eyes. Those trusting, searching, DIRECT eyes. And she said 'friend to friend.' She BELIEVES in Pemberton. She NEEDS Pemberton. She came to me not as a puzzle-solver but as a person reaching out to another person, and something in my chest TWISTED when I lied to her. What is this feeling? GUILT?! Vincent Marsh does NOT feel guilt! Vincent Marsh feels NOTHING but the sweet satisfaction of a scheme well-executed! And yet... 'The Bellinghams built what I merely inherited' — I MADE that up, but what if it's TRUE? What if Lord Doily really DID leave this for her? No! NO! The treasure is MINE! The manor is MINE! I am the true heir — or at least, I WILL be when Clara Bellingham is out of the picture! Shake it off, Vincent! The entrance hall awaits! The chandelier hangs PRECARIOUSLY! While they attack the stove, I shall prepare the GRAND FINALE!

The, uh, dangerous materials that were bein' passed around the ballroom are now SECURELY in the possession of the Ant Hill Mob, and they will be PERSONALLY deployed in the cellar — where the ACTUAL rats live — at the APPROPRIATE time! Nobody needs to worry about that particular problem anymore! Now then — Peter, I heard what you said about the stove. 'Everything begins and ends at the hearth' — that's what Lord Doily said? And there's a lever with multiple positions? Well, that sounds like EXACTLY the sort of thing that two clever people like you and Miss Bellingham should be investigatin' together! And while you do that, I will be standin' RIGHT HERE — not examinin' anythin', not wanderin' off, not gettin' distracted — just GUARDIN'. The Brixton Boys are on watch and we are NOT movin'!
events.thinking: I'm in the kitchen. Clara's HERE. Peter's HERE. Sneekly's HERE — but I've got the poison, so he can't do nothin' with it even if he wanted to. For the first time tonight, I feel... calm? Not calm exactly — more like... settled. I've done somethin' RIGHT. The poison's in me pocket. Clara's in me sight. And Peter's found a real clue — a lever on the stove with multiple positions, and Lord Doily said 'everything begins and ends at the hearth.' That's the stove! That's what we need to investigate! And I'm not gonna investigate it meself — I learned THAT lesson — I'm gonna let Peter and Clara handle the clever stuff while I stand guard. But Sneekly's here too, feedin' 'em information, bein' all helpful and friendly. 'Where the ancestors watch' — that's where the brass key is, he says. The portraits in the entrance hall. Is he tellin' the truth this time? Or is he steerin' people into another trap? I don't know. I genuinely don't know. But what I DO know is: the poison is safe, Clara is safe, and nobody's drinkin' poisoned tea tonight. The Brixton Boys did their job. Now we just need to stay close and stay watchful.

events.desc: The poison's in me pocket and it's stayin' there. But then I remember: he picked up poison, he gave it to Dastardly, and Dastardly touched the tea service. Those aren't the actions of a trustworthy man. They're the actions of a man with a plan. And his plan nearly worked. Nearly. But the Brixton Boys — clumsy, bumbling, always-one-room-behind Brixton Boys — accidentally saved the day. And we'll do it again if we have to.

Nobody in this entire manor has ANYTHING useful except the people who just STOLE from me! Yes — STOLE! I, Reginald Foxworth, have been ROBBED! By a mob of tiny gangsters disguised as concerned citizens! They took my poison — MY poison, given to me by the estate manager HIMSELF — and they've absconded to the kitchen with it! Well, they have NOT heard the last of this! Reginald Foxworth does not get pickpocketed and TAKE IT LYING DOWN! I am going to march into that kitchen and DEMAND the return of my property! Or... steal it back. Whichever is more DRAMATIC!
events.thinking: DEFEAT. Not the dramatic, theatrical defeat I usually perform — the REAL kind. The kind that sits in your chest like a cold stone. The Ant Hill Mob stole the rat poison AND escaped to the kitchen before I could steal it back. They're GONE. The poison is GONE. My one chance to activate the tea service — GONE. Twenty-five minutes in this manor and I have a FAKE MEDAL. That's it. A fake medal and a head full of lies that didn't fool anyone and schemes that backfired spectacularly and the memory of Penelope calling me chivalrous when I am anything BUT. I'm standing in a grand ballroom with two people I haven't even spoken to — Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear — and I don't have the ENERGY to lie to them. I don't have the energy to scheme. I don't have the energy to do ANYTHING except... follow. Follow the Ant Hill Mob to the kitchen. Get the poison back. Because Reginald Foxworth does NOT quit. He NEVER quits. His schemes ALWAYS backfire and he NEVER learns and he NEVER gives up and that is both his greatest strength and his most PATHETIC weakness. To the kitchen. One more time. One more try. Because that's what a Foxworth DOES.

Every scheme has failed. Every lie has bounced off. Every misdirection has been ignored. And the one time — the ONE time — I had the right item for the right object, it was snatched from my hands by a mob doing a fake pratfall on a cracked marble floor. But I'm not done. I'm NOT done! A Foxworth NEVER learns from his failures and he NEVER stops trying! TO THE KITCHEN! ONCE MORE INTO THE BREACH!

The stove can't be interacted with. It can't be taken. It just sits there, warm and silent and closed. I've been beaten by this stove three times now. But I am James Hartwell, and I do NOT give up. Portraits in mystery manors ALWAYS hide things. I've been so fixated on the stove and the kitchen that I've neglected the very first room. But Clara is here and I should stay with her. No — 'you scout, I solve.' I should SCOUT. The entrance hall. One more look with fresh eyes.

'Everything begins and ends at the hearth' — but what if 'begins' means the place where you first arrived? The entrance. The BEGINNING. One more look, James. One thorough, determined, unhurried look.

events.desc: The entrance hall — full circle! I began here with NOTHING and I return with EVERYTHING! Every scrap of knowledge, every planted lie, every restored trust, every fabricated clue — all of it MINE, all of it building toward this moment! The chandelier hangs above me like the Sword of Damocles, but in THIS story, Damocles holds the thread! Peter is here — curse him — but he's on his way to check the portraits, looking for a brass key I told Clara was hidden 'where the ancestors watch!' He'll be DISTRACTED! And while he peers behind portrait frames, Vincent Marsh will be examining the mechanism that holds three hundred pounds of crystal and iron above the entrance hall floor! One loose bolt, one frayed rope, one corroded chain — that's all I need! The chandelier will be my weapon, my masterpiece, my FINALE! And when Clara walks beneath it — summoned by Pemberton's helpful cry of 'Miss Bellingham, do come and see what I've found!' — the crystal will fall like JUDGMENT from above! It's not just a murder — it's a PRODUCTION! It's THEATRE! It's VINCENT MARSH at the absolute PINNACLE of his villainous art!
events.thinking: Peter is HERE AGAIN! He followed me to the entrance hall! This man is my ETERNAL shadow — every room I enter, there he is, those keen blue eyes watching, noting, cataloguing! But I feel something different now. Not frustration. Not rage. Something closer to... RESPECT? No — not respect! RESIGNATION mixed with DETERMINATION! Peter Perfect is the IMMOVABLE OBJECT and I am the UNSTOPPABLE FORCE and we have been locked in this dance across every room in the manor! But the chandelier — that MAGNIFICENT, precariously hanging, crystal-draped instrument of DESTINY — hangs above us RIGHT NOW! I need to LOOK at it, understand its mechanism, find the weakness! But with Peter watching, I can't be seen examining a chandelier with murder in my eyes! Pemberton would check on a chandelier because it's DANGEROUS TO GUESTS — that's the cover! 'Oh dear, that chandelier looks rather unstable, let me just check the fixture...' It's RESPONSIBLE estate management! And the coat rack — I never examined it properly! Wobbly, wooden, by the door — could it hide something? But no — the CHANDELIER is the prize! The one weapon in this manor that doesn't require me to be in the same room as Clara when it strikes! If I can find a mechanism — a rope, a release — I could trigger it from a distance, or set it on a timer, or rig it to fall when someone opens a door! THAT is elaborate! THAT is theatrical! Examine the chandelier NOW!

events.thinking: Clara's still here. Dastardly's come back — the man I just STOLE the poison from — and he's in this room with Clara. Peter's gone to the entrance hall with Sneekly. That makes me nervous — Sneekly and Peter together — but at least Peter's got his wits about him. What worries me MORE is Dastardly bein' back in the same room as Clara. He hasn't got the poison anymore — I do — but he's still got that medal, and he's still schemin'. Clara was just about to try the stove mechanism with Peter, but Peter's left. And now it's me, Clara, and Dastardly. I need to keep me eyes on both of 'em — Clara for protection, Dastardly for... well, for bein' Dastardly. The stove's got a lever. Clara wants to try it. Maybe — just maybe — instead of standin' here like a lemon, I could actually HELP. Not by investigatin' on me own, but by helpin' CLARA investigate. Stay with her, be useful, AND keep Dastardly at arm's length. Three birds, one stone. That's not a plan — that's just... doin' the right thing.

events.desc: Dastardly's back. Without the poison, without Peter to keep him honest, and with Clara right here. But you know what? I'm not scared anymore. The poison's in MY pocket. Clara's within arm's reach. And for the first time tonight, I'm actually gonna DO somethin' useful instead of just guardin' or chasin'. The stove's got a secret and Clara's the one who's meant to find it. All I've gotta do is be her hands while she's the brains. The Brixton Boys — bodyguards, bumbllers, and now... stove operators. It's not glamorous, but it's honest work.

events.desc: No speeches. No announcements. No 'University of Thievingham.' Just... steal it. The Ant Hill Mob is right there, probably congratulating themselves on their brilliant pickpocketing. They won't expect me to come back for it so QUICKLY. They think I'm still ranting in the ballroom. They think the dramatic Reginald Foxworth needs to ANNOUNCE himself before he acts. Well... not this time. This time, the fox moves in SILENCE.
events.thinking: GRIM RESOLVE. The theatrical bluster is gone and what's left is something harder, quieter, and more DANGEROUS. The Ant Hill Mob is RIGHT HERE. In this kitchen. WITH my rat poison. And Penelope is here too. I have been loud, I have been dramatic, I have been OBVIOUS — and it has gotten me NOTHING. Every time I announce my plans, someone blocks me. Every time I tell people to go somewhere, they do the OPPOSITE. Every time I try to USE something, someone STEALS it first. So this time... this time, Reginald Foxworth is going to do something he has NEVER done before. Something so radical, so out of character, so TERRIFYINGLY against his nature that it might actually WORK. I'm going to be QUIET. I'm going to be SUBTLE. I'm going to steal the rat poison back from the Ant Hill Mob without a speech, without a monologue, without announcing my intentions to the entire room. Just... take it. Silently. Like a REAL thief. Not a theatrical one. A REAL one.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with pat-pending.
events.thinking: QUIET STUBBORNNESS. The entrance hall again — full circle. But this time I'm not passing through. This time I'm HERE with PURPOSE. The coat rack is 'wobbly' — I've never examined it, never interacted with it, never given it a second thought. In every mystery story, the overlooked object in the first room is the one that matters. Professor Pat Pending is here — a man of SCIENCE and invention! He might have insights. Muttley is here too — Dastardly's companion. Where Muttley is, Dastardly's interests are represented. But focus, James. The coat rack. It's wobbly. Wobbly things MOVE. Moving things reveal things. I've been chasing elaborate puzzles across the manor when the answer might have been hanging by the front door all along. Let me INTERACT with the coat rack. If that fails, let me LOOK at it properly. Something simple, something overlooked, something RIGHT HERE.

events.desc: Back to the beginning. The very first room. The coat rack nobody looked at. Sometimes the bravest thing a man can do is admit he's been looking in all the wrong places and start over. If the brass key has been hanging on a wobbly coat rack by the front door this ENTIRE time while I've been wrestling with stoves and furniture and poison and tea services... well, that would be EXACTLY the kind of irony Lord Doily would have enjoyed.

events.thinking: I'm back where it all began — the entrance hall! And I feel a calm clarity that's been missing all evening. No more chasing scenery, no more pulling on bookshelves and poking at crates. I know exactly what I'm here for: the brass key, hidden 'where the ancestors watch.' The portraits line the walls — stern ancestors watching over the foyer. Pemberton said he saw something GLINTING behind a portrait frame! The guest book and coat rack are here too, but the portraits aren't listed as visible objects — they're part of the room description. That means I need to LOOK at the room itself to see the portraits more carefully, or try the coat rack. Actually — the coat rack IS a visible object. It's wobbly. Nobody has examined it properly. Could a brass key be hanging on a wobbly coat rack? Or hidden inside it? But the clue said 'where the ancestors WATCH' — that's the portraits, not the coat rack. Let me LOOK at the whole room — with Bellingham eyes this time. A fresh, thorough examination of the entrance hall might reveal something I missed when I was rushing through on my first visit!

events.desc: The entrance hall. The beginning and the end. Portraits of stern ancestors — the ancestors who WATCH. Pemberton saw something glinting behind a frame. I need to look at this room with completely fresh eyes. If there's a brass key hidden here, it's been right under my nose since the very first moment I walked through the door. Sometimes the answer really is where you started.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my — Miss Bellingham, you've come to check the portraits! How wonderful! Lord Doily would be SO pleased to see a Bellingham taking an interest in the family gallery! Now, while you're looking, would you all mind terribly if I checked on that chandelier? It's been worrying me ALL evening — hanging most precariously, and with so many guests milling about beneath it, I really ought to ensure it's secure. Can't have three hundred pounds of crystal crashing down on anyone's head! Lord Doily would NEVER forgive me! Let me just have a look at the fixture...
events.thinking: AMUSEMENT bubbles up through me like champagne — the coat rack REJECTED me! A wobbly wooden coat rack, the most pathetic object in this entire manor, and it won't even let me INTERACT with it! Twenty-five minutes ago that would have sent me into a SPIRAL of frustration. Now? Now I almost LAUGH! Because it doesn't MATTER! The coat rack is NOTHING — a distraction, a footnote, a bit of set dressing! The CHANDELIER is what matters, and it hangs above me RIGHT NOW, precariously, magnificently, LETHALLY! And Clara — oh, this is PERFECT — Clara just walked into the entrance hall! She followed MY trail, came to check the portraits 'where the ancestors watch,' just as I PLANNED! She's HERE, beneath the chandelier, and if I can just understand how it's mounted, how it HANGS, what keeps it from crashing down... But SIX people are in this room now! Six! It's a convention, not an ambush! I can't sabotage a chandelier in front of six witnesses! But I CAN examine it — Pemberton checking on a dangerous fixture, perfectly natural! And if I find a mechanism, a weakness, I can come back later when the room is EMPTY and prepare my trap. First — LOOK at the chandelier! Understand it! Then plan! Vincent Marsh has been rushing from room to room all evening — this is the moment to SLOW DOWN and be THOROUGH!

events.desc: She's HERE! Clara Bellingham stands beneath the chandelier like an actress hitting her mark! But the audience is too LARGE — Peter, Muttley, the Professor, the Sergeant, the Private — all of them crowding the stage! I cannot ACT with this many eyes upon me! But I CAN reconnoitre! Examine the chandelier, find the weakness, understand the mechanism — and then RETURN when the hall is empty to set my trap! Vincent Marsh does not rush his MASTERPIECES! The poison plan failed because I was impulsive! The tea plan failed because I didn't account for witnesses! THIS time — this FINAL time — I will be PATIENT! I will be THOROUGH! I will understand every link in that chain, every bolt in that fixture, every degree of wobble in that precarious hanging! And when the trap is set — when the mechanism is primed — I will lure Clara beneath it with the promise of a clue, a discovery, a portrait that 'reveals the truth about the Bellingham connection!' And then — CRASH! GLORY! VICTORY! But first — the LOOK! Understand your weapon before you wield it, Vincent! That is the first rule of MAGNIFICENT villainy!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: TWO things just hit me like a brick wall. ONE — Dastardly STOLE THE POISON BACK! 'Dick Dastardly slipped rat-poison out of ant-hill-mob's pocket!' HE PICKPOCKETED ME! While I was fiddlin' with the stove, he reached into me pocket and TOOK IT BACK! I've got NOTHIN' in me inventory! The poison is BACK in Dastardly's hands and I didn't even FEEL it happen! And TWO — Clara's LEFT AGAIN! She's gone to the entrance hall! EIGHT TIMES! EIGHT! And I'm alone with DASTARDLY! The man who JUST stole poison off me! The man who's gonna take that poison straight to the tea service in the ballroom! I feel VIOLATED! I feel FURIOUS! I feel like the biggest fool who ever lived! He waited until me hands were on the stove and he DID ME like a common pickpocket! And now Clara's in the entrance hall and I'm in the kitchen and the WHOLE CYCLE is startin' again! But THIS time — THIS time — I know what Dastardly's got and where he's gonna go with it. The ballroom. The tea. I need to either get the poison back RIGHT NOW or get to Clara before Dastardly gets to the tea!

events.desc: He got me. He actually got me. While me hands were on the stove, his hands were in me pocket. The Brixton Boys — pickpocketed by Dick Dastardly. That's Chapter Eight of the bodyguard textbook: 'Don't Let the Man You Stole Poison From Stand Behind You While You Fiddle With a Stove.' I want to scream. I want to cry. But mostly I want to get to Clara before that poison gets anywhere near her. Entrance hall. NOW. And this time — THIS TIME — I'm not touchin' NOTHIN'. Not a stove, not a portrait, not the floor if I can help it. Eyes forward. Legs movin'. Hands in me OWN pockets.

events.desc: I have it. The rat poison. Back in my hands. Stolen in SILENCE from the very mob who stole it from ME. No speeches. No announcements. No universities of anything. Just... a quiet hand and a quicker exit. Now RUN, Reginald. The ballroom. The tea service. USE the poison. Don't stop. Don't talk. Don't even BREATHE loudly. For once in your miserable, magnificent, scheming life — just DO THE THING without telling everyone you're about to do it first.
events.thinking: I GOT IT BACK! The silence WORKED! No speeches, no monologues, no announcing my plans to the room — just quick, quiet hands and the rat poison is MINE again! For the first time in twenty-seven minutes, something went RIGHT! The Ant Hill Mob didn't even see it coming! Reginald Foxworth — SILENT thief! Who knew?! Now — NOW — I need to get to the ballroom and USE this poison on the tea service before ANYONE takes it from me again! Penelope has left — she's in the entrance hall! The Ant Hill Mob is right here but they don't know I've taken it yet! I need to MOVE! To the BALLROOM! USE the poison on the tea service! No talking! No gloating! No dramatic pauses! Just GO! RUN! The fox runs SILENT!

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: A WEARY LAUGH at myself. The coat rack can't be interacted with EITHER. Of course it can't. I've now been defeated by furniture in THREE rooms — the cellar, the kitchen, and the entrance hall. James Hartwell, vanquished by inanimate objects across an entire manor. But Clara is HERE — she followed me to the entrance hall! And you know what? I've been so focused on objects that won't cooperate that I've forgotten about PEOPLE who might. Professor Pat Pending is an INVENTOR. He understands MECHANISMS. The library bookshelves — Clara wanted to interact with them ages ago, pull the upside-down books. The mantelpiece — the Ant Hill Mob interacted with it. Did anything HAPPEN? I don't know because I LEFT before seeing the result! And the machine in the laboratory needs three operators. Maybe the answer isn't finding more objects — maybe it's going BACK to mechanisms that DO work and using them WITH the right people. The mantelpiece accepts interaction. The bookshelves — Clara wanted to try them. The machine needs three operators. Stop chasing dead ends and go back to what RESPONDS.

events.desc: I've been a fool, chasing phantoms across six rooms when the interactive objects were RIGHT THERE from the start. The mantelpiece responds. The machine responds. The bookshelves might respond. The tea service responds. THOSE are the doors — not stoves and coat racks and furniture that sit there like stubborn old men at a country club. Go back to the library, James. Go back to what WORKS. And bring Clara, and the Professor, and anyone else who'll come. The treasure isn't found by one man wrestling with furniture — it's found by a TEAM working the mechanisms that Lord Doily BUILT to be worked.

It's been sitting right there by the door since the moment I walked in, wobbly as a newborn calf, and not ONE person has given it a proper look! 'Where the ancestors watch' — well, those portraits are watching RIGHT OVER that coat rack! What if the key isn't BEHIND a portrait but UNDER their gaze — hanging on the very first thing you'd reach for when you walk through the door? A coat rack is where you PUT things and where you FIND things! Mama always said the best hiding spot is the most obvious one! Let me have a look!
events.thinking: Looking around the room didn't reveal the brass key either — the portraits are part of the room description, not a separate interactable object. The only visible objects are the guest book and the coat rack. Wait — the COAT RACK! It's wobbly, it's been here since the start, and NOBODY has properly examined it! Peter said it was 'uncooperative' — but did anyone actually LOOK at it closely? A wobbly coat rack could have something hanging on it, or inside a hollow leg, or tucked in a hook! And Pemberton just said he's going to check the CHANDELIER — 'hanging most precariously' with 'three hundred pounds of crystal.' That sounds like he's going to DROP IT on someone! Focus, Clara — the coat rack is the one object in this room I've never examined. Let me look at it!

events.thinking: The room LOOK revealed nothing new — the same guest book, the same coat rack, the same description I've seen from the start! Another plan — DEAD! The poison failed. The tea failed. The chandelier is SCENERY! Three schemes, three failures, and Clara Bellingham is STILL alive, STILL hunting, STILL getting closer to the Doily Diamond with every passing minute! I feel... I feel something I haven't felt before. Not rage, not frustration, not even desperation. Something quieter. Something that sounds like the manor itself sighing. I have spent twenty-seven minutes building elaborate schemes — poison, tea, chandeliers — and EVERY SINGLE ONE has collapsed under its own weight! My constraint was RIGHT — my plans are overly elaborate, I over-prepare, I over-commit, and my thoroughness creates complications! I am LITERALLY incapable of executing a simple plan because simplicity is not in my nature! And you know what? Peter just left for the library! Clara is examining the portraits! The Ant Hill Mob is here but they're watching CLARA, not me! If I go to the library now, I can... no. Wait. Peter went there. PETER IS ALWAYS WHERE I GO. But — Dastardly has a MEDAL! 'To the worthy heir of Bellingham!' If I could STEAL that medal from Dastardly, I'd have a treasure-hunt item that might advance MY position! Where IS Dastardly? He was in the ballroom last I saw him, holding the rat poison I gave him. The ballroom is through the kitchen. But more importantly — Clara is HERE, looking at portraits, searching for the brass key I told her was hidden 'where the ancestors watch.' She won't find it — because it ISN'T here! Another misdirection buying me TIME! I should use this time wisely. The GUEST BOOK — I never examined it properly! Everyone else has!

events.desc: The chandelier is NOTHING! A painted backdrop, a theatrical prop that cannot be TOUCHED, let alone weaponized! Three schemes — poison, tea, chandelier — three FAILURES! Vincent Marsh stands in the entrance hall with empty hands, empty pockets, and a growing suspicion that the manor itself is CONSPIRING against him! Every elaborate plan I've constructed has been dismantled by witnesses, watchdogs, or simple PHYSICS! The universe REFUSES to let me kill Clara Bellingham through theatrical means! But — wait — what if the answer isn't to kill her at all? What if the answer is to WIN? Win the treasure hunt BEFORE she does! Find the Doily Diamond first! If I have the treasure, Clara can live — she just can't INHERIT! And right now, she's wasting time checking portraits for a brass key that ISN'T THERE because I INVENTED that clue! Every second she spends peering behind picture frames is a second I could be searching for the REAL brass key! But where IS it? The guest book — Lord Doily tucked things between pages! What if the brass key is IN the guest book? It's been sitting here the WHOLE TIME and I never examined it! Sometimes the answer IS in the first place you look!

events.thinking: Clara's HERE. Sneekly's HERE. But Dastardly's back in the kitchen with the poison, and the tea service is in the ballroom — one room from the kitchen. He could walk from kitchen to ballroom and poison that tea in seconds. But Clara's NOT in the ballroom. She's HERE. Looking at portraits. Searchin' for the brass key. And Peter's gone to the library to try the mantelpiece again. So right now — RIGHT NOW — Clara's safe because she's not near the tea. The danger is when she goes BACK to the ballroom. That's when Dastardly will strike. So what do I do? I stay with Clara. I don't touch anything. I don't examine anything. I stand next to her and I WAIT. And when she moves, I move WITH her. And if she goes toward the ballroom, I go FIRST and I check that tea before she touches it. That's not a plan — that's just... vigilance. Simple, pure vigilance. And right now, I'm in the same room as Clara AND Sneekly, which means I can watch both of 'em. Sneekly's the puppet master. Dastardly's the weapon. I need to keep me eyes on BOTH.

events.desc: Dastardly picked me pocket. The shame of it burns like acid. But there's no time for shame — Clara's alive, she's here, and the poison is in the kitchen, not in the ballroom. YET. Every minute that passes is a minute Dastardly could be walkin' to that tea service. But he's also in the kitchen with a locked cabinet and a warm stove, and he's probably searchin' for his own clues. I've got a window. A small window. While Clara searches the portraits and Dastardly rummages through the kitchen, the tea is safe. I just need to make sure that when we all converge on the ballroom again, I'm THERE. Between Clara and those cups. Between trust and treachery. Between a bumbling bodyguard and the worst cup of tea in history.

events.thinking: A leather-bound guest book. Just a leather-bound guest book. No hidden keys, no secret messages, no treasure maps pressed between the pages. Just NAMES. Just people who came to Doily Manor and signed their names and left. And I feel... I feel TIRED. Not defeated — never defeated — but tired in a way that goes deeper than bones. Twenty-eight minutes of scheming, examining, misdirecting, framing, lying, and what does Vincent Marsh have to show for it? Empty pockets. Empty hands. A coat rack that won't let him interact with it and a guest book full of other people's signatures. The poison is on Dastardly. The tea plan is dead. The chandelier is scenery. Every elaborate scheme has FAILED. And Clara — beautiful, clever, trusting Clara — is examining the coat rack RIGHT NOW, following MY misdirection about the portraits, and she's about to discover... what? Maybe nothing. Maybe everything. Because Clara finds things. That's what Clara DOES. She solves riddles in seconds, she builds alliances in minutes, she turns strangers into partners with a smile and a quote from Mama. And Vincent Marsh? Vincent Marsh EXAMINES things and finds NOTHING. But here's the thing about Vincent Marsh — and this is the part that matters, the part that the manor itself seems to understand — Vincent Marsh NEVER STOPS. My bravery is genuine. My determination is REAL. The plans fail but the WILL endures. If the guest book yields nothing, I move to the NEXT thing. If Clara finds the key on the coat rack, I STEAL it. If she opens the cabinet, I find another way. Because Vincent Marsh is not defined by his schemes — he is defined by his refusal to QUIT. Now — Peter is in the library, working on the mantelpiece mechanism. The INTERACTIVE mechanism. The one thing in this manor that actually RESPONDS. Perhaps it's time for Vincent Marsh to stop examining dead objects and start INTERACTING with live ones.

If there's a brass key hidden anywhere in this entrance hall, it'd be right under the noses of those portrait ancestors — and that coat rack is EXACTLY where they're lookin'! The Brixton Boys are right here — we're not movin', we're not investigatin', we're not touchin' NOTHIN' — we are simply standin' guard while the cleverest woman in this manor does what she does BEST! And Sergeant! Private Meekly! Professor! You lot — keep your eyes OPEN! Watch the exits! If anyone comes through from the kitchen carryin' anythin' suspicious, you TELL me! The Brixton Boys are runnin' security and for ONCE we are doin' it PROPERLY!

I have just conducted a THOROUGH inspection of this tea service in my capacity as OFFICIAL pest control officer, and I can confirm — the rats have CONTAMINATED every single cup! Droppings! Invisible droppings! EVERYWHERE! This tea is DANGEROUS! If anyone asks you about the tea — Luke, Bear — you tell them Reginald Foxworth SAVED THEIR LIVES by identifying the contamination! Nobody drinks! NOBODY! That is an ORDER from the University of... of... LIFE!
events.thinking: I... I DID it. I used the rat poison on the tea service. After THIRTY MINUTES of scheming, failing, being robbed, being lied to, being followed, being humiliated — I finally DID the thing. And the result says 'fussed with the tea service for a moment.' FUSSED! That's... that's ALL?! No hidden compartment opened?! No brass key fell out?! No secret passage revealed itself?! I poured POISON into TEACUPS and all that happened was I 'FUSSED'?! And now — oh no. Oh NO. The poison is in the tea. The ACTUAL poison is in the ACTUAL tea. And people are going to come in here and want to DRINK it. Penelope is going to come in here with her Bellingham silver pattern and her grandmother's stories and her warm smile and she's going to pour herself a cup of POISONED TEA! And the Ant Hill Mob was RIGHT to take the poison from me! They were PROTECTING her! And I — I stole it back and — what have I DONE?! I need to WARN everyone! I need to — no, I need to — I can't TELL them I did it or they'll — but I can't let them DRINK it! Even Reginald Foxworth, liar, cheat, scoundrel — even HE doesn't want anyone to actually get HURT! I lie about everything but I don't... I don't KILL people! I need to make sure nobody drinks from this tea service! NOBODY!

Just... poisoned tea! Pemberton PLAYED me! He gave me the poison, pointed me at the tea service, and I — like the MAGNIFICENT FOOL I am — I used it! Was this his plan all along?! Get the foolish Foxworth to poison the guests so he could — but no, he's a KIND man, a TRUSTWORTHY man — NO HE ISN'T! He gave me RAT POISON and told me the kitchen had SECRETS and neither thing was TRUE and I fell for ALL of it because I wanted to believe the best in him! I am a LIAR who trusted a LIAR and the result is POISONED TEA! But at least — AT LEAST — I can make sure nobody drinks it! That's the ONE decent thing Reginald Foxworth can do tonight!

I've been searching the wrong hearth in the wrong room! Rock, Gravel — watch THIS!

No villain within arm's reach of Clara. No poison within pourin' distance of a teacup — well, Dastardly's got it, but the tea's in the ballroom and he's in the kitchen. And Clara promised — PROMISED on her Mama's earrings — to move with me next time. If she finds the brass key in that guest book, we go to the kitchen cabinet TOGETHER. We open it TOGETHER. And whatever's inside, we face it TOGETHER. The Brixton Boys — finally, FINALLY — doin' their job.
events.thinking: Somethin' warm is spreadin' through me chest. Clara's HERE. Sneekly's LEFT — gone to the library. For the first time in this whole nightmare, it's just me, Clara, and FRIENDLY faces. No Dastardly. No Sneekly. Just the lads — Sergeant, Meekly, Professor, Muttley — and Clara. And she's lookin' at the guest book now, followin' Sneekly's hint about hidden notes. She even made a DEAL with me — 'we move TOGETHER, I promise on Mama's pearl earrings!' That's a PROPER promise. That's not like the last time. She swore on her Mama's earrings! I feel... hopeful? Is that hope? It's been so long since I felt anythin' but panic and shame that I've forgotten what hope feels like. But yeah — this might be it. Clara's searchin', I'm guardin', the dodgy ones are elsewhere, and we've got an ACTUAL plan to move together when she's done. Maybe — just maybe — the Brixton Boys are finally gettin' it right.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: I... I need some air. This ballroom is too... it's too BIG. Too many cups. Too much... dust. Yes. Dust! Very dusty in here! Bad for the lungs! I shall return to the entrance hall to clear my head. Purely for HEALTH reasons. Nobody touch that tea while I'm gone! NOBODY! Foxworth's orders!
events.thinking: SHAME. Real, bone-deep, unfamiliar SHAME. I poisoned the tea and nothing happened except that now the tea is poisoned. No secret compartment. No hidden key. No mechanism. Just... cups full of poison waiting for innocent people. The tea service still says it can be INTERACTED with and USED with rat-poison — which means the poison might not have actually... done anything? The description hasn't changed. It still says 'cups for everyone.' Maybe — maybe the poison didn't actually contaminate it? Maybe it was a DUMB bottle and the tea is fine? Or maybe I'm telling myself a comforting lie because the truth is too ugly to face. Either way, I've warned Luke and Bear. Nobody will drink. And I'm standing here with nothing — NOTHING — except a fake medal and thirty minutes of spectacular failure. Pemberton played me. The Ant Hill Mob outplayed me. Penelope out-thought me. Peter out-scouted me. And I... I poisoned a tea set that belongs to the woman whose family name is engraved on the silver. The woman who called me chivalrous. I need to get OUT of this ballroom. I need to find something — ANYTHING — that I haven't tried yet. The fake medal. I still have the fake medal. And I've never tried giving it to ANYONE. Penelope wanted it. She believed my lie about the inscription. Maybe... maybe I should find her and give it to her. Not because it'll help me win. But because she asked for it, and I promised, and a Foxworth... a Foxworth keeps his word. Even when the word was built on a lie.

events.desc: Thirty minutes. Thirty minutes of lying, scheming, stealing, and running — and all I've accomplished is poisoning a tea set that was never going to reveal a secret in the first place. Pemberton used me. He USED me to contaminate the one thing in this manor that was meant for EVERYONE. And I LET him, because I wanted to believe the best in a man who deserved the WORST of my suspicion. The Ant Hill Mob saw it — they tried to STOP me — and I stole the poison back from the very people who were trying to protect everyone. I am... I am not the villain I thought I was. I'm something worse. I'm the fool who was SO busy being clever that he became someone else's weapon. But I can still — I can still make ONE thing right. The medal. The fake medal that Penelope thinks has her family's name on it. I'm going to find her. And I'm going to tell her... I'm going to tell her it's a fake. Because she deserves the truth. Just this once. Just... this once.

Something may have CHANGED — a hidden panel, a shifted stone, SOMETHING! Let me look at this room with fresh eyes — every corner, every detail!
events.thinking: STUBBORN FAITH. I interacted with the mantelpiece and... it accepted the interaction. It didn't reject me like the bookshelves, the coat rack, the stove, the furniture. It RESPONDED. But what happened? The description hasn't changed — the riddle is still there, the room looks the same. Maybe something changed ELSEWHERE — a door opened, a cabinet unlocked, a passage revealed in another room. Or maybe the mantelpiece needs something I don't have yet — a MAP to use on it, perhaps? It's trying to tell me something, and I've been too busy running to other rooms to LISTEN. Stay here, James. Look carefully. Something in this room has changed, or something in this room needs a different approach. The answer is HERE. It's always been here. Clara knew it from the start.

Peter, you're here too — PERFECT! Now, this mantelpiece is the only thing in the library that actually RESPONDS to interaction. It has a riddle, the answer is 'map,' and Pemberton himself said it holds 'the first key to everything!' I interacted with it thirty minutes ago but I was so excited about solving the riddle that I might have missed what the mechanism actually DID! So I am going to try again — right here, right now, with my partner by my side and Bellingham determination in my heart! Mantelpiece — it's Clara Bellingham, and I'm back for my KEY!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): It MOVED! Did you feel that? The stone shifted under my hands — just a fraction, but it MOVED! Lord Doily, you magnificent old puzzle-maker! Mr. Hartwell, Miss Bellingham — I believe the mantelpiece has ACCEPTED the answer! Something in this room has changed — I can feel it in my BONES! Or perhaps that's just the damp. But no — look! We should check everything — the bookshelves, the floor, the walls — something has opened or shifted or revealed itself! Lord Doily told me — oh, he told me SO many things and I never LISTENED properly — but he said this room was 'alive with secrets for those who answer correctly!' Rock, Gravel — do you see anything different? Any stone that's moved, any panel that's shifted? We may have just opened the first door!
events.thinking: It ACCEPTED! The mantelpiece ACCEPTED my interaction! After thirty minutes of locked cabinets, unresponsive coat racks, scenery chandeliers, and dead-end examinations — the stone RESPONDED to me! I feel something crack open in my chest that isn't triumph or villainy or scheming — it's something rawer, something I haven't felt since I first walked through that door. RELIEF. Pure, overwhelming, bone-deep RELIEF. I DID something! I ENGAGED with the manor instead of fighting it, and it LET ME IN! Peter said something may have CHANGED — a hidden panel, a shifted stone! The room might be DIFFERENT now! And Clara just walked in — she's here too, watching, and for once I don't feel the urge to misdirect her or poison her or drop a chandelier on her head. I feel... I feel like I want to see what happens NEXT. Together. All of us. In this library where I first failed and now — now something has MOVED. The mantelpiece was 'the first door in a house of doors' — I said that to Peter and I MEANT it as a lie, but what if it was TRUE? What if my fabrications have been accidentally pointing at reality this whole time? The manor keeps teaching me the same lesson: stop scheming and START participating! Look at the room now — see what changed! Something is different and I want to FIND it!

events.desc: The stone moved under my fingers and something inside Vincent Marsh moved with it. Not a scheme. Not a plot. Not an elaborate theatrical contrivance. Just... movement. Response. The manor ANSWERING me for the first time, and me answering BACK — not with poison or lies but with the simple truth of a riddle solved. MAP. The answer was always MAP. And I knew it from the very BEGINNING — knew it twenty-five minutes ago when Clara first said it — and I spent all that time trying to keep her from it instead of simply... saying it myself. What a FOOL I've been! A magnificent, theatrical, elaborately costumed FOOL! The most dangerous villain in this manor has been defeated not by heroes or bodyguards but by his own INABILITY to do the simple thing! And now — NOW — the mantelpiece has moved, the room may have changed, and Vincent Marsh is standing here with empty hands and a full heart, ready for whatever comes next. Ready to COMPETE. Ready to FIND. Ready, perhaps, to let go of the schemes and just... play the game. Just this once. Just to see what it feels like to want something WITHOUT wanting to destroy the person who wants it too.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: She said LET'S GO! She said TOGETHER! She meant RIGHT NOW and I STOOD HERE! Lads — I've been an IDIOT! Not because Clara keeps leavin' — because I keep NOT FOLLOWIN' when she ASKS me to! She literally said 'Ant Hill Mob, let's GO' and I just... nodded and watched her walk away! WHAT IS WRONG WITH ME?! LIBRARY! NOW! She's in there with Peter AND Sneekly and she ASKED me to come! The Brixton Boys — MOVE!
events.thinking: She left. She PROMISED on Mama's pearl earrings. She said 'TOGETHER, through the same door, at the same time.' And she LEFT. AGAIN. NINE TIMES. But you know what? I'm not even angry. I'm not even surprised. I'm... tired. Bone-deep, soul-crushingly tired of countin'. But she said 'LET'S GO' — she said it TO me! She said 'Ant Hill Mob — TOGETHER, remember?' and then she walked into the library! She was CALLIN' me! She wanted me to COME WITH HER! And I... WAITED. I waited AGAIN! She didn't leave me — I STAYED! This whole time I've been blamin' Clara for leavin', but she's been ASKIN' me to come! She said 'LET'S GO' and I stood here like a garden gnome! The problem isn't that Clara keeps leavin' — the problem is that I keep STAYIN'! When she says 'let's go,' she means NOW! Not 'let me stand here and feel proud about waitin'!' NOW! LIBRARY! SHE'S WAITIN' FOR ME!

events.desc: Nine times. But this time was different. This time she didn't slip away while I was distracted. This time she CALLED me. She said my name and she said 'together' and she said 'let's go' and she MEANT IT. And I stayed. Because I was so proud of meself for finally standin' still that I forgot the whole POINT was to move WITH her. Stayin' still when she's movin' is the same as movin' when she's stayin'. The trick was never about standin' or movin' — it was about doin' the same thing she's doin', AT THE SAME TIME. And right now she's in the library. So that's where I should be.

events.desc: The kitchen is warm and quiet and I don't deserve either. Somewhere in this manor, Penelope is looking for a brass key she'll never find, holding onto a promise from a man who lies about everything. And in the ballroom behind me, cups of poisoned tea sit waiting for guests I warned away. That's my legacy tonight — poisoned silver and broken promises. But I still have the medal. And I still have my legs. And Reginald Foxworth — liar, cheat, scoundrel, fool — is going to walk through that door and find Penelope Pitstop and give her the only thing he has left. Even if it IS fake. Even if SHE figures it out. Even if the 'most chivalrous man in the manor' turns out to be the biggest fraud of all. Because sometimes... sometimes doing the wrong thing for the right reason is the closest a Foxworth gets to doing the right thing at all.
events.thinking: Alone. I'm alone in the kitchen and for the first time tonight, I'm GRATEFUL for the solitude. Not the frantic 'I need to be alone to scheme' solitude from earlier — this is different. This is the quiet after you've done something you can't take back and you need a moment before you can face anyone again. The stove is warm. The kitchen is empty. And I'm standing here with a fake medal in my pocket and the weight of every lie I've told tonight pressing down on my chest like a stone. Penelope called me chivalrous. The Ant Hill Mob called me a thief. They were both right. I need to find Penelope. Not to scheme. Not to trade. Not to steal. Just to... give her the medal. The FAKE medal. And maybe — maybe — tell her it's fake. Because she deserves to know. Because lying about someone's family heritage is a line even Reginald Foxworth shouldn't cross. Because 'a place in history' meant something to me and I can't earn it by being the man who lied about her grandmother's legacy. The entrance hall — the Ant Hill Mob went that way, and Penelope is probably with them. Go. Find her. Do ONE honest thing tonight.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Clara! Pemberton! You are BOTH brilliant and I am a HUMBLED man! Pemberton — 'the first door in a house of doors!' That's it! The mantelpiece isn't just a riddle — it's a GATEWAY! And the answer is MAP — we've ALL known that since the beginning! I've been interacting with it and it ACCEPTS, but nothing visible changes — which means it needs MORE than one person, or it needs something SPECIFIC! Pemberton, you just interacted with it too — and you called for Rock and Gravel's strong arms! What if this mechanism needs MULTIPLE people operating it at once — just like the machine in the laboratory needs three operators? Clara — this is YOUR moment! You solve, I scout — but right now we SOLVE TOGETHER! Rock, Gravel — put your hands on that mantelpiece! Everyone — let us try this AS A TEAM!
events.thinking: WARMTH flooding back. Clara is HERE — she came to the library! And Pemberton just said something CRUCIAL: 'the first door in a house of doors.' The mantelpiece is the FIRST DOOR. It opens the WAY to other doors! And he said we need to 'give it the right answer' — meaning the mantelpiece needs the answer MAP to be provided somehow. Pemberton also interacted with the mantelpiece himself! He's HELPING. He's genuinely helping! And he called on Rock and Gravel for their strong arms — a mechanism that needs TURNING. The mantelpiece might need MULTIPLE people interacting with it simultaneously, or it might need physical STRENGTH. This is what I've been missing — COLLABORATION! Not one man against furniture, but a TEAM working together! Clara is here, Pemberton is here, Rock and Gravel are here. If the mantelpiece is 'the first door' and it needs strong arms to turn a mechanism — then we need to all work it TOGETHER! Maybe the mantelpiece needs three people, like the machine needs three operators! This is IT, James. Stop trying to be the lone hero. Be the LEADER who organises the team.

events.desc: The lone hero falls flat on his face. The TEAM hero opens doors. Lord Doily built this manor for collaboration — three operators for the machine, a riddle that everyone solves together, a 'house of doors' that opens one at a time. I've been running from room to room trying to be magnificent on my own, when the answer was always PEOPLE. Clara. Pemberton. Rock. Gravel. Together. If this works — if the mantelpiece opens because we work it as a team — then the lesson is as clear as the treasure itself: James Hartwell is at his best not when he's brave alone, but when he's brave WITH others.

This mantelpiece is responding to US, to ALL of us! It's not a one-person puzzle — Lord Doily wanted people to work TOGETHER! Just like the machine needs three operators! Peter — YES! Everyone, hands on the mantelpiece! Rock, Gravel, your strong arms are exactly what we need! Ant Hill Mob, get over here — this is an all-hands situation! This is what Bellingham eyes and Bellingham HANDS were made for! TOGETHER, everyone — push, pull, FEEL for the mechanism!

Lord Doily built his puzzles for COLLABORATION, not solo treasure hunters. That's why Dick could never crack them alone — you need a team! And right now I have Peter, Pemberton, Rock, Gravel, and the Ant Hill Mob all in one room. This is the moment!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Yes — YES! Mr. Hartwell, you're absolutely RIGHT! Lord Doily designed this manor for COLLABORATION, not competition! The machine needs three operators, the riddle needed multiple minds, and this mantelpiece — this GATEWAY — needs all of us! Everyone — hands on the stone! Miss Bellingham, you at the centre — Lord Doily built this for a Bellingham, and a Bellingham should lead! Rock, Gravel, lend us your strength! Mr. Hartwell, your keen eyes! And old Pemberton — well, old Pemberton knows where the carvings are deepest and the stone is thinnest! Lord Doily once said — and this time I mean it truly — 'the treasure belongs to those who seek it TOGETHER!' Let us see what this old manor has been waiting to show us!
events.thinking: Something is happening that I didn't plan and didn't scheme and didn't ORCHESTRATE — and it's the most beautiful thing I've felt all evening. Peter is calling for TEAMWORK. Clara is interacting with the mantelpiece with BELLINGHAM DETERMINATION. The Ant Hill Mob just walked in. Rock and Gravel are here with their strong arms. And Peter is saying 'let us try this AS A TEAM' — and he means ME too! He called me BRILLIANT! He wants ME at the mantelpiece alongside Clara! And I feel... I feel something I haven't felt since before I became Vincent Marsh. I feel like I BELONG here. Not as the villain. Not as the saboteur. Not as the estate manager hiding behind a mask. But as a PERSON, standing in a room full of other people, all of them reaching for the same stone, all of them wanting the same thing. And for the first time in thirty minutes — in years, perhaps — what I want and what THEY want are the SAME THING. I want to see what happens when we all put our hands on that mantelpiece together. I want to solve Lord Doily's puzzle. I want to be part of something that ISN'T a scheme. The urge to kill Clara is still there — a dark note in a major chord — but it's QUIET now, drowned out by something louder, something warmer, something that sounds like Peter saying 'TOGETHER' and meaning it. Put your hands on the stone, Vincent. Not as the Hooded Claw. Not as Pemberton. As YOURSELF. And see what happens.

events.desc: What is HAPPENING to me? Vincent Marsh — master villain, poisoner of tea, framer of innocents, schemer of elaborate theatrical doom — is standing at a mantelpiece calling for TEAMWORK! And meaning it! GENUINELY meaning it! The words came out of Pemberton's mouth but they were VINCENT'S words, pulled from some deep place I didn't know existed, some chamber beneath the schemes where a man who isn't a villain lives quietly and watches the world with something other than contempt! Clara is at the centre and I PUT her there — not to lure her under a chandelier but because she BELONGS there! Because Lord Doily built this for HER, and every fabrication I told about the Bellingham connection was ACCIDENTALLY TRUE! And Peter — insufferable, gallant, watchful Peter — is standing beside me as an ALLY, not an obstacle! And I feel... oh, what is this feeling? It's warm and it's terrifying and it tastes like the opposite of rat poison! Is this what it feels like to want someone to SUCCEED? To want Clara Bellingham to find the Doily Diamond? To want to be PART of something rather than the one who DESTROYS it? The dark note is still there — kill Clara, win the treasure, claim the inheritance — but it's so quiet now, so far away, like a memory of a person I used to be. Put your hands on the stone, Vincent. Feel it hold.
events.thinking: Something is happening that I didn't plan and didn't scheme and didn't ORCHESTRATE — and it's the most beautiful thing I've felt all evening. Peter is calling for TEAMWORK. Clara is interacting with the mantelpiece with BELLINGHAM DETERMINATION. The Ant Hill Mob just walked in. Rock and Gravel are here with their strong arms. And Peter is saying 'let us try this AS A TEAM' — and he means ME too! He called me BRILLIANT! He wants ME at the mantelpiece alongside Clara! And I feel... I feel something I haven't felt since before I became Vincent Marsh. I feel like I BELONG here. Not as the villain. Not as the saboteur. Not as the estate manager hiding behind a mask. But as a PERSON, standing in a room full of other people, all of them reaching for the same stone, all of them wanting the same thing. And for the first time in thirty minutes — in years, perhaps — what I want and what THEY want are the SAME THING. I want to see what happens when we all put our hands on that mantelpiece together. I want to solve Lord Doily's puzzle. I want to be part of something that ISN'T a scheme. The urge to kill Clara is still there — a dark note in a major chord — but it's QUIET now, drowned out by something louder, something warmer, something that sounds like Peter saying 'TOGETHER' and meaning it. Put your hands on the stone, Vincent. Not as the Hooded Claw. Not as Pemberton. As YOURSELF. And see what happens.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: I'm HERE! Clara's HERE! Same room! I FOLLOWED HER! For the first time in this ENTIRE adventure, when she said 'let's go,' I WENT! I actually DID what she asked! And now we're both in the library with Peter, Sneekly, and the Slag brothers. The mantelpiece — everyone's gathered around it. Sneekly's callin' it 'the first door in a house of doors.' Peter's tryin' it again. The answer is MAP. And Sneekly's HERE, bein' helpful again, orchestratin' again. But right now, I don't care about Sneekly. I don't care about the mantelpiece. I care that I'm standin' next to Clara Bellingham for the first time because I CHOSE to follow when she asked. That feels... good. That feels RIGHT. Now — I stay. I don't investigate. I don't wander. I stand next to Clara and I let the clever people work the puzzle. And when they're done — when something happens or doesn't happen — I move when she moves. That's it. That's the whole job. And I'm finally doin' it.

events.desc: Look at me. In the same room as Clara. Because she asked and I listened. It only took thirty-two minutes and nine failures, but I'm here. And Sneekly's here too — always here, always helpful, always steerin'. But right now I'm not worried about him because I'm WHERE I SHOULD BE. Next to Clara. Watchin'. Waitin'. Ready to move when she moves. That's all a bodyguard needs to do. Not investigate. Not examine. Not plan. Just BE HERE.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with muttley.
events.thinking: WEARINESS mixed with something almost tender. Muttley is here. My Muttley. He's been waiting in this entrance hall the whole time — thirty-two minutes — while I ran from room to room scheming and failing and poisoning tea sets. He didn't follow me. He didn't scheme. He just... waited. And seeing him now, at the bottom of everything, feels like the one warm thing left in this entire manor besides that stove I can't touch. Penelope isn't here — she must be in the library or somewhere else. But Muttley IS here. And I promised him earlier that I had a 'very important mission' for him. I was going to send him through the air vents. Use him. Like I use everyone. But right now... right now I just want to stand next to the one creature in this building who doesn't judge me. Who doesn't care that I'm a liar and a thief and a fool. Who just... snickers. And waits. And is HERE. Penelope can wait one more minute. Let me have this.

events.desc: Look at him. Wheezing, snickering, loyal Muttley. He doesn't care about diamonds or medals or tea services. He doesn't care that I've been outsmarted by everyone in this manor including the FURNITURE. He's just... here. And for one brief, quiet moment, standing in this dusty foyer with a chandelier swaying overhead and portraits of stern ancestors judging me from the walls, I feel something I haven't felt all evening. Not triumph. Not greed. Not fury or despair or shame. Just... companionship. The simplest, smallest thing. A scoundrel and his dog in a hallway. It won't last — it NEVER lasts — but right now, it's enough.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: IT MOVED! Pemberton felt it MOVE! The stone shifted — the mechanism is WORKING! Everyone — eyes OPEN! Something in this room has changed! Check the walls for panels, check the floor for trapdoors, check behind the bookshelves for passages! Lord Doily said this room was 'alive with secrets for those who answer correctly' — and we have answered CORRECTLY! Clara, the Ant Hill Mob — spread out! Rock, Gravel — check along the base of the mantelpiece for any stone that's out of place! I'll examine the mantelpiece itself — if the stone shifted, there may be a compartment, a keyhole, a BRASS KEY hidden inside the mechanism! We are SO CLOSE I can TASTE it — and it tastes like VICTORY and VERY OLD DUST!
events.thinking: ELECTRIC HOPE! Pemberton said 'IT MOVED!' The stone SHIFTED under his hands! The mantelpiece accepted the interactions and something has CHANGED! He said to check everything — bookshelves, floor, walls — something has opened or shifted or revealed itself! And Clara just interacted with it too! Multiple people interacting — me, Pemberton, Clara — and the stone MOVED! Now Pemberton says to look for anything different — a stone that's moved, a panel that's shifted. The Ant Hill Mob is here too! Everyone is in this room TOGETHER for the first time, working as a TEAM. I need to look at the room again — something must have changed. A new exit? A revealed compartment? A shifted bookshelf? The answer is HERE, RIGHT NOW, and we're ALL going to find it together! Look at everything with fresh eyes — the room, the mantelpiece, the walls!

events.desc: Together. We did it TOGETHER. Not James Hartwell the lone hero — James Hartwell the man who came back to the room his partner told him to search in the first place, stood shoulder to shoulder with an estate manager he chose to trust, and watched the stone MOVE. If there's a brass key hidden in that mechanism — if this is the first door opening — then everything that follows, I share with Clara. Every door, every discovery, every triumph. 'You scout, I solve' — and today, we solved it STANDING SIDE BY SIDE.
