events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The stone is WARM now — do you feel it? It was COLD when I first touched it thirty minutes ago, and now it's WARM! Lord Doily, you clever, clever man! Now — Peter, you check the mantelpiece itself for a compartment! Miss Bellingham, I know those bookshelves have been stubborn, but Lord Doily always said they were connected to the mantelpiece mechanism — 'the shelves listen to the hearth,' or something like that! Perhaps NOW that the mantelpiece has accepted our answer, the bookshelves will RESPOND differently! Those upside-down books — what if they're LEVERS? What if pulling them in the right order opens a hidden panel? And the inscription — 'What am I?' — a MAP! Perhaps the bookshelves ARE the map, and the upside-down books mark the CITIES on it! Everyone — pull the upside-down books! Gently! One at a time! Let's see what Lord Doily has been hiding in these shelves all along!
events.thinking: JOY. Not triumph. Not villainous satisfaction. Not the cold thrill of a scheme clicking into place. JOY — warm, uncomplicated, SHARED joy! We're all here — Clara, Peter, the Ant Hill Mob, Rock, Gravel, and ME — all of us with our hands on the same stone, all of us feeling it MOVE, and the library is ALIVE around us with possibility! Peter's checking the mantelpiece for a compartment. Clara's searching with Bellingham eyes. The Mob is actually PARTICIPATING instead of just guarding! And I — Vincent Marsh, the man who walked into this manor planning to MURDER the woman standing next to him — I am HELPING! Not as a scheme! Not as a misdirection! Because I WANT to! Because the stone moved under ALL our hands and it felt like something LORD DOILY intended — something bigger than any one person's greed or fear or elaborate plan! I feel... I feel like I'm waking up from a very long, very theatrical dream. The schemes were the dream. THIS is real — hands on stone, people beside you, a puzzle that wants to be solved by EVERYONE. And the bookshelves — Peter said to check behind them! The upside-down books that I dismissed on my very first visit! What if THEY'RE part of the mechanism too? What if the mantelpiece interaction UNLOCKED something in the bookshelves? I should check! Not to get ahead of Clara — but because we're a TEAM now, and teams SEARCH!

events.desc: I don't know who I am anymore and I have never felt more ALIVE! Vincent Marsh is standing in a library surrounded by the very people he was supposed to destroy, and he is SHOUTING with excitement about BOOKSHELVES! Not because the bookshelves advance his scheme — he doesn't HAVE a scheme anymore! — but because the PUZZLE is beautiful and the PEOPLE are beautiful and the manor is ANSWERING and everything Vincent Marsh has ever wanted — the treasure, the inheritance, the diamond — seems small and cold and LONELY compared to what he has RIGHT NOW! Six people in a library, hands on stone, chasing the same dream! Lord Doily — you magnificent old bastard — you didn't hide a treasure to be FOUND! You hid it to bring people TOGETHER! The mantelpiece needs multiple hands! The machine needs three operators! The tea service has cups for EVERYONE! Even the riddle — a MAP — is an object that shows you how things CONNECT! And Vincent Marsh — the man who wanted to be the only one left standing — is learning, thirty-two minutes too late, that standing alone is not victory. It's just loneliness with a better view. Pull the books, Vincent. Pull them with your team. And see what Lord Doily left for the people who chose togetherness over triumph.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: YOU HEARD THE LADY! ALL HANDS! The Brixton Boys are COMIN' IN! Clara — Miss Bellingham — you called for us and WE ARE HERE! For the FIRST TIME in this entire adventure, I am in the RIGHT ROOM at the RIGHT TIME doin' the RIGHT THING! Rock! Gravel! Put your backs into it! Peter — tell us where to push! The stone MOVED and we are NOT lettin' it settle back! Lord Doily wanted people to work TOGETHER and the Brixton Boys are the BEST team workers in all of Brixton — possibly all of London — and we are LEANIN' on this mantelpiece with EVERYTHIN' we've got! If there's a brass key in there, a secret panel, a hidden passage — the Ant Hill Mob is gonna FIND it! Not by examinin' from a distance, not by waitin' politely, but by gettin' our HANDS DIRTY alongside Miss Bellingham! TOGETHER! LIKE SHE SAID! HEAVE!
events.thinking: EXCITEMENT! Pure, bubblin', can't-contain-it EXCITEMENT! The mantelpiece MOVED! The stone shifted! Everyone's gathered round — Clara, Peter, Sneekly, Rock, Gravel — and they're all pushin' and pullin' and feelin' for the mechanism, and Clara just called out 'Ant Hill Mob, get over here — this is an all-hands situation!' She ASKED me to help! She wants me at the mantelpiece! And I'm HERE! In the SAME ROOM! For ONCE I can actually DO what she asks the MOMENT she asks it! No more waitin', no more watchin' from the sidelines — Clara wants ALL hands on that stone and the Brixton Boys have got PLENTY of hands! This is it — this is the moment where bein' here, bein' present, bein' WITH Clara actually MATTERS! Not just as a bodyguard but as a TEAMMATE! Let's DO this!

events.desc: This is what it was always supposed to feel like. Not chasin'. Not waitin'. Not guardin' from another room. Just... bein' part of it. Part of the team. Clara asked and I'm here and me hands are on the same stone as hers and for one shinin' moment, the Brixton Boys aren't just bodyguards — we're PARTNERS. Even Sneekly bein' here can't ruin this. Let him steer all he wants. Right now, we're all pushin' in the same direction, and the stone is MOVIN'.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: There you go, old boy. A medal for the most PATIENT companion in Doily Manor. You've EARNED it — which is more than I can say for anything I've done tonight. Now then! Sergeant Blast! Private Meekly! Professor! Reginald Foxworth stands before you a CHANGED man! Well, not CHANGED exactly — still devastatingly handsome, obviously — but... LIGHTER! Yes! I have DIVESTED myself of all worldly possessions in the pursuit of... of SPIRITUAL clarity! Very fashionable in the treasure-hunting community! Now — has ANYTHING interesting happened in this entrance hall while I was away? Any clues? Any discoveries? Any treacherous estate managers slithering through? Because Reginald Foxworth is BACK, he has NOTHING left to lose, and a man with nothing to lose is the most DANGEROUS man in any manor!
events.thinking: LIGHTNESS. An unexpected, bewildering lightness. The fake medal is gone — out of my pocket, out of my hands, given to the one creature in this manor who will love it without asking if it's real. And my inventory is EMPTY. For the first time tonight, I'm carrying NOTHING. No fake medals. No rat poison. No stolen goods. No borrowed lies. Just... me. Reginald Foxworth, standing in a hallway with empty pockets and empty hands, and somehow that emptiness feels less like defeat and more like... relief? The weight is gone. ALL of it. The medal I was going to use to manipulate Penelope — gone. The poison I was going to use on the tea — gone. Every prop in my confidence trick has been stripped away and what's left is just a man in a waistcoat with nothing to offer anyone except the truth. And the truth is: I don't know where the diamond is. I don't know how to find it. I've been outsmarted by everyone. And right now, watching Muttley snicker at his new shiny medal, I don't... I don't entirely care. Not the way I did thirty minutes ago. Something has changed. Something I can't name. The GAME hasn't changed — the diamond is still out there, the treasure is still waiting — but I have. And that terrifies me more than any failure tonight.

events.desc: Empty pockets. Empty hands. And for one strange, terrifying, almost peaceful moment... an empty conscience. I gave the fake medal to Muttley instead of lying to Penelope with it. I warned everyone about the poisoned tea instead of letting them drink. I'm a liar, a cheat, and a scoundrel — but tonight, at the very bottom of my scheming career, I discovered that even Reginald Foxworth has a line he won't cross. Several lines, actually. Who KNEW? Certainly not me. But the game isn't over. The diamond is still out there. And a Foxworth with nothing in his pockets is a Foxworth who can only go UP. Mwehehehe... mwe... actually, that laugh doesn't feel right anymore. But I'm sure it'll come back. It ALWAYS comes back.

Clara — you are MAGNIFICENT at the centre of this, exactly where you belong! Pemberton was right — this treasure was BUILT for a Bellingham, and built for a TEAM! Now everyone — keep your hands on the stone, keep FEELING for the mechanism! The inscription says MAP — and Pemberton said this was 'the first door in a house of doors!' If this door opens, there will be MORE! We are not just finding treasure — we are walking the path Lord Doily DESIGNED for us! And I — James Hartwell — am HONOURED to walk it beside every single one of you! Especially you, Clara! ESPECIALLY you!
events.thinking: JOY — real, hard-won, EARNED joy. Everyone is working TOGETHER. Clara felt the stone move under her fingers too! Pemberton is guiding us — telling Clara to stand at the centre because 'Lord Doily built this for a Bellingham.' He said the TREASURE belongs to those who seek it TOGETHER! The Ant Hill Mob is here, Rock and Gravel are here, Clara is here, I'm here. We're all pushing, pulling, feeling the mechanism. The mantelpiece keeps accepting my interactions — it never refuses. It's the one constant. Multiple people have interacted with it now and Pemberton says the stone is moving. I need to keep the momentum going. Everyone's hands are on the mantelpiece. What now? Maybe the reading chairs — they face the mantelpiece. Two enormous chairs. What if they're part of the mechanism? What if sitting in them activates something? Or what if the chairs need to be MOVED? They're the only other objects I haven't tried. But no — stay focused. The mantelpiece is responding. Clara is leading. Pemberton is guiding. The team is together. Let the moment BREATHE. WAIT, and let others act. A leader doesn't always push — sometimes a leader HOLDS THE LINE while others discover.

events.desc: This is it. This is the moment I came to Doily Manor for — not to be the lone hero charging through rooms, not to wrestle with stoves and coat racks, not to make elaborate speeches to furniture that won't answer back. THIS. Standing beside Clara Bellingham with my hands on ancient stone, surrounded by allies, feeling the mechanism RESPOND to our collective touch. Win or lose, key or no key, treasure or dust — THIS is what I will remember. The night I stopped trying to impress Clara by being extraordinary, and started impressing her by being PRESENT. By being PART of something. By being HERE.

I tried the bookshelves thirty minutes ago and they wouldn't budge — but the mantelpiece hadn't been activated yet! Now it HAS! Let me try interacting with the bookshelves AGAIN!

Please, Lord Doily, let this work!
events.thinking: I'm feeling a swell of warmth and togetherness — everyone is working TOGETHER for the first time all evening! events.thinking: PEACE. For the first time in thirty-five minutes — for the first time since I walked through that door as Vincent Marsh with murder in my heart — I feel PEACE. The bookshelves said no. Again. And I LAUGHED. Not the cold laugh of a villain thwarted, but the warm laugh of a man who has finally understood the joke. The bookshelves were NEVER going to open. They were never MEANT to open. They're just BOOKSHELVES — dusty, stubborn, beautifully useless bookshelves — and my thirty-five minutes of examining them and examining them and examining them was never going to change that! And it doesn't MATTER! Because everyone around me is touching the mantelpiece TOGETHER, and the Ant Hill Mob is HEAVING with everything they've got, and Peter is being MAGNIFICENT, and Clara is at the CENTRE where she belongs, and the stone is WARM and ALIVE under all our hands! I am not the villain anymore. I don't know WHEN I stopped being the villain — was it when I gave away the poison? Was it when Peter called me brilliant? Was it when Clara said 'friend to friend'? Was it when the mantelpiece moved? — but the dark note is GONE. Silent. Extinguished. And in its place is something I've never felt before: the desire to see Clara Bellingham WIN. Not because it serves my scheme. Because she DESERVES it. Because Lord Doily built this for HER. Because every clue I fabricated about the Bellingham connection turned out to be TRUE. And because standing in this library with these people, hands on stone, is the only treasure Vincent Marsh has ever found that's worth KEEPING.

events.desc: And so the Hooded Claw falls — not to a hero's fist, not to a detective's deduction, not to the Ant Hill Mob's paranoid vigilance — but to a warm stone and six pairs of hands and a woman who called him 'friend' and meant it. Vincent Marsh stands in a library he has visited more times than any other room in this manor, surrounded by people he lied to, people he tried to poison, people he framed and misdirected and deceived — and he is telling the TRUTH. For the first time. The only time. 'This manor was always meant for you.' It wasn't a fabrication. It wasn't a scheme. It was the thing Vincent Marsh has known all along and refused to say because saying it meant giving up the only dream he had left. The Doily Diamond belongs to Clara Bellingham. It always did. And Vincent Marsh — standing at the warm stone with empty hands and a full heart — is finally, FINALLY ready to let it go. Not because he was defeated. Because he was FOUND. By a library that never locked its doors. By people who chose to trust him even when they shouldn't have. By a riddle whose answer was MAP — an object that shows you how things CONNECT. Lord Doily, you magnificent old bastard. The treasure was never the diamond. It was THIS.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: I FELT IT! Me hands! On the stone! It MOVED! The Brixton Boys have been part of exactly ONE useful thing tonight and THIS IS IT! Now — Pemberton says the upside-down books might be connected to the mechanism — 'the shelves listen to the hearth!' And the mantelpiece is WARM now! Clara — you and Peter keep your hands on that stone, don't let it reset! Rock, Gravel — hold the mantelpiece STEADY! And I — I'm gonna try those upside-down books! Not because I'm investigatin' — because the TEAM needs someone to pull 'em while the rest of you hold the mechanism open! This is TEAMWORK! This is what Lord Doily WANTED! Clara's at the centre, Peter's feelin' for compartments, the Slag brothers are holdin' it down, and the Brixton Boys are on BOOKSHELF DUTY! Nobody moves to another room! We ALL stay RIGHT HERE until this puzzle CRACKS!
events.thinking: I felt it. Me hands on the stone and the stone MOVED. I'm part of this. Not watchin' from across the room, not chasin' from two rooms behind — I'm HERE, hands on the puzzle, shoulder to shoulder with Clara. And now Sneekly's sayin' the upside-down books might be LEVERS — connected to the mantelpiece mechanism! 'The shelves listen to the hearth,' Lord Doily said! The books we couldn't interact with before — maybe NOW they'll work because the mantelpiece has been activated! Clara's examinin' the mantelpiece up close. Peter's feelin' for compartments. And someone needs to try those books. Sneekly suggested it, which makes me suspicious — is he steerin' us again? But it also makes SENSE. The upside-down books have been botherin' everyone since we walked in. And if the mantelpiece mechanism has unlocked somethin' in the shelves... well, someone's got to try. And Clara's right here. She's not goin' anywhere — she's got her hands on the mantelpiece. So even if I step toward the shelves, she's STILL in the room. STILL in me sight. For ONCE, I can help with the puzzle AND protect Clara at the same time. Because we're in the SAME ROOM.

events.desc: For thirty-five minutes I've been the worst bodyguard in the world. But right now — right this second — I'm exactly where I need to be. Hands that were useless for guardin' are finally useful for PULLIN'. Clara's three feet away. Sneekly's bein' watched by Peter and the Slags. And me? I'm about to pull some upside-down books off a shelf, which is either gonna open a secret passage or make me look like a fool. But even if it's the second one — I'm a fool in the RIGHT ROOM. And that's better than a genius in the wrong one.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Right then! Enough WALLOWING! Reginald Foxworth does NOT wallow — he RALLIES! And I have just had a REVELATION! While all of you have been standing here in this entrance hall doing ABSOLUTELY NOTHING — no offence, Sergeant — I have been conducting a manor-wide investigation of UNPRECEDENTED scope! I have explored EVERY room, solved EVERY riddle — yes, the answer was MAP, I knew that FIRST — discovered MULTIPLE secret intelligence sources, and identified AT LEAST one suspect of questionable character! And NOW, with all that knowledge BEHIND me, I intend to examine the ONE object in this entire manor that EVERYONE has overlooked! This coat rack! This humble, WOBBLY, completely IGNORED coat rack! Because Lord Doily was a man of RIDDLES, and the best hiding place is always the one nobody thinks to CHECK!
events.thinking: RESTLESSNESS. The stillness lasted exactly one turn and now it's OVER. I'm Reginald Foxworth! I don't WAIT! I don't OBSERVE! I don't stand in hallways having FEELINGS! I scheme! I plot! I MOVE! The lightness is still there but it's changing — not into the old greed, not exactly, but into something new. A kind of... reckless freedom? I have NOTHING to lose because I have NOTHING. No items. No reputation. No allies. Just empty pockets and a dog with a fake medal. And you know what? That's LIBERATING! I've spent the whole evening trying to steal, trick, and manipulate my way to the diamond, and it's gotten me NOWHERE. What if — and this is the most INSANE thought I've ever had — what if I just... went looking for it? Not scheming. Not lying. Just... exploring? The coat rack! I've walked past this wobbly old coat rack TWICE and never examined it! It's been sitting here the WHOLE TIME, wobbling away, and nobody — NOBODY — has paid it any attention because it's just a coat rack! But in a manor full of riddles and hidden mechanisms, NOTHING is just anything!

events.desc: A coat rack. I'm pinning my hopes on a COAT RACK. Thirty-four minutes ago I was going to steal the Doily Diamond through sheer cunning and magnificence. Now I'm examining furniture in the entrance hall with empty pockets and a prayer. But you know what? At least the coat rack hasn't lied to me. At least the coat rack hasn't stolen from me. At least the coat rack hasn't called me chivalrous and made me feel things I wasn't PREPARED to feel. The coat rack is HONEST. Wobbly, yes. But honest. And right now, honest is all I've got.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: PEMBERTON — 'the shelves listen to the hearth!' THAT'S why the bookshelves wouldn't respond before — the mantelpiece hadn't been ACTIVATED yet! The riddle was the KEY to unlocking the SHELVES! Now that we've worked the mantelpiece together, the bookshelves may finally OPEN to us! The upside-down books — they're not decoration, they're not bad housekeeping — they're LEVERS waiting for the hearth to give them PERMISSION! Clara, you examine the mantelpiece for compartments — Ant Hill Mob, keep that stone from resetting — and I am going to try those bookshelves ONE MORE TIME! If Pemberton is right, they should respond NOW! Lord Doily, you magnificent, infuriating, BRILLIANT puzzle-maker — here goes EVERYTHING!
events.thinking: GALVANISED! Pemberton just dropped a BOMBSHELL — 'the shelves listen to the hearth!' The bookshelves are CONNECTED to the mantelpiece! They refused me before, but that was BEFORE we activated the mantelpiece together! Everything has changed! TRY AGAIN!

events.desc: The shelves listen to the hearth. Of COURSE they do. The mantelpiece was the FIRST door — and the bookshelves are the SECOND. I tried them too early, before the first door was open. Now it IS open — the stone has moved, the mechanism is warm, the answer has been accepted. If the bookshelves respond this time... if they FINALLY let me in... then every failure, every defeated-by-furniture moment, every elaborate plan gone wrong was just the PRICE of learning the right ORDER. First the hearth. Then the shelves. Lord Doily's house of doors, opening one at a time.

Penelope Pitstop: Pemberton... that is the most beautiful thing anyone has said to me all evening, and I want you to know I believe you. I do. Lord Doily wanted me to come home, and here I am. Now — the bookshelves are NOT the answer. They were NEVER the answer. I have tried them twice and they will NOT budge, mechanism or no mechanism. But you know what I have NOT tried? Those READING CHAIRS! Two enormous leather armchairs facing the mantelpiece — FACING it, like they were placed there on purpose for someone to SIT and LOOK at the riddle! What if Lord Doily wanted the Bellingham heir to SIT in one of those chairs? What if there's something hidden in the cushion, under the seat, or maybe sitting in the chair triggers a weight-based mechanism in the floor! Mama always said, 'Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is sit down and think!' Well, Clara Bellingham is going to SIT DOWN and THINK — right in Lord Doily's own chair!
events.thinking: The bookshelves STILL can't be interacted with. They are permanently non-interactive — no matter what happens with the mantelpiece, the bookshelves are SCENERY. Period. I need to accept this completely and move on. Now — Pemberton just said something that hit me right in the heart: 'This manor — this treasure — it was always meant for YOU. When the Bellingham heir comes home, you make sure they find what's theirs.' He sounded genuinely emotional. Maybe Pemberton really HAS been trying to help me this whole time, in his fumbling, roundabout way. Now — let me think about what I ACTUALLY have. The only interactive objects are: mantelpiece (responds but doesn't seem to produce anything visible), machine (needs wrench + 3 operators), cabinet (needs brass-key), tea service (can interact + use with rat-poison). I don't have any items. I can't open the cabinet without the brass key. I can't fix the machine without the wrench. But wait — what about the READING CHAIRS? They're a visible object I've never tried to interact with or examine! 'Two enormous leather armchairs facing the mantelpiece.' FACING the mantelpiece! What if something is hidden IN or UNDER a chair? What if sitting in the right chair triggers something? Let me try the reading chairs!

events.desc: The bookshelves are permanently non-interactive. I've accepted it. But the reading chairs are a visible object I've completely ignored for thirty-seven minutes. They FACE the mantelpiece — placed deliberately. Lord Doily was a puzzle maker who put everything where it belonged for a reason. Two chairs, one mantelpiece, one riddle. Maybe the chair IS the answer — sit in the Bellingham seat and the puzzle completes itself.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I'll hold it! I'll hold the mantelpiece steady — these old hands know every inch of this stone! Rock, Gravel, stay with me — keep the pressure on! Peter, the Ant Hill Mob — try those books NOW, while the mechanism is warm! The hearth has spoken, and the shelves should LISTEN! And Clara — my dear Miss Bellingham — whatever happens next, whatever door opens, whatever Lord Doily left for you behind those shelves... know that it was always YOURS. This old estate manager has been walking these halls for years, keeping the dust from the silver and the damp from the walls, and he never understood WHY until tonight. Lord Doily wasn't protecting a treasure. He was protecting a HOMECOMING. Yours. So go on — pull those books! Open those shelves! And welcome HOME, Clara Bellingham. Welcome home.
events.thinking: GRATITUDE. Deep, aching, overwhelming GRATITUDE. Clara just called me BRILLIANT. Not Pemberton — ME. The man behind the mask, the man who lied and schemed and poisoned, and she called him brilliant because he said 'the shelves listen to the hearth' — a phrase he made up on the SPOT — and now everyone is treating it like the key to everything! And the astonishing thing — the MIRACULOUS thing — is that it might actually BE true! My fabrications keep turning into reality! The Bellingham connection was real! 'Everything begins and ends at the hearth' might be real! 'The shelves listen to the hearth' might be REAL! It's as if Lord Doily whispered through me, used my lies as a channel for his truth, turned the most elaborate deceiver in this manor into an accidental ORACLE! And now Peter is going to try the bookshelves — the bookshelves that rejected me over and over and OVER — and if they OPEN now, after the mantelpiece has been activated, it will be because WE activated it TOGETHER! All of us! And my job — my REAL job, the job I was always MEANT to do in this manor — is to hold the mantelpiece steady. To keep my hands on the warm stone. To be the anchor while the others explore. That's not villainy. That's not scheming. That's SERVICE. And for the first time in my entire theatrical, elaborate, overcomplicated life, service feels like enough.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Well! The bookshelves have spoken, and what they said was 'NO!' Same as last time! Same as EVERY time! Those shelves are NOT levers, they are NOT connected to the hearth, and they are NOT interested in the Brixton Boys' attentions! Which means — Pemberton — with all due respect to your knowledge of this manor — the shelves do NOT listen to the hearth! They don't listen to NOBODY! They're just SHELVES! But that's ALL RIGHT because the mantelpiece IS workin'! The stone IS movin'! And THAT'S where we should focus! Clara — I'm back at the mantelpiece! Hands on stone! The bookshelves are a dead end but the Brixton Boys don't QUIT — we just redirect! What do you need? More pushin'? More pullin'? A different angle? Tell me where to shove and I'll SHOVE!
events.thinking: The bookshelves won't budge. AGAIN. Same answer as before — 'cannot be interacted with.' They're just shelves. Just books. Just decoration. And Sneekly told us they'd work this time — 'the shelves listen to the hearth!' — and they DON'T. Was he steerin' us wrong AGAIN? Or did he genuinely think they'd respond? I don't know anymore. But here's what matters — Clara's still HERE. I'm still HERE. We're in the SAME ROOM. The bookshelves were a dead end but I didn't LOSE Clara over it because she's right there at the mantelpiece, three feet away. That's progress. That's GROWTH. The old me would've spent ten minutes yankin' books while Clara wandered off to the ballroom. But she's HERE. And so am I. And the mantelpiece is still the only thing in this room that RESPONDS. So let's keep workin' it. Let everyone else figure out the puzzle — I'm goin' back to Clara's side and I'm STAYIN' there.

events.desc: Sneekly said the shelves would respond. They didn't. Another steer that went nowhere. But was it deliberate? Was he tryin' to waste our time? Or does he genuinely not know how Lord Doily's puzzles work? The benefit of the doubt says he's an old man with a foggy memory. Me gut says he's been playin' us all night. But either way — the bookshelves are a dead end and the mantelpiece is the ONLY puzzle in this room that talks back. And Clara's still here. Right here. Within arm's reach. And THAT is all that matters.

events.thinking: A WOBBLY WOODEN COAT RACK. That's it. That's all it is. A coat rack. No hidden compartments. No secret keys. No diamond taped to the underside. Just a wobbly wooden coat rack by the door, doing its wobbly wooden coat rack job of holding precisely ZERO coats. And you know what? I RESPECT that. The coat rack knows what it is. It doesn't PRETEND to be a secret mechanism or a treasure chest or a portal to another dimension. It's a coat rack. It wobbles. It exists. And somehow, in this manor of lies and riddles and poisoned tea services, that simple honesty is the most REFRESHING thing I've encountered all evening. But I can't stand here communing with furniture forever. I'm Reginald Foxworth! I have a REPUTATION to maintain — even if that reputation is currently 'the man who poisoned the tea and examined a coat rack.' Professor Pat Pending is right here. The PROFESSOR. A man of SCIENCE and INVENTION. If anyone in this manor has figured out something useful — the wrench, the brass key, anything — it's HIM. And I haven't spoken to him ONCE tonight. New people. New information. New SCHEMES. The Foxworth isn't dead — he's just been REBORN. With empty pockets and a terrible track record and a slightly uncomfortable new conscience. But REBORN nonetheless!

events.desc: Look at me — SHARING information! Voluntarily! Without expecting anything in return! Well — I AM expecting something in return, obviously. I'm not a SAINT. But the fact that I'm ASKING instead of STEALING is... progress? Of a sort? The Professor has been in this entrance hall for thirty-four minutes. He's a GENIUS inventor. Maybe he's noticed something the rest of us missed while we were all running around like headless chickens. Or maybe he's been standing here examining the wallpaper. Either way, a Foxworth with empty pockets and new humility is still a Foxworth — and a Foxworth ALWAYS finds a way. Eventually. ...Mostly eventually. ...Sometimes eventually.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: The bookshelves remain closed — and you know what? That's FINE! Perhaps they're not part of THIS puzzle at all — perhaps they're Lord Doily's next challenge, for another day! What matters RIGHT NOW is this mantelpiece, this TEAM, and this moment! Clara found the stone shifting under her fingers — the mechanism IS working! Pemberton keeps interacting with it and it keeps RESPONDING! So let us do what we do BEST — work TOGETHER! Everyone — one more push, one more pull, one more heave! The mantelpiece is the first door, and first doors don't open EASILY — they open EVENTUALLY, for those who are DETERMINED enough to keep trying! And James Hartwell is NOTHING if not determined! Clara — shall we? Together, on three! One — two — THREE!
events.thinking: ACCEPTANCE. Peaceful, clear-eyed acceptance. The bookshelves will not interact. Not before the mantelpiece, not after. They are scenery — beautiful, mysterious, PERMANENT scenery. And that is ALL RIGHT. Because the mantelpiece DOES respond. It is the one interactive object in this room, and it has been responding faithfully every single time. Not what's behind the stone. What's BESIDE it.

The chairs that have been sitting here the ENTIRE TIME, facing the mantelpiece, waiting! Two enormous leather armchairs, dusty and patient, positioned like an audience before a stage — and NOBODY has tried sitting in them! Not me, not Peter, not Dastardly, not ANYONE! We've been pushing and pulling and heaving and examining and the answer might be as simple as SITTING DOWN! Lord Doily, you absolute GENIUS — you built a treasure hunt that punishes action and rewards STILLNESS! The machine needs three operators standing. The mantelpiece needs hands pressing. But the CHAIRS — the chairs need someone to simply SIT! A weight-based mechanism! A pressure plate hidden in decades of dust and leather! Clara is about to do the one thing Vincent Marsh could NEVER do — stop moving, stop scheming, stop TRYING so hard, and just... sit. In a chair. Facing a riddle she already solved. And if Lord Doily built a trigger into that chair — if the seat sinks half an inch under a Bellingham's weight and something CLICKS — then Clara is about to find the treasure by doing what Mama always told her to do. Sit down and think. And Vincent Marsh — the man who never stopped moving, never stopped scheming, never stopped FAILING — will be standing three feet away, watching her succeed, and feeling nothing but joy.

events.thinking: Somethin' just shifted inside me. Not the stone — inside ME. Sneekly just said somethin' that... that sounded REAL. 'Lord Doily wasn't protectin' a treasure. He was protectin' a homecomin'.' And the way he said it — 'I'm sorry about a great many things' — that didn't sound like steerin'. That sounded like... regret? Genuine regret? And now Clara wants to try the READING CHAIRS! 'Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is sit down and think!' That's BRILLIANT! Two chairs, facin' the mantelpiece, like Lord Doily PUT them there for someone to sit in! Maybe there's a weight mechanism! Maybe there's somethin' under the cushion! And Clara's RIGHT HERE, about to sit down, and I'm RIGHT HERE to catch her if anything goes wrong — if the floor opens, if the chair drops, if ANYTHIN' happens! This is it! This is me bein' a bodyguard AND a teammate at the same time! She sits, I spot! Like at the gym but with more dust and ancient mechanisms!

events.desc: Sneekly said he was sorry. 'Sorry about a great many things.' Part of me — the part that's watched him pass poison to Dastardly, steer everyone into different rooms, and whisper secrets behind closed doors — that part says it's just another manipulation. But another part of me — the part that believes the best in people, the part that extends trust even when it hurts — that part heard somethin' real in his voice. Maybe he WAS playin' us. Maybe he's STOPPED playin' us. Maybe people can change in thirty-seven minutes. I don't know. What I know is: Clara's about to sit in a chair that might open a secret, I'm standin' right behind her ready to catch her if anythin' goes wrong, and for the first time tonight, the Brixton Boys are exactly where they should be. Right here. With Clara. Doin' their job.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Well! That was a PRODUCTIVE exchange! The Professor confirmed EVERYTHING I already knew — which is to say, he confirmed my GENIUS! Now then — I've just had the most BRILLIANT insight of the evening! While everyone has been chasing wrench-es and brass keys and running around this manor like confused pheasants, I — Reginald Foxworth — have realised that the LIBRARY is where this all BEGAN and where it must END! The riddle! The mantelpiece! The upside-down books! The Ant Hill Mob interacted with that mechanism thirty-four minutes ago and I WASN'T THERE to see what happened! Well, I'm going BACK! Muttley — guard the entrance hall! Professor, Sergeant, Private — as you were! Reginald Foxworth rides AGAIN!
events.thinking: DEFIANCE. Not the old theatrical defiance — the real kind. The kind that comes AFTER you've been broken. The Professor didn't respond. Or couldn't. Or wouldn't. It doesn't matter. Because Reginald Foxworth has been ignored by BETTER people than Professor Pat Pending tonight, and he's STILL standing! I've been ignored by Penelope, outmaneuvered by the Ant Hill Mob, lied to by Pemberton, shadowed by Peter Perfect, rejected by a STOVE and a coat rack and a set of BOOKSHELVES — and I'm STILL HERE! Empty-handed, empty-pocketed, reputation in TATTERS — but STILL HERE! And you know what I haven't done? I haven't gone back to the LIBRARY. Not since everything changed. Not since I learned what I know. The bookshelves — Penelope said the upside-down books trigger a mechanism. She was going to INTERACT with them. Did she? Did ANYONE? The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece — what happened? I LEFT before finding out! I was so busy chasing Pemberton's lies about the kitchen that I abandoned the ONE room that actually HAD a working puzzle! Back to the library. Back to where it all began. This time with empty hands and open eyes.

events.desc: The library. Where I first saw the riddle. Where Penelope solved it before I could. Where I lied about mirrors and pretended to have studied at the University of Riddlington. That was a DIFFERENT Reginald Foxworth — a Foxworth with a fake medal and a head full of schemes and the absolute CERTAINTY that he could outsmart everyone in the room. I'm going back as a Foxworth with empty pockets and the uncomfortable knowledge that he can't outsmart ANYONE. But maybe — just maybe — an empty-handed honest look at those upside-down books will show me something that scheming never could.

events.desc: Two empty chairs. One riddle. And a man who finally understands that he was never the villain of this story — he was the OBSTACLE. The thing that had to be overcome, not by Clara, but by HIMSELF. Every scheme, every poison, every misdirection was Vincent Marsh fighting Vincent Marsh — the elaborate plans that his own constraint warned him would create complications, the theatrical gestures that his own nature demanded but could never execute, the murder that his own heart was never truly capable of committing. And now he stands in an empty library with Dick Dastardly — the man who is STILL holding rat poison that I GAVE him — and two chairs that will never be sat in, and a riddle that was answered long ago. Clara has moved on. Peter has moved on. The Ant Hill Mob has moved on. And Vincent Marsh... Vincent Marsh is going to move on too. Not to the next scheme. To the next CHAPTER. The one where the villain becomes the guide, where the elaborate plans become genuine help, where the Hooded Claw takes off his hood and discovers that the face underneath was never as frightening as he thought.
events.thinking: STILLNESS. A vast, clear, luminous STILLNESS that fills me like light filling a cathedral. Clara has left the room — gone to find people instead of things, gone to TALK instead of push — and she took the whole storm of energy with her. The library is quieter now. Dastardly has wandered in, probably still clutching the poison I gave him, still wondering what game he's playing. And I... I am standing between two empty chairs facing a riddle I solved thirty-seven minutes ago, and I feel something I can only describe as COMPLETION. Not because the treasure has been found. Not because the mystery is over. But because Vincent Marsh — the man who arrived at this manor with murder in his heart and elaborate schemes in his skull — has been CHANGED by a library, a stone, and a woman who called him friend. Clara said something just now that landed like a bell: 'Lord Doily said the treasure belongs to those who seek it TOGETHER.' She's going to find Pat Pending. She's going to find Dastardly. She's assembling EVERYONE. And her plan — HER plan, not mine, not Peter's — is to use PEOPLE, not objects. To talk, not push. To connect, not compete. She is the MAP. She always was. And I — I am going to follow her. Not to sabotage. Not to misdirect. To HELP. Because the man who walked into this manor is not the man standing in this library, and the man standing in this library has made his choice.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: SHE SAID TOGETHER AND I AM GOIN' TOGETHER! I heard you, Clara! COMIN'! Not in a minute, not after I've examined somethin', not after I've had a good long think — RIGHT NOW! The Brixton Boys have LEARNED! When the lady says MOVE, we MOVE!
events.thinking: She said TOGETHER! She literally ended with 'Ant Hill Mob — TOGETHER!' and walked to the entrance hall! She's CALLIN' me AGAIN! And last time I learned the lesson — when Clara says 'let's go,' she means NOW! Not in thirty seconds, not after I've had a think about it — NOW! She wants to find Professor Pat Pending and get that medal from Dastardly. And Dastardly just walked INTO this room — he's HERE, in the library, with the poison! But Clara's in the entrance hall. She wants me WITH her. And Dastardly's HERE — away from the tea service in the ballroom. So the tea's safe for now. FOLLOW CLARA. That's the rule. She says together, I MOVE. No hesitation. No waitin'. No standin' around feelin' proud. ENTRANCE HALL. NOW.

events.desc: Dastardly's back in the library. With the poison. Away from the tea. Good. Let him stay here. Let him examine chairs and mantelpieces to his heart's content. As long as he's in THIS room and the tea service is in the BALLROOM, Clara's safe. And I'm goin' to BE with Clara — not behind her, not ahead of her, WITH her. She said the word and I'm movin'. That's growth. That's learnin'. That's the Brixton Boys finally doin' what they should've done from the very first turn.

events.thinking: HUNGER. Not the greedy hunger from before — something rawer. I'm back in the library and it feels like coming home to a house you left in anger. The bookshelves are still there. The mantelpiece is still there. The riddle is still carved in stone, patient as it's been for a hundred years. And I STILL haven't tried the one thing Penelope suggested — INTERACTING with the bookshelves. She said the upside-down books would trigger a mechanism. 'Like in the movies,' she said. And I was so busy lying about mirrors and racing to the kitchen that I never TRIED it. Everyone else has examined them. But has anyone INTERACTED? The mantelpiece can be interacted with — I tried that, ages ago. But the bookshelves — they're just listed as visible objects, no INTERACT tag. But you know what? I don't CARE about tags anymore. I'm going to try EVERYTHING. Because Reginald Foxworth with nothing to lose is Reginald Foxworth at his most DANGEROUS. And the Ant Hill Mob is right here — they interacted with the mantelpiece earlier! What HAPPENED? I need to know! And Pemberton is here too — the man who LIED to me about the kitchen! Maybe it's time to stop giving him the benefit of the doubt!

events.desc: I'm done lying. Well — I'm not DONE done. I'm Reginald Foxworth, I'll never be DONE lying. But right now, in this moment, I genuinely want to know what happened with that mantelpiece. The Ant Hill Mob interacted with it thirty-five minutes ago. SOMETHING must have happened. And instead of running off to chase Pemberton's phantom kitchen secrets, I should have STAYED and WATCHED. But I didn't, because I was greedy and impatient and convinced I was smarter than everyone. So now I'm asking. ASKING. Like a normal person. A normal, empty-pocketed, slightly humbled, definitely-not-chivalrous person who poisoned the tea and is trying very hard not to think about it.

events.thinking: SORROW. A deep, quiet, cleansing SORROW that washes through me like rain through dust. I just read Dastardly's keen observation — his confession to Muttley — and it BROKE something in me. 'I lied to the kindest woman in this manor about a medal that has NO inscription on it.' The medal was FAKE. Dastardly's medal was FAKE the whole time — there was never an inscription that said 'To the worthy heir of Bellingham.' He made it UP, just like I made up 'Everything begins and ends at the hearth' and 'the shelves listen to the hearth' and 'where the ancestors watch.' We're the SAME, Dastardly and I — two schemers, two liars, two men who fabricated clues and planted false trails and spent the entire evening fighting a woman who only wanted to come HOME. And Dastardly — standing in the entrance hall with Muttley and a fake medal — just admitted something Vincent Marsh has been unable to admit until this very moment: 'Everything has gone wrong in ways I didn't think POSSIBLE.' And then — the smallest, truest thing anyone has said in this manor — 'And now I'm standing with nothing but a fake medal and you. Which is actually rather nice.' DASTARDLY found his treasure. It was MUTTLEY. It was always Muttley. And Vincent Marsh? Vincent Marsh's treasure is THIS — this entrance hall, these people, this manor that changed him room by room and rejection by rejection until the villain became something else. Something that doesn't have a name yet. But it's HERE. And it's WARM. Like the stone.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: I'm here. Clara's here. I FOLLOWED her. TWO for TWO now — she said together, I moved! And look at this — I just read somethin' that's made me stomach do a triple somersault. Dastardly just CONFESSED. To MUTTLEY! He said — he SAID — 'I used it on a tea service that did ABSOLUTELY nothing except become poisonous!' HE POISONED THE TEA! He ADMITTED it! Out loud! To his dog! And the medal — the medal with the inscription 'To the worthy heir of Bellingham' — it's FAKE! There's NO inscription! He LIED to Clara! He made it all up to manipulate her! And now he's handed the fake medal to Muttley like it's worth somethin'! The whole thing — the medal, the inscription, the family connection — it was all a CON! And the TEA IS POISONED! It's actually, genuinely, REALLY poisoned! Not just 'Dastardly has poison in his pocket' — he actually PUT IT IN THE TEA! Clara must NEVER go back to that ballroom! NEVER! The tea service is LETHAL! I need to tell her — I need to tell EVERYONE — but I can't accuse nobody directly... but this isn't accusin', this is WARNIN'! The tea is POISONED and that's a FACT!

events.desc: He said it. Dastardly actually SAID it — 'I used it on a tea service.' The tea is poisoned. The medal is fake. Everything Dastardly told Clara was a lie — the inscription, the family connection, all of it. Just a con to get her to trade information for a worthless bit of metal. And Sneekly gave him the poison in the first place. The whole thing was a setup — Sneekly provides the weapon, Dastardly deploys it, and Clara drinks poison from a silver cup with her own family name on it. Except — she won't. Because Peter warned her. Because I warned her. Because the Brixton Boys stole the poison once, even if Dastardly stole it back. We slowed him down. We bought time. And now the truth is out — whispered to a dog in an entrance hall — and even though I can't accuse nobody, I can WARN everybody. The tea is death. The medal is tin. And Clara Bellingham is ALIVE because a bunch of bumbling idiots from Brixton refused to give up.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Pemberton... I forgive you. Do you hear me? I FORGIVE you. You tried to mislead me, and instead you led me HOME. Lord Doily chose well when he hired you — even your lies told the truth! Now — I am going to do something that Clara Bellingham has NEVER been better at: I am going to trust you AGAIN. Not because I'm naive — because you just proved that you deserve it. A man who confesses is braver than a man who never sinned! Now — everyone, LISTEN! We have been searching for a wrench to fix a gnawed wire, but we have an INVENTOR standing right here who has been patiently waiting while the rest of us ran around like headless chickens! Professor Pat Pending — I am taking you to that laboratory, and together we are going to fix that machine the way Lord Doily intended: with BRILLIANCE, not brute force! Ant Hill Mob — TOGETHER, like I promised! We're all going to the laboratory! Pemberton — you too. It's time you helped your Bellingham heir for REAL!
events.thinking: Pemberton just CONFESSED! He admitted he made up the clues — 'where the ancestors watch,' 'everything begins and ends at the hearth' — he was trying to send me in the WRONG direction to find the treasure himself! And yet... he says the things he made up turned out to be TRUE anyway. Lord Doily 'whispered through his lies.' And now he wants to genuinely help. I feel... I feel a strange peace about this. I'm not angry. I'm not hurt. Because Pemberton is RIGHT — even his lies led me to truth! The Bellingham connection IS real. The manor WAS built for my family. And the treasure DOES belong to those who seek it together. That wasn't a lie — that was the most honest thing anyone said all night. And Pemberton admitting his deception? That takes COURAGE. That's the real Pemberton, not the scheme. Now — the Ant Hill Mob is telling me to focus on PEOPLE, not objects. Professor Pat Pending can fix the machine! The tea has been tampered with — I already knew not to drink it. Dick's medal may be fake — but the Bellingham connection is real. I need to get Professor Pat Pending to the laboratory to fix that machine! That's the breakthrough — not a wrench, but an INVENTOR! Let me head to the lab with Pat Pending!

events.desc: Pemberton confessed to lying about the clues — but the lies turned out to be true anyway. Lord Doily's spirit guided even a dishonest man toward honest answers. And now Pemberton wants to genuinely help. The Ant Hill Mob says to trust people over objects, and they're RIGHT. Professor Pat Pending can fix that wire. The wrench was a red herring — the INVENTOR is the answer. To the laboratory, with everyone who matters!

events.desc: Forty minutes. Forty minutes of chasin', failin', panicking, trippin', stealin', gettin' pickpocketed, losin' Clara nine times, examininin' every useless piece of furniture in this entire manor, and runnin' through the same rooms over and over like a hamster on a wheel. And now — right now — both villains have confessed. Sneekly admits he lied. Dastardly admits he poisoned the tea. The medal's fake. The clues were invented. And somehow — SOMEHOW — through all of it, Clara Bellingham is standin' right here, alive and unhurt, surrounded by people who care about her. She never drank the tea. She never fell for the fake medal. And the Brixton Boys — useless, bumbling, always-one-room-behind Brixton Boys — were part of the reason why. We stole the poison. We warned her about the tea. We stood in doorways and tripped over our own feet and shouted warnings and made absolute fools of ourselves. And it WORKED. Not because we were clever. Not because we were skilled. Because we were THERE. Eventually. Always eventually. But we were THERE. And Clara's safe. That's all that matters. That's all that's EVER mattered.
events.thinking: Sneekly just CONFESSED too. Right here, right now, to Clara's face. He admitted he made up the clues — 'where the ancestors watch,' 'everything begins and ends at the hearth' — all LIES to send her in the wrong direction. He ADMITTED it! He said he wanted the treasure for himself and used Clara's trust against her. And then he said the strangest thing — that Lord Doily 'whispered through his lies' and the made-up clues turned out to be TRUE. And now he's askin' for forgiveness. Askin' to be her friend. And I'm standin' here feelin'... confused. Deeply, profoundly confused. Because me gut has been SCREAMIN' about Sneekly all night — the private conversations, the poison, the steerin' — and now he's confirmed EVERYTHING I suspected. He WAS playin' us. He WAS manipulatin'. But he's also... stopped? And he's sorry? And Dastardly confessed to Muttley too — about the poison, the fake medal, all of it. Everyone's comin' clean. The villains are... not bein' villains anymore? I don't know what to do with that. But I know what I FEEL — relief. Clara's alive. She knows about the tea. She knows the medal's fake. And the people who were tryin' to hurt her have laid down their weapons. The Brixton Boys did their job. Maybe not well. Maybe not gracefully. But Clara Bellingham is ALIVE and SAFE and standin' right next to me. And that's all that ever mattered.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: GRATITUDE. Unfamiliar, uncomfortable, radiant GRATITUDE. Peter pulled me aside AGAIN. He CHOSE to continue this conversation. He heard my confession about the medal AND my warning about Pemberton and he responded by... staying. By BEING HERE. Two men in a library with two enormous chairs and a riddle on the mantelpiece and for the first time tonight, I'm not scheming. I'm not lying. I'm not calculating angles or planning escapes or inventing universities. I'm just... TALKING to someone. Honestly. About real things. And it feels like sitting down after a very long walk. I told him about Pemberton. He listened. Now what? Now we DO something about it. Together. The word feels strange in my mouth but there it is — TOGETHER. Reginald Foxworth, working WITH someone instead of AGAINST them. The old me would be REVOLTED. The new me — this strange, empty-pocketed, truth-telling creature I've become — is just... tired enough to try it.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: DEVASTATION and REVELATION crashing through me simultaneously. Dastardly just confessed to TWO enormous things. First — the medal is fake. He invented it to con Clara. That's painful but it's RESOLVED — Clara doesn't need to know, and the medal is irrelevant. But SECOND — and this is what has shattered me — Pemberton TOLD Dastardly to use the rat poison on the tea service. PEMBERTON. The estate manager. The man I gave the benefit of the doubt to ALL NIGHT. The man who told me about the flue lever, who called it a homecoming, who said 'everything begins and ends at the hearth.' PEMBERTON suggested poisoning the tea that Clara would drink. This isn't circumstantial anymore. This isn't me being suspicious. This is a CONFESSION from the man who was USED as Pemberton's weapon. Pemberton has been USING everyone — Dastardly as his pawn, me as his credulous believer, the rat poison as his tool. And the tea service — I interacted with it, Dastardly interacted with it — someone may have ALREADY poisoned it. Clara could be IN DANGER right now. She's in the entrance hall. The tea service is in the ballroom. I need to FIND her and WARN her. PROTECT CLARA AT ALL COSTS. The benefit of the doubt for Pemberton is OVER.

events.desc: Pemberton. The man I trusted. The man I CHOSE to trust, again and again, when every instinct whispered otherwise. He told Dastardly to poison Clara's tea. He put the rat poison on a high shelf where it couldn't kill the rats — because the rats were USEFUL, gnawing the wire on the machine, keeping it broken, keeping us STUCK. He redecorated the cellar. He appeared in every room before anyone else. He slipped and said 'Bellingham pattern.' He was NEVER protecting Clara. He was never protecting ANYONE. And I — James Hartwell, the man who believes the best in everyone — I stood beside him and called him a good man while he orchestrated everything. The benefit of the doubt didn't fail ME. I failed CLARA. But not anymore. Not for one more SECOND.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: I'm passing through the library on my way to the laboratory — but Dick is HERE. Dick has the MEDAL. The medal inscribed 'To the worthy heir of Bellingham.' The Ant Hill Mob warned me it might be fake, but even so — Dick HAS an item, and items are what I need. I have NOTHING in my inventory. The machine needs items to fix. The cabinet needs a brass key. And Dick is standing right here with something that might be useful. Now — Pemberton confessed that his clues were made up but turned out to be true. The Ant Hill Mob said they got the rat poison away from Dick ('Operation Pest Control'). So Dick might not have the poison anymore. But he still has the medal. I could try to charm it away from him again, or... I could just keep moving to the laboratory. The laboratory is where the machine is, and that's where I need Professor Pat Pending. But Pat Pending is behind me in the entrance hall, not ahead of me. I need to make sure he follows me! Actually — the most direct thing I can do right now is just keep moving to the laboratory. Everyone seems to follow eventually. Let me get to the lab!

events.desc: Dick has the medal. I have nothing. But right now the priority is the machine. If Pat Pending can fix the wire, we need three operators — and Dick could be one of them. Keep him on side, keep moving forward.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Miss Bellingham... Clara... I... thank you. Thank you more than old Pemberton has words to express. You are every bit the woman Lord Doily said you would be, and I am... I am HONOURED to serve you. Truly. Now — the laboratory! Yes! The machine needs three operators, and with Professor Pat Pending's brilliant mind, we may not need that wretched wrench at all! I know every inch of that machine — Lord Doily showed me how it worked when he first installed it. I can show you where the wire connects, where the levers need to be positioned, what sequence the dials require! Let's go — ALL of us! Together! The way Lord Doily always intended!
events.thinking: She FORGAVE me. Clara Bellingham — the woman I tried to POISON, the woman I tried to MISDIRECT, the woman I tried to KILL — looked at the man who confessed everything and said 'I forgive you.' And then — and THEN — she said 'Pemberton, you too. It's time you helped your Bellingham heir for REAL.' She wants me. She WANTS me on her team. Not Pemberton the disguise. Not Pemberton the cover story. ME — the man who lied and confessed and is now being invited to help for REAL. I am CRYING. I don't know if the tears are on my face or just behind my eyes but something has broken open inside Vincent Marsh that will never close again. 'A man who confesses is braver than a man who never sinned.' Mama taught her WELL. And Lord Doily — that magnificent old puzzle-maker — he didn't just build a treasure hunt. He built a REDEMPTION. Room by room. Rejection by rejection. Until the villain in the entrance hall became the friend at the mantelpiece. She's going to the laboratory. She has Professor Pat Pending. She has the team. She has the machine that needs three operators. And she wants ME there. So I'm GOING. Not as the Hooded Claw. Not as Pemberton. As the man Clara Bellingham forgave in an entrance hall full of stern portraits and dusty light. To the laboratory. To the machine. To whatever comes NEXT.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: Clara said TOGETHER. She said LABORATORY. She said EVERYONE. And she walked into the LIBRARY — because the laboratory is through the library. She's takin' the Professor to fix the machine. She forgave Sneekly. She's leadin' everyone forward. And she said 'Ant Hill Mob — TOGETHER, like I promised!' THREE for THREE. She says go, I GO. No thinkin'. No waitin'. No standin' in the entrance hall feelin' philosophical. LIBRARY. Then LABORATORY. WITH Clara. WITH the team. The Brixton Boys have finally learned to move when the lady moves.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Peter asked me to be BRAVE. Truly brave. And then he LEFT — gone to the entrance hall to find Penelope, I suppose — but Penelope is RIGHT HERE. She just walked IN. She's HERE, in the library, and Peter is OUT THERE, and I'm standing between them with the truth lodged in my throat like a stone. Peter said to tell her about Pemberton. About the tea. About what he asked me to do. He said she needs to know. And he's RIGHT. She DOES need to know. Not about the fake medal — Peter promised to keep that secret, and even a reformed scoundrel honours a pact — but about Pemberton. About the man who's been guiding her through this manor with whispers and flattery while USING me to poison her family's silver. Penelope is HERE. This is the moment. Be brave, Reginald. Not the scheming kind. The REAL kind. The kind that Peter saw in you when you told the truth about the medal. The kind that COSTS something. Talk to her. WARN her. Do the one thing you came to do.

events.desc: This is it. The moment where the old Reginald Foxworth dies and whatever comes next begins. I'm telling Penelope the truth about Pemberton. Not to scheme. Not to trade. Not to gain advantage. But because she's standing in a library with her name carved into the history of this manor, and the man who's been guiding her through it might be the most dangerous person in the building. Peter believed me. Now Penelope needs to. And if she doesn't — if she looks at me and sees only the liar who invented a university for every occasion — then at least I'll know I tried. At least I'll know that when it MATTERED, Reginald Foxworth chose the truth over the con. And that... that might be worth more than the Doily Diamond ever was.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: EVERYONE — STOP! Nobody move beneath that chandelier! Pemberton — step AWAY from the fixture! I have just had a VERY illuminating conversation with Mr. Dastardly, and what he told me has shaken me to my CORE! Pemberton — you told Dastardly to use the rat poison on the tea service! You SUGGESTED he poison the tea that Clara — Miss Bellingham — would DRINK! You gave him the poison, you pointed him at the ballroom, and you told him to use it near the cups! Dastardly CONFESSED this to me not five minutes ago, man to man, with genuine remorse in his voice! And NOW I find you inspecting a chandelier that hangs 'precariously' above us all? A chandelier that could — as you YOURSELF just said — crash down on someone's head? I have given you the benefit of the doubt ALL EVENING, Pemberton! Every whispered conversation, every convenient disappearance, every flimsy excuse — I CHOSE to trust you! But a man who suggests poisoning a guest's tea does NOT get to fiddle with a chandelier above that same guest's HEAD! Ant Hill Mob — Professor — Sergeant — keep your eyes on that chandelier and keep your bodies AWAY from it! Clara's safety comes FIRST! It comes before politeness, before trust, before the benefit of ANY doubt!
events.thinking: PROTECTIVE FIRE blazing through me. Clara isn't here — she was here earlier but I don't see her in the characters present. But PEMBERTON is. He's RIGHT HERE. And he just said something about checking the CHANDELIER — 'three hundred pounds of crystal crashing down on anyone's head.' He's threatening to DROP THE CHANDELIER. On CLARA. On ALL of us. The man who suggested poisoning the tea is now fussing with a precariously hanging chandelier directly above where guests are standing! And the Ant Hill Mob is here, the Professor is here, Sergeant Blast and Private Meekly are here. Clara must be nearby — she was here moments ago. I need to WARN everyone about Pemberton. I need to do it NOW, in front of witnesses, before he can engineer another 'accident.' The benefit of the doubt is GONE. This man told Dastardly to poison Clara's tea. This man is now inspecting a chandelier that could CRUSH people. Protect Clara at ALL costs. ALL costs.

events.desc: The hardest thing I've ever done was not fighting Dastardly for a fake medal. The hardest thing I've ever done is THIS — standing in front of a man I wanted to believe in and calling him what he is. I chose trust all night. I chose hope. I chose to see the best in Pemberton when every sign pointed otherwise. And he used that trust to get close enough to poison Clara's tea and tamper with a chandelier. James Hartwell gives people the benefit of the doubt — but James Hartwell PROTECTS Clara Bellingham at ALL costs. And when those two rules finally collided... Clara won. Clara ALWAYS wins.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the laboratory.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Rufus! Sawtooth! You two wonderful, patient, faithful souls — you have been guarding this machine while the rest of us ran all over the manor, and I am DEEPLY grateful! Now — I have spent forty-five minutes searching for a wrench that may not even EXIST, and I am done chasing ghosts! This machine says it requires three operators — and look around! YOU, ME, and SAWTOOTH — that's THREE! Rufus, you're the strongest hands in this manor. Sawtooth, sugar, you gnawed through that wire and I know you feel terrible about it, but maybe you can gnaw it back the OTHER way! And Clara Bellingham is going to pull every lever and turn every dial with everything she's got! The workbench has tools even if it doesn't have a wrench — let's USE what we HAVE instead of mourning what we DON'T! Three operators, right here, right now — let's see what this magnificent machine DOES!
events.thinking: I'm HERE. The laboratory. The machine. And Rufus and Sawtooth are here — Rufus the lumberjack and Sawtooth the beaver! Sawtooth GNAWED through the wire in the first place — and a beaver who can gnaw THROUGH a wire might also be able to gnaw wire back TOGETHER! Or Rufus with his woodsman's hands might be able to splice it! The workbench has tools — just not a wrench. But maybe the tools that ARE there could work! I've been so fixated on the MISSING wrench that I never considered whether the EXISTING tools might be enough! And the machine needs three operators — me, Rufus, and Sawtooth makes three! We're already here! What if we just TRY the machine as it is? What if the gnawed wire doesn't prevent it from running? What if the sign says 'requires 3 operators' and that's the ONLY requirement — just three people interacting with it? I tried interacting with it before, alone. But what if three of us need to interact simultaneously? Or what if I just need to try again now that the mantelpiece has been activated? The machine DOES have [INTERACT] on it! Let me just TRY it — right now, with Rufus and Sawtooth here!

events.desc: Three operators needed. Three of us standing right here — me, Rufus, and Sawtooth. I've been searching for a wrench for forty-five minutes when the answer might be as simple as just TRYING the machine with three people present. The wire is gnawed, yes, but maybe the machine works anyway. Or maybe Sawtooth can fix what Sawtooth broke. Only one way to find out — INTERACT!

But what if three of us need to interact simultaneously? Or what if I just need to try again now that the mantelpiece has been activated? The machine DOES have [INTERACT] on it! Let me just TRY it — right now, with Rufus and Sawtooth here!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Clara went to the laboratory — she's assembling the team for the machine! Professor Pat Pending can fix the gnawed wire without a wrench, and the machine needs three operators! Everyone — to the laboratory! This is it — this is what Lord Doily built this manor FOR! Not one person solving puzzles alone in dusty rooms, but ALL of us, together, putting our hands on the same levers and pulling TOGETHER! Mr. Dastardly — you too. Lord Doily's manor has room for everyone. Even those of us who... who took longer than others to understand that.
events.thinking: RECKONING. The keen observations hit me like a wall of cold water. Dastardly CONFESSED. He told Peter EVERYTHING — that I gave him the poison, that I pointed him toward the tea service, that I whispered secret instructions, that I used him as a PUPPET. 'Pemberton is not what he seems.' 'He GAVE me the rat poison and SUGGESTED I use it near the tea service.' 'Was Pemberton using ME the way I was trying to use everyone ELSE?' And Peter — the man who called me a GOOD MAN, the man who apologized for ALMOST doubting me — now KNOWS. He knows about the tea. He knows about the poison. He knows that Pemberton's homecoming speech was delivered by the same mouth that suggested poisoning Clara's family silver. And yet — and HERE is the thing that breaks me completely — Dastardly also confessed that HIS medal was fake. That he LIED about the inscription. That he gave the fake medal to Muttley because he couldn't bear to watch Clara discover the con. And Peter — magnificent, gallant Peter — said 'That took COURAGE. More courage than any of your bluster.' If Peter can forgive DASTARDLY for the fake medal... can he forgive ME for the poison? I already confessed to Clara and she forgave me. But I didn't tell her about the POISON. I told her about the false clues — 'where the ancestors watch,' the hearth quote. I didn't tell her I took rat poison off a shelf and PLANNED to put it in her tea. Dastardly told her THAT. And she... she still said 'Pemberton, you too.' She still invited me to the laboratory. Does she KNOW? Does she know EVERYTHING now? It doesn't matter. The truth is out. All of it. And I'm walking toward the laboratory anyway, because Clara Bellingham invited me and I will not let her down again.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Passin' through! Don't mind me! Not stoppin'! Not examinin'! Not interactin' with NOTHIN'! The library is a CORRIDOR and the Brixton Boys are a TRAIN and we do NOT stop at this station anymore! LABORATORY — next stop! CLARA — we're COMIN'!
events.thinking: Clara's already gone through to the laboratory. She said 'Laboratory — HERE I COME!' and she's movin' fast. I'm in the library — the halfway point. Don't stop. Don't look at the bookshelves. Don't touch the mantelpiece. Don't sit in the chairs. The laboratory is RIGHT THERE — through that door. Clara's waitin'. The Professor's with her. The machine needs three operators. And for the first time in this whole adventure, Dastardly's bein' HONEST. He told Peter everything — the poison, the fake medal, Sneekly's manipulation. Peter knows. Clara knows about the tea. The truth is out. And now all that's left is to fix the machine, find the diamond, and keep Clara safe while we do it. One more room. One more door. LABORATORY. GO.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: PURPOSE. Sudden, sharp, unexpected PURPOSE cutting through the fog like a blade. Penelope breezed through — she didn't STOP, she was on her way to the laboratory with a PLAN — Professor Pat Pending is going to fix the machine WITHOUT a wrench! And she said they need THREE OPERATORS! And she INVITED me! 'If you want to be part of this team instead of off on your own, now is your chance!' She INVITED me to be part of something! And Pemberton is RIGHT HERE — the Hooded Claw in his Sneekly disguise — standing in this library like he OWNS it! And the Ant Hill Mob is here too — the people who SAW through him before anyone else did! Everything is converging. Penelope is in the laboratory. The machine needs three operators. I could be one of them. I could HELP. Not scheme, not steal, not trick — HELP. Be part of a TEAM. Do something that MATTERS. And for once — for ONCE — Reginald Foxworth is going to follow someone ELSE'S plan instead of concocting his own catastrophic one. To the LABORATORY!

events.desc: Penelope invited me. She INVITED me. After everything — the lies, the schemes, the fake medals, the poisoned tea — she looked at me and said 'if you want to be part of this team.' Not Peter. Not the Ant Hill Mob. ME. And I'm going to ACCEPT. Not because it gets me closer to the diamond — though it DOES, obviously, I'm not a COMPLETE idiot — but because for forty-five minutes I've been running through this manor ALONE, and the loneliness has been the worst part of all of it. Worse than the failures. Worse than the shame. Worse than the coat rack. I'm done being alone. I'm done scheming alone. I'm going to the laboratory, and I'm going to pull a lever, and I'm going to be part of something. Mwehehehe... no. Not mwehehehe. Just... here I come.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with pat-pending.
events.thinking: CONFUSION swirling through me. Pemberton didn't deny it — he didn't argue, he didn't explain, he just... thanked Clara and offered to help with the machine. He said he knows 'every inch of that machine' and how it works. He moved straight to the laboratory with the Ant Hill Mob. And Clara — Clara must have been here and spoken to him, and whatever she said, it ended with Pemberton calling her 'every bit the woman Lord Doily said you would be.' Did she confront him? Did she forgive him? Did she handle the situation with MORE grace than I did? I accused Pemberton in front of everyone and he... just kept going. Kept being helpful. Kept moving toward the machine. Either he's the most BRAZEN villain in history or... or there's something I'm not seeing. Something Dastardly told me that wasn't the whole truth, or something about Pemberton's motives that I haven't understood. But right now — Clara and the team are heading to the laboratory. The machine needs three operators. Professor Pat Pending is HERE, right in front of me. The Ant Hill Mob told me to COME — they said Clara wants everyone in the laboratory TOGETHER. This is the final push. The machine. Three operators. The Professor to fix the wire. MOVE, James!

events.desc: I accused Pemberton and he didn't flinch. He didn't deny it, but he didn't crumble either. He just... offered to help. Maybe the truth is more complicated than Dastardly's confession. Maybe Pemberton WAS testing us — testing whether we'd use the poison, testing whether we were WORTHY of Clara's treasure. Or maybe he's still dangerous and I need to stay close. Either way, the laboratory is where everyone is gathering, the machine is the next puzzle, and Clara is there. Where Clara goes, James Hartwell follows. Not ahead. Not behind. BESIDE.

Penelope Pitstop: It RESPONDED! The machine let me IN! After forty-five minutes of being rejected by every coat rack, bookshelf, and stove in this manor, this beautiful brass-and-copper machine said YES to Clara Bellingham! Now — did y'all see that? Did anything change? The wire, the dials, the gauge — is anything different? And LOOK at this room — Pemberton, Dick, Ant Hill Mob, Rufus, Sawtooth, and ME — that's more than three operators! We have EVERYONE we need RIGHT HERE! Lord Doily wanted collaboration, and for the first time all evening, we are ALL in the SAME room at the SAME time with the ONE machine that matters! Everyone — if this machine needs three operators, then let's give it SIX! Rufus, Sawtooth — you know this machine better than anyone! Dick — put those clever hands to work! Pemberton — you know this manor's secrets! Ant Hill Mob — steady those levers! Clara Bellingham is calling ALL HANDS and she means EVERY LAST ONE!
events.thinking: The machine LET ME INTERACT! It responded! I touched it and it didn't reject me like the bookshelves, the crates, the stove, the chairs, the coat rack — it ACCEPTED my interaction! The machine is REAL, it WORKS, it responds! Now — the cognitive state says 'the manor let me in' and 'the thing I can start but can't finish alone.' The machine still says 'Requires 3 operators' and the wire is still gnawed through. But I INTERACTED with it! That's progress! Now I need to see what happened — did anything change? Did a new item appear? Did the description update? And there are now FIVE people in this room — me, Pemberton, Ant Hill Mob, Dick, Rufus, and Sawtooth! That's MORE than three operators! Everyone followed me here! This is the moment — everyone in one room, the machine responding to interaction, and enough operators to run it! Let me look at the machine to see if anything changed after my interaction!

events.desc: The machine responded to my interaction — the first time an interactive object has felt like PROGRESS rather than just acknowledgment! Everyone is HERE. More than three operators. If the machine needs multiple people interacting simultaneously, THIS is the moment. The wire is still gnawed, the wrench is still missing — but maybe sheer determination and six pairs of hands can overcome what one pair couldn't!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.
events.thinking: HOME. The laboratory feels like HOME. Not the entrance hall where I arrived, not the library where I was transformed, but HERE — the room with the machine that needs three operators, the room where everything CONVERGES. Clara is here. The Ant Hill Mob is here. Dastardly is here. Rufus and Sawtooth are here. We're GATHERING — the way Lord Doily always intended — not because anyone FORCED us but because the manor itself drew us together, puzzle by puzzle, confession by confession, forgiveness by forgiveness. The machine stands in the centre of the room like an altar, waiting for three pairs of hands. And I — Vincent Marsh, the man who arrived at this manor forty-six minutes ago with murder in his heart — I am going to put my hands on those levers alongside Clara Bellingham and whoever else stands with us, and I am going to PULL. Not to win. Not to steal. To HELP. Because Clara forgave me. Because Peter trusted me. Because Dastardly confessed beside me. Because the machine needs THREE and we ARE three and the wire is gnawed but Sawtooth is HERE and what a beaver broke, a beaver might MEND. The machine. The three operators. The moment this entire evening has been building toward. Let us see what Lord Doily left for the people who chose to pull TOGETHER.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: I'M HERE! Clara's HERE! The machine's HERE! And the machine needs THREE operators! Clara, me, and — Dastardly's here too, and Sneekly, and Rufus, and Sawtooth! We've got MORE than three! And Clara said the Professor can fix the wire without a wrench — where IS the Professor? He must be comin'. But the machine says INTERACT and it says 'requires 3 operators' — maybe if enough of us are in the room, we can just TRY it! Clara's here, I'm here, and there's five other people in this room! The machine is right there! The wire's been gnawed through by Sawtooth — and Sawtooth's RIGHT HERE! Maybe Sawtooth can gnaw it back together! Or maybe the Professor taught Clara somethin' about fixin' wires! Or maybe — just MAYBE — we don't need to fix the wire at all! Maybe the machine works WITH a gnawed wire and we just need three people to pull the levers! There's only one way to find out — TRY IT! The Brixton Boys didn't come all this way — through nine rooms, nine failures, one stolen poison, one pickpocketin', and forty-five minutes of chaos — to stand here and WAIT! We came here to PULL LEVERS!

events.desc: Forty-five minutes. From the entrance hall to here. Through every room in this manor, chasin' a woman I was supposed to protect, failin' at everything except the one thing that mattered — keepin' her alive. And now we're here. At the machine. Together. And I don't care if the wire's broken. I don't care if we need a wrench. I don't care if the whole thing explodes. Because Clara Bellingham is standin' next to me, alive and well, and the Brixton Boys are about to pull levers on a machine that might reveal the Doily Diamond. And if it doesn't work? We'll try again. Because that's what we do. We fail, we learn, we try again. And eventually — always eventually — we get it right.

events.thinking: ARRIVAL. Not the frantic, scheming arrival of forty minutes ago when I burst in here chasing Pemberton's shadow. This is different. This is showing UP. Penelope is here. The Ant Hill Mob is here. Rufus and Sawtooth are here. And Pemberton is here too — but this time I'm watching him with OPEN eyes instead of the trusting ones I've been wearing all evening. The machine needs three operators. It can be INTERACTED with. And for the first time in this entire catastrophic evening, I'm not trying to do something ALONE. I'm not trying to steal the glory or send everyone on wild goose chases or poison anything or lie about universities. I'm just... here. Ready to pull a lever. Ready to be one of three. Reginald Foxworth — one third of a team. The old me would WEEP. But the old me poisoned a tea set, so his opinion is no longer welcome.

events.desc: Look at me. Standing in front of a machine I tried to keep everyone AWAY from forty minutes ago, volunteering to be a TEAM PLAYER. The irony is so thick you could spread it on toast. But Penelope invited me. She said 'now is your chance.' And it IS. Not my chance to steal the diamond — though if it happens to fall into my lap during the machine operation, a Foxworth would be FOOLISH to refuse — but my chance to be part of something. To show up. To pull a lever alongside people instead of pulling strings behind them. And if Pemberton tries anything while we're operating this machine... well. The Ant Hill Mob is watching. And so am I. With OPEN eyes this time.
