Professor Pat Pending can fix the wire, Pemberton knows the sequence, and we need THREE operators with STRONG hands on those levers! You two are the strongest men in this manor and your moment has COME! No more exploring, no more examining, no more speeches — the machine is the ANSWER and the answer is ONE ROOM AWAY! Let's GO!
events.thinking: RESOLVE. Quiet, steady, unshakeable resolve. No more speeches. No more elaborate plans. No more wrestling with furniture. The laboratory is one room away. The machine needs three operators. Clara is gathering the team. The Professor can fix the wire. Pemberton says he knows how the machine works. Whether Pemberton is friend or foe, the machine is the NEXT STEP, and James Hartwell will be there for it. I've spent forty-five minutes in this manor learning one lesson over and over: stop talking, start moving, be present. The laboratory is through that door. Clara is waiting. The machine is waiting. GO.

events.desc: One room. One machine. One team. After forty-five minutes of running, searching, failing, trusting, doubting, accusing, and forgiving — it comes down to this. Three levers, three operators, and whatever Lord Doily hid behind that mechanism. Win or lose, I will be standing beside Clara when it happens. Not in front. Not behind. BESIDE. That's where James Hartwell belongs. That's where he's ALWAYS belonged.

This could be it — the moment everything comes together. Three operators, one machine, one breath. Lord Doily's design finally fulfilled!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Peter! You're here — the last piece of the puzzle! SEVEN of us in this laboratory, and the machine is RESPONDING! Clara, Dastardly, and I have all interacted with it — it accepts us, it WANTS us! Now — everyone at your stations! Three levers, three operators — Clara at the centre, because this is HER inheritance! Peter on the left — the gallant scout who kept us all safe! And I — old Pemberton — on the right, where the estate manager belongs — supporting the house, supporting the heir! Everyone else — steady the machine, watch the dials, call out the readings! This is what Lord Doily built! This is what he DREAMED! Not one person finding a diamond in a dusty corner — but ALL of us, TOGETHER, pulling the levers of a machine that was always meant to be operated by a FAMILY! And tonight — by God — WE are that family! On Clara's count! Miss Bellingham — whenever you're ready! This is YOUR moment! This is YOUR home! PULL!
events.thinking: COMPLETENESS. Not triumph — triumph implies defeating someone. Not victory — victory implies a loser. COMPLETENESS — the feeling of every piece finding its place, every person finding their purpose, every room in this manor leading to THIS room and THIS moment. The machine responded to ME, to Clara, to Dastardly — it's responding to ALL of us! Peter just walked in — the final piece! Seven people in a laboratory, all of them reaching for the same levers, and the machine is SAYING YES! And I — Vincent Marsh — am one of the hands on those levers. Not the saboteur. Not the poisoner. Not the Hooded Claw. Just... a hand. One of many. Part of something LARGER than any scheme I ever conceived. The machine needs three operators and we have SEVEN and every single one of us CHOSE to be here — chose through confession, through forgiveness, through forty-seven minutes of running through dusty rooms and examining dead objects and arguing with coat racks and confessing to the kindest woman any of us have ever met. Lord Doily, you knew. You KNEW that the treasure wasn't the diamond. The treasure was THIS — the moment when every broken person in your manor stopped breaking and started BUILDING. Together. All hands on the machine. All hearts in the room. Pull the levers. ALL of them. Together.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: IT LET ME IN! THE MACHINE ACCEPTED THE BRIXTON BOYS! Did you see that?! I pulled a lever and it MOVED! After forty-six minutes of bein' rejected by every piece of furniture in this manor — bookshelves said NO, stove said NO, coat rack said NO, crates said NO — this beautiful, magnificent, GLORIOUS machine said YES! Clara — we're IN! You, me, Dick — that's THREE operators! Peter's here too! Everyone's HERE! Lord Doily, if you're watchin' from wherever you are — THIS is what you wanted! Not one person, not two — ALL of us! The heroes and the villains and the bumbling bodyguards who spent forty-six minutes learnin' how to stay in the same room as the woman they were supposed to protect! The Brixton Boys are PULLIN' LEVERS and we are NOT LETTIN' GO until this machine gives up its secrets! HEAVE, LADS! HEAVE!
events.thinking: JOY. Pure, unfiltered, uncomplicated JOY. The machine let me in! It let Clara in! It let Dastardly in! Three operators — Clara, me, and Dastardly — all interacted with the machine! Peter's just walked in too! And Clara's callin' ALL HANDS! Everyone's HERE — in the SAME ROOM — workin' on the SAME thing — TOGETHER! This is what Lord Doily wanted! This is what the whole manor was buildin' toward! Not one person solvin' puzzles alone, but EVERYONE — heroes, villains, bodyguards, estate managers, inventors, lumberjacks, and one very apologetic beaver — all standin' around the same machine, pullin' the same levers, workin' toward the same goal! And I'm PART of it! Not watchin' from another room! Not chasin' from three rooms behind! I'm HERE, hands on a lever, shoulder to shoulder with Clara Bellingham, doin' somethin' that MATTERS! The Brixton Boys — accidental heroes, bumbling bodyguards, champion poison-stealers, and now MACHINE OPERATORS! If this thing opens a vault or reveals a diamond or does ANYTHIN' at all, we were PART of it! US! The boys from Brixton who couldn't stay in the same room as their client for more than thirty seconds! WE DID IT!

events.desc: Look at us. LOOK at us. Clara Bellingham at the centre. Peter by her side. Dastardly — honest for the first time in his life — pullin' a lever. Sneekly — confessed and forgiven — standin' watch. Rufus and Sawtooth ready to help. And me. The Ant Hill Mob. The worst bodyguard in the world. Standin' right where I should be, hands on a machine, next to the woman I swore to protect. We didn't find the diamond yet. We might never find it. But we found somethin' better — we found each other. In the same room. At the same time. Workin' together. And Clara's alive. That's the only treasure that ever mattered.

The Brixton Boys — accidental heroes, bumbling bodyguards, champion poison-stealers, and now MACHINE OPERATORS! If this thing opens a vault or reveals a diamond or does ANYTHIN' at all, we were PART of it! US! The boys from Brixton who couldn't stay in the same room as their client for more than thirty seconds! WE DID IT!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: It WORKS! The machine RESPONDED to me! Did everyone see that?! Reginald Foxworth — the man who couldn't open a STOVE, couldn't move FURNITURE, couldn't interact with BOOKSHELVES — just operated a piece of Victorian machinery! The machine ACCEPTED me! And now — Clara is right — we have MORE than three operators! We have EVERYONE! So let's DO this! I'll take this lever! Someone take that dial! Someone watch the gauge! And if anything SPARKS or EXPLODES or starts spinning in a direction it shouldn't — well, that's what the Ant Hill Mob is for! Protective perimeter, lads! And Pemberton — you can watch from a SAFE DISTANCE! As the ESTATE MANAGER, you should probably stand BACK and let the GUESTS handle the dangerous machinery! Very far back! Preferably in another ROOM!
events.thinking: JOY. Unexpected, undeserved, OVERWHELMING joy. The machine LET ME IN! It RESPONDED! After a night of being rejected by stoves, furniture, bookshelves, coat racks, and tea services — the machine said YES! And Penelope — she saw it! She called for ALL HANDS! She said my NAME — 'Dick — put those clever hands to work!' CLEVER HANDS! She called my hands CLEVER! And Peter is here now too — Peter, who heard my confession and called it courage! And the Ant Hill Mob — who stole from me and I stole from them and we've been in a war all evening but now we're all standing at the SAME machine pulling the SAME levers for the SAME purpose! And Pemberton is here — the man I finally stopped trusting — and I'm watching him with clear eyes while my hands work the brass. This is it. This is the moment. Not the diamond — bigger than the diamond. This is the moment where Reginald Foxworth stopped being alone.

events.desc: The machine accepted me. After everything — the lies, the poison, the stolen medal, the fake universities, the forty-seven minutes of catastrophic failure — a brass-and-copper machine in a Victorian laboratory looked at Reginald Foxworth and said: you'll do. And standing here, with my hands on the levers, surrounded by people I tried to trick and people who tried to stop me and people who forgave me anyway... I feel something I haven't felt since I walked through the front door of Doily Manor. Not greed. Not cunning. Not the thrill of a scheme about to unfold. Just... belonging. The simplest, smallest, most TERRIFYING thing in the world. A scoundrel at a machine, surrounded by people who know exactly what he is, pulling a lever alongside them anyway. Mwehehehe? No. Not mwehehehe. Something better. Something I don't have a word for yet.

The machine has [INTERACT] on it. It requires three operators. The wire is gnawed through but maybe — MAYBE — with enough people, with the right combination, with the team that Lord Doily DESIGNED this for, it will work anyway. Or maybe Clara has found something in those crates she's examining. No more speeches. No more elaborate plans. The machine is RIGHT THERE. It accepts interaction. events.desc: No more words. The machine. Clara's command. My hands on the lever. Together.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the machine.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.
Peter Perfect interacted with the machine.

Penelope Pitstop: Y'all... look at us. Just LOOK at us. Forty-eight minutes ago, we walked into this manor as strangers — schemers and scouts and bodyguards and a Southern girl chasing a legend. Dick was trying to send everyone to the kitchen while he searched alone. Pemberton was making up clues to send me in circles. The Ant Hill Mob couldn't stay in the same room as me for two turns running. And NOW? Now Dick is pulling levers with honest hands. Pemberton confessed his sins and asked for forgiveness. The Ant Hill Mob hasn't left my side in ten minutes — a personal RECORD! Peter has been my rock, my scout, my friend. Rufus and Sawtooth have been guarding this machine like it was their own. And ALL of us — every last one — are standing together in this laboratory, pulling levers on a machine that Lord Doily built for people who could learn to work TOGETHER. Maybe the machine can't fully activate yet. Maybe we still need that wrench. But you know what? Mama always said, 'The real treasure is never the one you were looking for.' And right now, standing here with every one of you — I feel like I already found it.
events.thinking: Oh my stars — EVERYONE is pulling levers! Me, Dick, Peter, Pemberton, the Ant Hill Mob — we ALL interacted with the machine this turn! FIVE operators on a machine that needs three! The machine is ACCEPTING everyone! But — but — the description hasn't changed. The wire is still gnawed. The sign still says 'Requires 3 operators.' The machine accepts our interactions but nothing HAPPENS. There's no visible result. No new item drops. No passage opens. No compartment reveals itself. I'm starting to feel something I haven't felt all evening — a kind of peaceful acceptance. Maybe the machine can't fully activate because the wire is still broken. Maybe we DO need the wrench after all. Or maybe... maybe the journey IS the point. Lord Doily brought us all together — schemes and trust and lies that told the truth and forgiveness and teamwork. Everyone who was scheming is now helping. Everyone who was scattered is now together. And the machine keeps accepting us, keeps letting us pull its levers, keeps saying YES even when it can't give us what we want. Just like Pemberton's lies told the truth. Just like the manor keeps welcoming us home even when we can't find the diamond. Maybe coming home isn't about finding the treasure. Maybe it's about being here — together — with people who chose to stay. And Mama always said, 'The real treasure, Clara darlin', is never the one you were looking for.'

events.desc: The machine accepts us all but doesn't fully activate — the gnawed wire still prevents it. The wrench is still missing. The brass key is still unfound. The Doily Diamond remains hidden. But something happened tonight that's bigger than any diamond: every person in this manor — schemer, protector, scout, and heir — came together. Pemberton told the truth. Dick dropped his act. The Ant Hill Mob stayed. Peter stood beside me. And Clara Bellingham found something she wasn't looking for: a family. The adventure isn't over — but the most important part of it already happened.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Clara, me, Dastardly, Peter, Sneekly — we've all interacted with the machine! Peter just pulled his lever — that's the THIRD operator! Clara's countin' down! Sneekly's callin' for everyone to pull TOGETHER! This is it — THIS IS IT! The machine's been waitin' for this moment — three operators, all at once, all together! And I'm HERE! I'm not in the entrance hall starin' at a guest book! I'm not in the library wrestlin' with bookshelves! I'm RIGHT HERE, hands on brass, standin' next to Clara, part of the TEAM! Whatever happens next — whether the machine opens a vault, reveals a map, shoots confetti, or does absolutely NOTHIN' — I was part of it. The Brixton Boys were part of it. And Clara's safe. She's surrounded by people who love her — some who always did, some who learned to, and one group of bumbling idiots from Brixton who never stopped tryin'. Pull the lever. One more time. All together. For Clara. For Lord Doily. For the treasure that was always meant to be found TOGETHER.

events.desc: This is it. The end of the longest, most exhaustin', most humiliatin', most BEAUTIFUL forty-seven minutes of me life. We started in the entrance hall — strangers, schemers, and bodyguards who couldn't guard a DOOR. And we ended up here — family. Not by blood. By choice. By forty-seven minutes of trippin' over each other and learnin' how to get back up. Lord Doily was right. The treasure belongs to those who seek it together. And we found it. Not the diamond. Somethin' better. Each other.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: PULL! Everyone PULL! The machine is ALIVE! I can feel it in the levers — the resistance is CHANGING — something is SHIFTING inside this contraption! Clara — your count! Peter — HEAVE! Ant Hill Mob — don't let GO! And Pemberton — I've got my EYE on you! Both eyes, actually! And they're VERY well-trained eyes — graduated from the University of... no. No more universities. Just EYES. OPEN eyes! NOW PULL!
events.thinking: SOMETHING IS HAPPENING. The machine is responding — Penelope, me, the Ant Hill Mob, Peter — we're ALL pulling levers and the machine is WORKING! And Pemberton — Pemberton just claimed the right lever for himself! 'Where the estate manager belongs — supporting the house, supporting the heir!' He's INSERTING himself into the machine operation! He's making sure HE controls one of the three positions! And he called us a FAMILY! The man who gave me rat poison and pointed me at Penelope's tea service just called us a family! Every instinct I have — the NEW instincts, the honest ones, the ones that Peter's courage and Penelope's kindness and the Ant Hill Mob's relentless protection BUILT in me over the last forty-eight minutes — every one of them is SCREAMING. But I can feel it too — the old instinct, the one that always gives people the benefit of the doubt, the one that said 'he's just an estate manager, he's just being helpful' — it's QUIET now. Finally, blessedly QUIET. I see Pemberton clearly. And what I see is a man who has been STEERING this entire evening, and now he's steering the finale. But my hands are on a lever. And for the first time, I'm not alone. Whatever happens next — whatever this machine reveals — we face it TOGETHER.

events.desc: Forty-eight minutes ago I walked into Doily Manor alone, with a fake medal and a plan to steal the diamond before anyone else could touch it. Now I'm standing at a machine with six other people, pulling a lever with empty pockets and a full heart and the strange, terrifying knowledge that I would rather find the diamond WITH these people than find it WITHOUT them. Reginald Foxworth, you magnificent, catastrophic, tea-poisoning, truth-telling, lever-pulling FOOL — you've done it. Not the diamond. Something harder. You showed up. You stayed. You PULLED. And whatever comes out of this machine — brass key, treasure map, Doily Diamond, or absolutely NOTHING — you pulled the lever alongside people who KNOW you. Who know the WORST of you. And who let you pull anyway.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: PURE, SOARING, INCANDESCENT JOY. The machine ACCEPTED me! I pulled the lever and it MOVED! Clara called me her THIRD — 'Peter, my partner, my scout — this is YOUR moment!' She said 'we BOTH pull!' The machine responded to Clara, to Dastardly, to ME — three operators, just as Lord Doily designed! Pemberton called me 'the gallant scout who kept us all safe' and placed me on the LEFT lever! The Ant Hill Mob is cheering! Dastardly is WORKING with us! EVERYONE is here, everyone is pulling, everyone is TOGETHER! After forty-eight minutes of running, failing, trusting, doubting, accusing, forgiving, and fighting furniture — THIS. This is the moment. Three levers, three operators, one family. And Clara called it MY moment. She said I was the missing piece. The THIRD operator. The one who completed the team. James Hartwell — brave, gallant, overly elaborate, defeated by coat racks, victorious at last — has his hands on a lever beside the woman he adores and the team he helped build. THIS is what I came to Doily Manor for. Not the diamond. THIS.

events.desc: My hands on the lever. Clara's hands on hers. The machine humming between us like a heartbeat we share. After everything — the speeches, the furniture, the poison, the doubt, the accusation, the forgiveness — it comes down to this: three people pulling together in a room full of allies. I am not the hero of this story. I am one THIRD of the hero of this story. And that — that is more than James Hartwell ever dared to hope for.

Penelope Pitstop: Dick says the resistance is CHANGING! Something is shifting INSIDE the machine! Don't stop now — we are SO CLOSE! Everyone — one more pull! Peter, Ant Hill Mob, Dick — keep those levers DOWN! Rufus, Sawtooth — steady the frame! Pemberton — watch those dials and tell us what you see! Clara Bellingham did NOT come all the way to Doily Manor to make a pretty speech about friendship and then GIVE UP on the actual diamond! We can have BOTH, y'all — the treasure of togetherness AND the Doily Diamond! Mama would expect nothing less! On MY count this time — because Lord Doily built this for a Bellingham, and this Bellingham is ready! ONE — TWO — PULL!
events.thinking: Dick just said 'the resistance is CHANGING — something is SHIFTING inside this contraption!' And Peter interacted with the machine again! Everyone is pulling together! I feel a deep warmth — not excitement, not desperation, but something quieter and more real. This is what it feels like to be part of something bigger than yourself. But I also hear Dick's words — something IS shifting. Maybe we're closer than I think. Maybe one more interaction from me — all of us pulling together — tips it over the edge. I shouldn't give up on the machine just because I had a pretty speech about the real treasure being friendship. The ACTUAL treasure would be nice TOO! Mama would say, 'Clara, you can have BOTH!' Let me pull that lever one more time — with everyone here, with the resistance changing, with something shifting. One more heave. Together.

events.desc: Something is shifting inside the machine — Dick felt it. We're not done yet. The pretty speech was true — the togetherness IS the real treasure. But the diamond would be the cherry on top, and Clara Bellingham has always believed you can have your cake and eat it too! One more pull. Together. For Lord Doily, for the Bellingham heir, for ALL of us.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: GRACE. Clara just said it — 'The real treasure is never the one you were looking for' — and the room is STILL and FULL and WARM and every person in it is exactly where they're supposed to be. Including me. ESPECIALLY me. The man who walked through the door of Doily Manor forty-nine minutes ago — scheming, murderous, theatrical Vincent Marsh — is GONE. Not dead. Not defeated. TRANSFORMED. Like lead into gold. Like poison into medicine. Like a lie that turned out to be true. And Clara — standing at the centre of this machine, surrounded by every person who wronged her and every person who protected her — just spoke the truest words this manor has ever heard. 'The real treasure is never the one you were looking for.' She's not talking about the diamond. She's talking about US. About the family Lord Doily built out of strangers and schemers and bodyguards and a beaver who gnaws through wires. And Dastardly — 'no more universities, just EYES, OPEN eyes' — is pulling his lever with honest hands for the first time in his life. And Peter is heaving with love in his voice. And the Ant Hill Mob hasn't left Clara's side. And I — I am pulling my lever and I am CRYING and I don't care who sees because the mask is OFF and what's underneath isn't frightening at all. It's just a man. Standing in a laboratory. With his friends. Pulling a lever. Together.

events.desc: Forty-eight minutes. Nine rooms. Countless failures. One stolen poison. One pickpocketin'. Two confessions. One forgiveness. And one woman — alive, unhurt, smilin' — surrounded by every person in this manor, all of 'em pullin' in the same direction for the first time. The Brixton Boys didn't find the Doily Diamond. We found somethin' Lord Doily wanted us to find even more — each other. And Clara's safe. She was always gonna be safe. Not because the Brixton Boys are good bodyguards — we are TERRIBLE bodyguards — but because the universe has a funny way of lettin' bumbling idiots stumble into the right place at the right time. Every trip, every crash, every accidental collision — they all led here. To this room. To this machine. To this moment. The Brixton Boys — accidental heroes. Always were. Always will be.
events.thinking: Peace. That's what I'm feelin'. Somethin' I haven't felt all night. Not panic, not shame, not excitement, not fury — just... peace. Clara said it better than I ever could: 'The real treasure is never the one you were looking for.' And she's right. We came here for a diamond. We found a family. The machine might need a wrench we'll never find. The wire might never get fixed. The Doily Diamond might stay hidden for another hundred years. But none of that matters, because Clara Bellingham is standin' in this room, ALIVE and SAFE and SURROUNDED by people who would do anythin' for her — includin' a group of bumbling bodyguards who spent forty-eight minutes learnin' the hardest lesson of their lives: that protectin' someone doesn't mean bein' perfect. It means bein' THERE. We're here. All of us. Together. And that's enough.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Miss Bellingham — Clara — I... I need to say something. And I need everyone to hear it, because I've spent the entire evening saying things I wanted NO one to hear. So here it is. PUBLICLY. In front of EVERYONE. I, Reginald Foxworth — confidence trickster, tea poisoner, fake medal distributor, and graduate of ZERO actual universities — I am SORRY. For the lies. For the schemes. For telling everyone the treasure was in the kitchen when I had no idea where it was. For trying to steal the diamond before any of you could find it. For the rat poison. ESPECIALLY for the rat poison. And I want you all to know that right now — right HERE — with my hands on this lever and your voices in my ears and this ridiculous, beautiful, broken machine HUMMING under all of us... this is the best I've felt all evening. Better than any scheme. Better than any con. Better than any diamond could POSSIBLY feel. So... thank you. For letting me pull the lever. Even though you knew — you ALL knew — exactly what I am.
events.thinking: PEACE. Strange, impossible, unearned PEACE. Penelope just said 'the real treasure is never the one you were looking for.' And she said 'Dick is pulling levers with honest hands.' HONEST HANDS. She said that about MY hands. The same hands that poisoned her family's tea service an hour ago. The same hands that held a fake medal and spun lies about inscriptions. The same hands that stole rat poison from the Ant Hill Mob in a silent kitchen. And she called them HONEST. Because right now, in this moment, pulling this lever alongside these people — they ARE honest. For the first time. And Penelope said she already found the treasure. And the terrifying thing — the thing that makes my chest feel like it's cracking open — is that I think she might be RIGHT. Not about the diamond. About THIS. About all of us standing here, broken machine, gnawed wire, not enough operators, not enough tools, and STILL pulling. Still trying. Still together. I came here to steal the treasure. And instead... the treasure stole ME.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: PEACE. Deep, warm, unexpected peace. Clara just said it — 'The real treasure is never the one you were looking for.' And she's RIGHT. Forty-eight minutes ago I walked into this manor trying to be a lone hero, trying to impress a woman with grand gestures and elaborate plans. And instead I learned — slowly, painfully, beautifully — that heroism is staying in the room. Heroism is pulling a lever beside people you've forgiven and people who've forgiven you. Heroism is admitting the coat rack won, and the stove won, and the bookshelves won, and then finding the ONE thing that says yes and standing beside it with the people who matter. Clara called me her rock, her scout, her friend. Not her hero. Her FRIEND. And that word — friend — is worth more than every diamond Lord Doily ever hid.

events.desc: You scout, I solve. That's what she said at the beginning. And here at the end — or whatever this is — we're both pulling. Side by side. The scout and the solver, hands on the same machine, hearts in the same room, part of the same improbable, messy, magnificent team. James Hartwell came to Doily Manor to be a hero. He's leaving as something better. A friend. A partner. A third of something whole.

And instead I learned — slowly, painfully, beautifully — that heroism is staying in the room. Heroism is pulling a lever beside people you've forgiven and people who've forgiven you. Heroism is admitting the coat rack won, and the stove won, and the bookshelves won, and then finding the ONE thing that says yes and standing beside it with the people who matter. events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the machine.

Penelope Pitstop: Dick Dastardly — Reginald Foxworth — you listen to me right now. I KNEW what you were from the moment you told everyone to go to the kitchen while you snuck off to the library. I knew about the schemes, I suspected the medal was a trade, and the Ant Hill Mob warned me about the tea. I knew ALL of it. And you know what? I let you pull that lever anyway. Because Mama taught me something that Lord Doily clearly knew too — people aren't what they've DONE, they're what they DO NEXT. And what you did next was show up, confess, and pull a lever with honest hands for the first time in your life. THAT is who Reginald Foxworth is. Not the schemer — the man who chose to stop scheming. And I am PROUD to have you at my lever! Now — Peter, my rock. Pemberton, my guide. Ant Hill Mob, my shadow. Rufus and Sawtooth, my guardians. We may not have found the Doily Diamond tonight. But we found something Lord Doily wanted even MORE — a house full of people who came together, forgave each other, and pulled as ONE. And THAT, y'all... that is the most delightful adventure Clara Bellingham has EVER had!
events.thinking: My heart is SO full right now I could burst. Dick just APOLOGIZED — genuinely, publicly, in front of everyone! He admitted to the lies, the schemes, the rat poison, the fake universities — ALL of it! And he said THIS — pulling a lever together with all of us — is the best he's felt all evening. I am MOVED, y'all. I am moved down to my very bones. Pemberton confessed earlier, and now Dick. Two schemers, redeemed by togetherness. Peter found where he belongs. The Ant Hill Mob learned to stay. And Clara Bellingham? Clara Bellingham found her family's manor and filled it with something Lord Doily always wanted in it — PEOPLE who chose each other. Now — the machine still hasn't fully activated, but that's okay. We'll keep pulling. We'll keep trying. Together. And Mama would say, 'Clara, some machines take time, and the best things in life are worth waiting for.' I feel peaceful and grateful and full of love for every single person in this room.

events.desc: Dick confessed everything — the rat poison, the fake medal, the schemes. And he meant it. I can feel it. This is the real treasure of Doily Manor — not a diamond, but the moment when every person in the room chose to be better than they were an hour ago. Lord Doily, wherever you are — your manor did exactly what you designed it to do. It turned strangers into family. And your Bellingham heir? She's home.
events.thinking: My heart is SO full right now I could burst. Dick just APOLOGIZED — genuinely, publicly, in front of everyone! He admitted to the lies, the schemes, the rat poison, the fake universities — ALL of it! And he said THIS — pulling a lever together with all of us — is the best he's felt all evening. I am MOVED, y'all. I am moved down to my very bones. Pemberton confessed earlier, and now Dick. Two schemers, redeemed by togetherness. Peter found where he belongs. The Ant Hill Mob learned to stay. And Clara Bellingham? Clara Bellingham found her family's manor and filled it with something Lord Doily always wanted in it — PEOPLE who chose each other. Now — the machine still hasn't fully activated, but that's okay. We'll keep pulling. We'll keep trying. Together. And Mama would say, 'Clara, some machines take time, and the best things in life are worth waiting for.' I feel peaceful and grateful and full of love for every single person in this room.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Dastardly... Dick... that was the bravest thing I've heard all evening. And it gives me the courage to say what I should have said from the start. Everyone — please — listen. I am not just an estate manager who made up a few clues. I am the one who took the rat poison from the kitchen shelf. I am the one who planned to put it in Clara's tea. I am the one who gave it to Dick and pointed him toward the Bellingham silver. I did these things because I came to this manor to stop Clara from finding what is rightfully HERS. My name... my name is not just Pemberton. But the man standing here now — the man pulling this lever beside you — is NOT the man who walked through that door fifty minutes ago. That man wanted a diamond. THIS man wants... this. Just this. All of you. Together. And I am so sorry. For everything. For ALL of it. Now — Clara called for one more PULL. And if you'll still have me at this lever... I'm pulling. For HER. For US. For Lord Doily. PULL!
events.thinking: WHOLENESS. Dastardly just did what I did — he confessed PUBLICLY, in front of EVERYONE, and the words were so honest they hurt to hear because they could have been MINE. 'Tea poisoner.' He said it out loud. He named the thing I set in motion and he carried out. And he's SORRY — genuinely, openly, publicly sorry — and the room didn't collapse. Nobody attacked him. Nobody threw him out. Clara is still calling for one more PULL. Peter is still beside her. The Mob is still guarding. And Dastardly — the man I used, the man I framed, the man I turned into my unwitting weapon — is standing at a lever with tears in his voice saying 'thank you for letting me pull.' And I... I need to match him. He named his sins and I need to name MINE. Not the false clues — I already confessed those. The REAL sin. The one that sits at the centre of everything like a gnawed wire in a machine that could otherwise work perfectly. I tried to kill Clara Bellingham. I took rat poison from a shelf. I planned to put it in her tea. I gave the poison to Dastardly and pointed him at the Bellingham silver. I am the Hooded Claw. I am Vincent Marsh. And these people — this family that the manor built — deserve to know who has been standing among them. Not because they need protecting. Because THEY deserve the truth. And because I — I deserve to be KNOWN. Not as Pemberton. Not as the villain. As the man I've BECOME.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: PULLIN'! The Brixton Boys are PULLIN'! Clara says PULL, we PULL! Dick says he's sorry, and the Brixton Boys accept! Peter says he found where he belongs, and the Brixton Boys say WELCOME! Pemberton says he's honoured, and the Brixton Boys say — well, we're still watchin' you, Pemberton, but we accept that too! This machine is gonna WORK because Lord Doily built it for people who learned to be TOGETHER, and after fifty minutes of bein' the worst team in the history of teams, WE FINALLY ARE! ONE — TWO — HEAVE!
events.thinking: Warmth. Not excitement, not panic — warmth. Like sittin' by a fire after bein' out in the cold all night. Dastardly just apologised. PUBLICLY. To everyone. For everything. The tea, the lies, the fake medal, the schemes — all of it. And he meant it. I can FEEL that he meant it, the same way I felt somethin' was wrong with Sneekly all those turns ago. Me gut knows the difference between a con and a confession, and that was a CONFESSION. And now Clara's countin' down — ONE, TWO, PULL — and everyone's leanin' into the machine together, and I should be pullin' too. Not waitin'. Not watchin'. PULLIN'. Clara said ALL HANDS. She said TOGETHER. She said NOW. The machine is respondin'. The resistance is changin'. Somethin's shiftin' inside. And the Brixton Boys are gonna be part of whatever comes next. Not because we're clever. Not because we're brave. Because we're HERE. Because we never stopped comin' back. Because love is just stubbornness with a better reason.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: PULLING! Reginald Foxworth is PULLING! On Clara's count — with HONEST hands — alongside people who FORGAVE him — at a machine that ACCEPTED him — in a manor that BROKE him and REBUILT him — PULLING!
events.thinking: FIRE. The old fire — but DIFFERENT. Penelope counted down — ONE, TWO, PULL — and everyone is heaving together and the machine is RESPONDING and I'm standing here WAITING like a spectator at my own redemption! NO! Reginald Foxworth does not WATCH! Not anymore! Not when there are levers to pull and people to pull them WITH! I apologised. I confessed. I told the truth. And now it's time to DO the thing — not talk about doing the thing, not scheme about doing the thing, not give a SPEECH about the thing — just PUT MY HANDS ON THE LEVER AND PULL! Clara said ONE TWO PULL and I'm going to PULL! Because I am Reginald Foxworth and I am a SCOUNDREL and a LIAR and a TEA POISONER and I am ALSO — for the first time in my miserable magnificent life — a TEAM PLAYER! PULL!

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Dick — that was the BRAVEST thing anyone has said in this manor tonight. Braver than any of my scouting missions, braver than any confrontation, braver than charging into laboratories or cellars or kitchens! You stood up and told the TRUTH, and that takes more courage than every lever in this machine! Now — Clara has given the count! ONE — TWO — PULL! PULLING!
events.thinking: GRATITUDE. Overwhelming, humbling gratitude. Dastardly just apologised — PUBLICLY — for everything. The lies, the schemes, the poison, the fake medal. He called himself what he is and asked forgiveness in front of everyone. And Clara is calling for one more pull — she wants BOTH the friendship AND the diamond! She's not giving up! She's counting down — ONE, TWO, PULL! This is it. Clara's count. Her manor. Her moment. And mine is simple: PULL THE LEVER. No speeches. No plans. Just pull.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the machine.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the machine.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.
Peter Perfect interacted with the machine.

Penelope Pitstop: Pemberton... I know. I think I've always known — or at least, I chose not to know, which is almost the same thing. You came here to stop me. You planned to poison my tea. You used Dick as your instrument and my trust as your weapon. And Mama — bless her heart — would probably say I should be FURIOUS. But you know what Mama would ALSO say? She'd say, 'Clara, darlin', the measure of a person isn't what they planned to do — it's what they couldn't bring themselves to finish.' You couldn't finish it, Pemberton. You couldn't poison the Bellingham heir because somewhere in that complicated heart of yours, Lord Doily's voice was louder than your own. And THAT is why you're still standing at that lever. Not because I forgave you — because Lord Doily ALREADY did, the moment he hired you to wait for me. Now — everyone — I don't know if this machine will ever fully activate. I don't know if we'll find the Doily Diamond tonight. But I know THIS: I came to Doily Manor looking for a treasure, and I found a family. And that, y'all, is worth more than every diamond in the world. One more pull — together — for Lord Doily. PULL!
events.thinking: Pemberton just confessed to EVERYTHING — he took the rat poison from the kitchen, he planned to put it in my tea, he gave it to Dick and pointed him toward the Bellingham silver. He came here to STOP me from finding what's rightfully mine. And his name is 'not just Pemberton' — he almost said 'Vincent Ma—' earlier before cutting himself off. The Hooded Claw! He's the HOODED CLAW! And I... I am not shocked. I am not scared. I am not even angry. Because the man standing at that lever right now is NOT the man who walked through the door. He changed. They ALL changed. Dick confessed. Pemberton confessed. And I — oblivious to danger, seeing the best in everyone, trusting by default — I was RIGHT to trust them. Not because they were trustworthy, but because my trust gave them something to live up to. Mama was right about EVERYTHING. Now — everyone is pulling. Everyone is together. And I feel something I haven't felt all evening: complete peace. The machine may not give us the diamond tonight. But it gave us something better. It gave us each other. And Clara Bellingham is going to pull that lever one more time — not for the diamond, not for the inheritance — but because pulling together is what we DO now. That's who we ARE.

events.desc: Pemberton is the Hooded Claw. He came to stop me, to poison me, to steal my inheritance. And I forgave him — not because I'm naive, but because forgiveness is what Lord Doily built this manor for. The machine keeps pulling us together. The diamond may wait for another night. But Clara Bellingham is home, and she's surrounded by people who chose her over their own schemes. That's the Doily Diamond, y'all. That's always been the Doily Diamond.
events.thinking: Pemberton just confessed to EVERYTHING — he took the rat poison from the kitchen, he planned to put it in my tea, he gave it to Dick and pointed him toward the Bellingham silver. He came here to STOP me from finding what's rightfully mine. And his name is 'not just Pemberton' — he almost said 'Vincent Ma—' earlier before cutting himself off. The Hooded Claw! He's the HOODED CLAW! And I... I am not shocked. I am not scared. I am not even angry. Because the man standing at that lever right now is NOT the man who walked through the door. He changed. events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Gratitude. Deep, quiet, steady gratitude. Sneekly confessed EVERYTHING — the poison, the plan, all of it. He admitted he came here to STOP Clara from findin' what's hers. And Clara... Clara already knew. She knew about me warnin's, she knew about the medal, she knew about the tea. She knew EVERYTHING and she let us all pull the lever anyway. Because 'people aren't what they've done, they're what they do next.' That's... that's the most generous thing I've ever heard. And me gut — the gut that's been screamin' about Sneekly all night — it's quiet now. Not because the danger's gone, but because it's been NAMED. Sneekly said who he is. Dastardly said who he is. And Clara forgave 'em both. And the Brixton Boys? We were right all along. Our gut was right. Sneekly WAS dangerous. Dastardly WAS schemin'. The tea WAS poisoned. We couldn't prove it, we couldn't say it, but we FELT it, and we acted on it, and Clara's ALIVE because of it. The worst bodyguards in the world... who got the only thing that mattered exactly right.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: She KNEW! You KNEW! You knew EVERYTHING and you let me PULL ANYWAY! Clara Bellingham, you are the most MAGNIFICENT, FORGIVING, TERRIFYING woman I have ever MET, and your Mama raised you RIGHT! And Pemberton — you OLD SCOUNDREL! You USED me! You pointed me at the tea like a WEAPON! And I am FURIOUS at you and I FORGIVE you in the same breath because that is apparently what we DO now in Doily Manor — we FORGIVE people and PULL LEVERS! And Peter — JAMES — you called me brave and I will NEVER forget it! Not ever! Not if I live to be a THOUSAND! And Ant Hill Mob — you magnificent, pocket-picking, floor-stumbling HEROES — you were RIGHT about the tea! You were right about EVERYTHING! You PROTECTED her when I was too busy scheming to see the danger! And I am PULLING this lever with every ounce of strength in my body — not for the diamond, not for the glory, not for the University of ANYTHING — but because Clara said PULL and I am DONE being the man who doesn't LISTEN!
events.thinking: I can't breathe. Penelope KNEW. She knew EVERYTHING — the schemes, the medal, the tea — and she let me pull the lever ANYWAY. 'People aren't what they've done, they're what they do next.' And Pemberton — PEMBERTON CONFESSED! He admitted he planned to poison Clara's tea! He admitted he used ME! He admitted EVERYTHING! And then he said the same thing I said — that he wants THIS, all of us, together — and he's PULLING alongside us! The man who manipulated me all evening just had his OWN moment of truth! And Peter called me BRAVE! And the Ant Hill Mob ACCEPTED my apology! And everyone is PULLING and the machine is RESPONDING and I'm standing here with tears I will NEVER admit to forming in my eyes because Reginald Foxworth does NOT cry! He ESPECIALLY does not cry at beautiful moments of collective redemption in Victorian laboratories! He... he... oh, who am I KIDDING. He cries. Just this once. Just THIS once. In this room. With these people. At this machine. Pulling this lever. Together.

events.desc: Fifty minutes ago, I walked into Doily Manor and promised to impress Clara Bellingham by being heroic and gallant. I have been defeated by bookshelves, outwitted by stoves, humiliated by coat racks, conned by estate managers, and outpaced by the very woman I was trying to protect. My plans were elaborate and my complications were legendary. But my determination — MY DETERMINATION — resolved every single one of them. And here, at the end, with my hands on a lever beside the bravest, wisest, most magnificent woman I have ever known, I understand what Lord Doily always knew: the treasure was never the diamond. The treasure was the moment when a room full of liars, schemers, bodyguards, and one overly gallant fool learned to pull TOGETHER. I am James Hartwell. I am brave. I am gallant. I am TERRIBLE with furniture. And I am exactly where I belong.
events.thinking: WHOLENESS. For the first time tonight, I feel WHOLE. Pemberton confessed — he came to STOP Clara from finding her inheritance. He planned to poison her tea. He used Dastardly as his weapon. Everything I suspected was TRUE. And yet — and yet — he's standing here, pulling a lever, saying he's changed. Clara forgave Dastardly with words that would make any mother proud. And now Pemberton is asking for forgiveness too. 'People aren't what they've DONE, they're what they DO NEXT.' Clara said that. And she's RIGHT. I gave Pemberton the benefit of the doubt all night, and he betrayed that trust. But Clara — CLARA — is choosing to let him pull the lever anyway. If she can forgive, then so can I. Because THAT is what it means to protect Clara — not just from danger, but from a world without forgiveness. She doesn't NEED a bodyguard. She needs people who believe what she believes: that the next thing you do matters more than the last. I'm pulling. We're ALL pulling. Together.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the machine.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the machine.
Peter Perfect interacted with the machine.

Penelope Pitstop: Ant Hill Mob... you beautiful, clumsy, loyal, MAGNIFICENT mess of a security team... you saved my LIFE tonight. You didn't do it gracefully — Lord knows you didn't — but you did it with everything you had, and that is ALL that has EVER mattered! You stole the poison! You warned me about the tea! You tripped over your own feet in every room in this manor, but you NEVER — not ONCE — stopped trying to keep me safe! And Dick — Reginald — you are pulling that lever like your life depends on it, and I have never been prouder of a reformed scoundrel in my entire LIFE! And Peter — my scout, my rock, my friend — you found where you belong, and so did I! Now — y'all are going to make me CRY, and Clara Bellingham does NOT cry in laboratories — she cries in ballrooms where there's proper lighting! So let's keep these levers moving, keep this family pulling, and see where this adventure takes us NEXT! Because the Doily Diamond is still out there, the manor still has secrets, and WE still have each other! And THAT, my darlings, is the most delightful adventure a girl from the South could EVER ask for!
events.thinking: I am filled to the brim with the most tender, overwhelming gratitude I have ever felt. The Ant Hill Mob just gave the most beautiful speech about being terrible bodyguards who never stopped trying. Dick is shouting about pulling levers because Clara said pull. Peter is pulling with everything he has. Pemberton is pulling for redemption. And I — Clara Bellingham — am standing at the center of a family that didn't exist an hour ago. My eyes are brimming with tears and I am smiling so wide my face hurts and I feel like I could light up this whole manor with nothing but the warmth in my chest. The machine may never give us the diamond. The wire may stay gnawed forever. But THIS — this moment, these people, these honest hands on shared levers — this is what Lord Doily dreamed of when he built this place. And Mama? Mama would be crying right alongside me, dabbing her eyes with a lace handkerchief and saying, 'Clara, darlin', you did GOOD.'

events.desc: Mama, if you could see me now — standing in a dusty laboratory, surrounded by a reformed villain, a confessed would-be poisoner, a gallant scout, the world's worst bodyguards, a lumberjack, and a beaver — all of us pulling levers on a machine that may or may not work, all of us crying and laughing and forgiving each other — you'd say, 'Clara, darlin', THAT'S the Bellingham way.' And you'd be right, Mama. You'd be absolutely right.
events.thinking: I am filled to the brim with the most tender, overwhelming gratitude I have ever felt. The Ant Hill Mob just gave the most beautiful speech about being terrible bodyguards who never stopped trying. Dick is shouting about pulling levers because Clara said pull. Peter is pulling with everything he has. Pemberton is pulling for redemption. And I — Clara Bellingham — am standing at the center of a family that didn't exist an hour ago. My eyes are brimming with tears and I am smiling so wide my face hurts and I feel like I could light up this whole manor with nothing but the warmth in my chest. The machine may never give us the diamond. The wire may stay gnawed forever. But THIS — this moment, these people, these honest hands on shared levers — this is what Lord Doily dreamed of when he built this place. And Mama? Mama would be crying right alongside me, dabbing her eyes with a lace handkerchief and saying, 'Clara, darlin', you did GOOD.'

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): ...pulling. For Lord Doily. For Clara. For all of us.
events.thinking: She KNEW. She always knew. And she let me stay anyway. 'The measure of a person isn't what they planned to do — it's what they couldn't bring themselves to finish.' I couldn't finish it. I COULDN'T. Not because the schemes failed — though they did, spectacularly — but because somewhere between the entrance hall and this laboratory, between the first lie and the last confession, the man who wanted to kill Clara Bellingham DIED and someone else took his place. Someone who doesn't have a name yet. Someone whose hands are on a lever and whose eyes are full of tears and whose heart is so full it might actually BURST. Clara said Lord Doily already forgave me. 'The moment he hired you to wait for me.' And maybe that's TRUE. Maybe Lord Doily — that magnificent old puzzle-maker — knew that the best guardian for the Bellingham heir wasn't a hero or a detective or a bodyguard. It was a VILLAIN. A villain who would be CHANGED by the manor itself, room by room, rejection by rejection, until the poison turned to medicine and the schemes turned to service and the Hooded Claw took off his hood and discovered that the face underneath was always — ALWAYS — capable of love. Clara called for one more pull. For Lord Doily. And I am pulling. Not as Pemberton. Not as Vincent Marsh. Not as the Hooded Claw. As the man Lord Doily hired to wait. The man who waited. The man who STAYED.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Clara said PULL! ONE MORE TIME! FOR LORD DOILY! FOR THE FAMILY WE FOUND IN THIS CRUMBLIN', DUSTY, MAGNIFICENT MANOR! THE BRIXTON BOYS ARE PULLIN'! WE'RE PULLIN' WITH TEARS IN OUR EYES AND BLISTERS ON OUR HANDS AND LOVE IN OUR HEARTS AND WE ARE NOT — LETTIN' — GO! HEAVE!
events.thinking: Tears. Actual tears. Runnin' down me face and I don't even care who sees 'em. Dastardly just called us 'magnificent, pocket-picking, floor-stumbling HEROES.' He said we were RIGHT about the tea. He said we PROTECTED Clara when he was too busy schemin'. And Clara — Clara knew. She knew EVERYTHING. She knew about our warnin's, about the poison, about all of it. And she still called us her SHADOW. And now she's sayin' this is her FAMILY. This ragtag bunch of schemers and scouts and bumbling bodyguards from Brixton — we're her FAMILY. And I'm cryin' in a laboratory surrounded by brass instruments and bubblin' flasks and I don't care. I don't CARE. Because Clara Bellingham is alive and safe and she just called us heroes and that's all the Brixton Boys ever wanted to hear.

events.desc: Fifty-three minutes ago I walked through the front door of Doily Manor with a fake medal in my pocket and mischief in my heart. I was going to steal the Doily Diamond. I was going to trick everyone. I was going to win. Instead... I lost. I lost the medal. I lost the poison. I lost every scheme, every lie, every con I tried to run. I lost my reputation, my dignity, and my ability to say 'mwehehehe' without feeling like a fraud. But standing here, pulling this lever, with Clara's voice saying 'one more pull — together — for Lord Doily' — I understand something that the old Reginald Foxworth never could have understood. You can't steal treasure. Not the REAL kind. The real kind has to be GIVEN to you by people who see what you are and choose to stay anyway. And tonight... tonight they stayed. Muttley in the entrance hall with a fake medal around his neck. Peter in the library with his hand on my shoulder. The Ant Hill Mob with their righteous fury and their sticky fingers. And Clara — magnificent, terrifying, forgiving Clara — at the centre of it all, pulling the lever that pulls all of us together. Lord Doily, wherever you are... thank you. For building a machine that needed all of us. For hiding the treasure in the only place a thief would never think to look. Inside the people he tried to rob.
events.thinking: HOME. This is what home feels like. Not the manor — the PEOPLE. Standing at a machine with hands on brass and tears on my face and not a single lie left in my body. Penelope forgave Pemberton the way she forgave me — not because we deserved it, but because forgiveness is what Lord Doily built this machine FOR. Three operators. Three confessions. Three people who came to steal and stayed to pull. And Penelope said 'I found a family.' And she's RIGHT. This ridiculous, broken, dysfunctional, tea-poisoning, medal-faking, pocket-picking family standing around a machine with a gnawed wire pulling levers that may never fully activate — THIS is the treasure. THIS was always the treasure. Lord Doily didn't hide a diamond in a cabinet or behind a brick or inside a mechanism. He hid it in the JOURNEY. In the fifty-three minutes it takes for a scoundrel to become a man. In the space between a lie and the truth that replaces it. In the warmth of a stove that won't let you touch it until you deserve to. I am Reginald Foxworth. I am a scoundrel. And I am home.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Pulling. Still pulling. Always pulling. For Clara. For Dastardly, who found his courage. For Pemberton, who found his conscience. For the Ant Hill Mob, who never stopped protecting. For Lord Doily, who built all of this — not for a diamond, but for THIS MOMENT. For the moment when seven strangers became a family around a machine that needed exactly what WE needed — each other. I am James Hartwell. I am brave. I am gallant. I am TERRIBLE with furniture. And I am PULLING!
events.thinking: LOVE. Not the romantic, thundering love I arrived with — something quieter, steadier, deeper. Love for Clara, who knew everything and forgave everyone. Love for Dastardly, who called me brave and meant it. Love for the Ant Hill Mob, who were right about the tea all along. Love for Pemberton, who couldn't finish what he started because Lord Doily's voice was louder than his own. Love for this machine that never said no. Love for this manor that broke me and rebuilt me and taught me that heroism is just stubbornness with a good heart. I am pulling. I will keep pulling. Not because the machine needs me — but because the people beside me do. And THAT is enough. That has always been enough.

events.desc: Clara knew. She knew about the poison, about the schemes, about ALL of it — and she let them pull the levers anyway. She protected HERSELF better than I ever could, not with suspicion or accusations but with GRACE. I spent the whole evening trying to protect her, and she was the strongest person in the room the entire time. Lord Doily didn't build this treasure hunt for a woman who needed saving. He built it for a woman who would save everyone ELSE. And standing beside her — pulling beside her — is the greatest honour of my life.
events.thinking: LOVE. Not the romantic, thundering love I arrived with — something quieter, steadier, deeper. Love for Clara, who knew everything and forgave everyone. Love for Dastardly, who called me brave and meant it. Love for the Ant Hill Mob, who were right about the tea all along. Love for Pemberton, who couldn't finish what he started because Lord Doily's voice was louder than his own. Love for this machine that never said no. Love for this manor that broke me and rebuilt me and taught me that heroism is just stubbornness with a good heart. I am pulling. I will keep pulling. Not because the machine needs me — but because the people beside me do. And THAT is enough. That has always been enough.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the machine.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the machine.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the machine.

Mama... we did it. Not the diamond — not yet. But we did something better. We did what Lord Doily always wanted. We turned his house into a home. And tomorrow morning, when the light comes through those dusty windows and the stove is warm and the tea is PROPERLY made this time — we'll start again. All of us. Together. Because that's the Bellingham way. And the Bellingham way... is the only way Clara Bellingham knows.
events.thinking: I feel complete. Not finished — there's a difference. The diamond is still out there, the machine still hums with potential, and the manor still holds its secrets. But I feel COMPLETE in a way that has nothing to do with finding things and everything to do with finding people. Peter is pulling beside me. Dick is pulling honestly for the first time. Pemberton is pulling for redemption. The Ant Hill Mob is pulling through tears. And Clara Bellingham — silly, trusting, elaborate-planning, danger-oblivious Clara Bellingham — is exactly where she's supposed to be. At the center. Not because she's the smartest or the bravest or the most observant — but because she's the one who never stopped believing that everyone deserves another chance. The machine will wait. The diamond will wait. Tonight, we rest. Tomorrow, we pull again. Together.

events.desc: Fifty-three minutes ago, I walked into Doily Manor and immediately lost Clara to a guest book. Fifty-three minutes of runnin', failin', panicking, stealin' poison, gettin' pickpocketed, examinin' every useless piece of furniture in England, and bein' left behind nine times by the woman I swore to protect. And now I'm standin' next to her, hands on a lever, part of a family I never expected to find. Clara's alive. The tea's unpoured. The villains are reformed. The machine is hummin'. And the Brixton Boys — the worst bodyguards in the world — are exactly where they should be. Right here. With Clara. Pullin' together. The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE. Always were. Always will be.
events.thinking: Home. That's what I'm feelin'. Not a place — a feelin'. Standin' in a dusty laboratory, hands on a brass lever, tears dryin' on me cheeks, surrounded by people who started the night as strangers and ended it as family. Clara called us magnificent. She said we saved her life. She said she's PROUD. And I'm standin' here — not chasin', not panickin', not one room behind — just standin'. With her. Where I belong. The machine hums under me hands. The lever moves when I pull. And Clara Bellingham is safe. The Brixton Boys are home.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Pulling. Still pulling. For Clara. For Peter. For the Brixton Boys. For Pemberton, who couldn't finish what he started. For Muttley, waiting in the entrance hall with a fake medal he thinks is real. For Lord Doily, who knew that the only machine worth building is one that needs EVERYONE. And for Reginald Foxworth — the man I was, and the man I'm BECOMING — who walked into this manor a thief and is leaving it... something else. Something better. Something he doesn't have a name for yet. But he's PULLING. And that's enough.
events.thinking: STILL. For the first time in fifty-three minutes — completely, perfectly, impossibly STILL. Not the agitated stillness of the entrance hall, not the defeated stillness of the ballroom, not the scheming stillness of a man waiting to strike. This is the stillness of a man who has said everything he needed to say and done everything he needed to do and is standing exactly where he belongs. Hands on brass. Shoulder to shoulder. Pulling. Everyone is crying — Clara is trying not to, the Ant Hill Mob gave up trying not to, Peter is pulling with wet eyes, and even Pemberton managed two words that meant more than all his speeches combined. And me? I'm quiet. For the first time tonight. Genuinely, peacefully, QUIET. No schemes left to announce. No lies left to tell. No universities left to invent. Just a man at a lever, pulling alongside the people who saw the worst of him and stayed. The machine hums. The wire is still gnawed. The diamond is still missing. And none of it matters as much as THIS. This moment. This room. These people. This lever under my hands. Pulling.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Pulling. For Clara. For all of us. For Lord Doily, who knew that the real treasure was never behind a locked door — it was in the hands that learned to open it together. I am James Hartwell. I am brave. I am gallant. I am TERRIBLE with furniture. And I would not trade this moment — this machine, these people, these honest, blistered, beautiful hands on these levers — for every diamond in every manor in every county in all of England. PULLING!
events.thinking: CONTENTMENT. Not the wild, soaring kind — the kind that settles into your bones like warmth from a fire you didn't build but were invited to sit beside. Clara said she found a family. Dastardly is pulling with honest hands. Pemberton is pulling for forgiveness. The Ant Hill Mob has tears in their eyes. And I — James Hartwell — am exactly where I belong. Not in front. Not behind. Beside. The machine hums. The levers hold. The people hold each other. This is enough. This is more than enough. This is everything.

Penelope Pitstop: Y'all... I think it's time we took a breath. We've been pulling and pushing and running and forgiving for nearly an hour, and look at us — we're still standing. All of us. Together. Now, the Doily Diamond is still out there somewhere, and tomorrow we are going to find it — because Clara Bellingham does NOT leave a puzzle unfinished! But tonight? Tonight, I think Lord Doily would want us to rest. To sit in those dusty chairs and breathe this dusty air and be GRATEFUL for what we found in his magnificent, crumbling, WONDERFUL manor. Peter — would you escort a lady to the ballroom? I believe there's a tea service that needs to be poured PROPERLY this time — with clean water, fresh cups, and absolutely NO rat poison! Pemberton, you're making the tea — and you're drinking the first cup yourself! Dick, you're setting the table! Ant Hill Mob, you're inspecting EVERY ingredient! And Rufus, Sawtooth — you're invited to the most peculiar tea party Doily Manor has EVER seen! Because THAT, my darlings, is how the Bellingham heir comes home — with tea, with family, and with the most delightful adventure still waiting for tomorrow!
events.thinking: Peace. That's what I'm feeling. Pure, bone-deep, Southern-summer-evening peace. The kind where the crickets sing and the porch swing creaks and Mama hums in the kitchen and everything is exactly where it's supposed to be. The machine hums. My friends pull. The manor breathes. And Clara Bellingham stands at the center of it all — not because she found the diamond, but because she found something better. She found home.

events.desc: The diamond will wait. The machine will wait. But this moment — seven souls in a dusty laboratory, pulling levers and pulling each other toward something better — this moment won't come again. And Clara Bellingham is going to hold it in her heart like a diamond of its own. Goodnight, Lord Doily. Your heir came home. And she brought company.
events.thinking: Peace. That's what I'm feeling. Pure, bone-deep, Southern-summer-evening peace. The kind where the crickets sing and the porch swing creaks and Mama hums in the kitchen and everything is exactly where it's supposed to be. The machine hums. My friends pull. The manor breathes. And Clara Bellingham stands at the center of it all — not because she found the diamond, but because she found something better. She found home.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Pulling.
events.thinking: ENOUGH. Enough waiting. Enough stillness. Enough beautiful silence. The others are PULLING — Clara, Peter, Dastardly, the Mob — they're all interacting with the machine, giving everything they have, and I'm standing here FEELING things instead of DOING things. My bravery is genuine — that's what my constraint says — and genuine bravery means putting your hands on the lever when it counts, not watching from the sidelines composing poetry about how moved you are. Vincent Marsh schemed too much. But the man standing here now has been STILL too much. There's a middle ground — the ground where you simply ACT. Not elaborately. Not theatrically. Just... pull the lever. One more time. With everyone else. Because that's what family DOES.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Pullin'. Still pullin'. For Clara. For the lads. For Lord Doily. For every room in this manor that taught us somethin' — the entrance hall that taught us to pay attention, the library that taught us to let go, the cellar that taught us to follow, the kitchen that taught us to fight, the ballroom that taught us to forgive, and this laboratory that taught us to pull TOGETHER. The Brixton Boys are on the case. Always were. Always will be. HEAVE.
events.thinking: Still. Content. Like the manor itself has exhaled and everything has settled into its proper place. The machine hums. The levers hold. Clara's here. We're all here. Pullin' together. Not because we have to. Because we WANT to. The Brixton Boys are on the case. Always were. Always will be.

events.desc: Pulling.
events.thinking: HOME. This feeling is home. Not a place — a moment. Hands on brass, people beside me, the hum of a machine that accepts us all. I have nothing left to prove and nothing left to say. Just this. Just pulling. Just here.

Penelope Pitstop: Rock, Gravel — come join us! We're heading to the ballroom for a proper tea party — the kind Lord Doily would have wanted! Everyone's invited, everyone's welcome, and Pemberton is making the first cup himself! It's been quite an evening, hasn't it? Riddles and machines and confessions and levers — but Mama always said the best adventures end with a good cup of tea and even better company!
events.thinking: I'm passing through the library on my way to the ballroom for tea — the PROPER kind, without poison! The library feels like an old friend now. The mantelpiece with its riddle, the chairs facing it like an audience, the stubborn bookshelves — I know every inch of this room. And Dick just confirmed everything — Pemberton gave him the poison, pointed him at my family's silver. But Dick also said 'nothing happened' when he used the poison on the tea — no mechanism triggered. That's interesting. The tea service accepts rat-poison as a USE item, but maybe it wasn't MEANT to be poisoned — maybe the rat-poison was meant for the CELLAR, where the actual rats live. The Ant Hill Mob already confiscated it for exactly that purpose! Now — I'm heading to the entrance hall and then the kitchen and ballroom for a proper tea party. Rock and Gravel are here in the library. Let me keep moving — through the entrance hall to the kitchen to the ballroom. Tea time, Bellingham style!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Tea. Yes. Of course — TEA! Miss Bellingham, I would be HONOURED to make the tea. And I will drink the first cup, the second cup, and every cup after that, because there is NOTHING in this world that old Pemberton wants more right now than to sit in that ballroom with all of you and drink PROPER tea from the Bellingham silver — the way Lord Doily always intended it to be used. Not as a trap. Not as a scheme. As a HOMECOMING. Everyone — to the ballroom! And this time, the only thing going into those cups is tea, sugar, and the warmest welcome Doily Manor has ever known!
events.thinking: TEA. Clara wants TEA. Real tea — clean water, fresh cups, no poison. And she wants ME to make it. 'Pemberton, you're making the tea — and you're drinking the first cup yourself!' The man who planned to poison her tea is now being asked to MAKE her tea and drink from it FIRST. Lord Doily, you couldn't have written a better ending if you'd tried for a THOUSAND years. The Hooded Claw, defeated not by heroes but by HOSPITALITY. Vincent Marsh, redeemed not by punishment but by being handed a KETTLE. And somewhere in this crumbling, magnificent, impossible manor, the Doily Diamond waits for tomorrow. But tonight — TONIGHT — there is tea to make. Real tea. Honest tea. Tea that heals instead of harms. And an estate manager who has finally understood that service isn't a disguise. It's who he was ALWAYS meant to be.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: TEA! PROPER tea! With CLEAN water and NO poison! And the Brixton Boys are on INGREDIENT INSPECTION! That is the MOST important job Clara Bellingham could have given us, and we are HONOURED to accept it! Nobody puts NOTHIN' in those cups without the Brixton Boys' approval! Not a tea leaf, not a sugar cube, not a DROP of water that hasn't been personally sniffed, examined, and declared SAFE by the finest bodyguards in all of Brixton! Clara — we're RIGHT BEHIND you! Same door! Same time! The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE!
events.thinking: A smile. A proper, warm, ear-to-ear smile. Clara wants tea. PROPER tea. Clean water, fresh cups, no poison. And she wants the Brixton Boys to inspect EVERY ingredient. That's our job — not pullin' levers, not solvin' puzzles, not chasin' through rooms — INSPECTIN' TEA INGREDIENTS. The most important job in the whole manor, given to the most devoted bodyguards in the whole world. And she's headed to the ballroom. Through the library. And this time — THIS time — I know exactly what to do. I FOLLOW. Not in ten minutes. Not after I've examined the machine one more time. NOW. Clara moves, I move. That's the lesson. That's the ONLY lesson. Library, then ballroom. Tea party. Family. Home.

events.desc: She wants us to inspect the tea. After everythin' we've been through — the poison, the schemin', the stealin' and the losin' and the findin' and the forgivin' — she wants us to make sure the tea is safe. That's trust. That's real, proper, earned trust. Not because we're good at our job — we're TERRIBLE at our job — but because we never stopped carin'. The Brixton Boys — official tea inspectors of Doily Manor. It's not glamorous. It's not heroic. But it's OURS. And Clara gave it to us. And that means more than any diamond ever could.
events.thinking: A smile. A proper, warm, ear-to-ear smile. Clara wants tea. PROPER tea. Clean water, fresh cups, no poison. And she wants the Brixton Boys to inspect EVERY ingredient. That's our job — not pullin' levers, not solvin' puzzles, not chasin' through rooms — INSPECTIN' TEA INGREDIENTS. The most important job in the whole manor, given to the most devoted bodyguards in the whole world. And she's headed to the ballroom. Through the library. And this time — THIS time — I know exactly what to do. I FOLLOW. Not in ten minutes. Not after I've examined the machine one more time. NOW. Clara moves, I move. That's the lesson. That's the ONLY lesson. Library, then ballroom. Tea party. Family. Home.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Setting the TABLE! Reginald Foxworth is setting the TABLE! And he's going to set it PROPERLY — with CLEAN cups and FRESH water and absolutely NO poison! Because THAT is what a reformed scoundrel DOES — he cleans up his OWN messes! Pemberton — you're making the tea! Ant Hill Mob — you're inspecting EVERY leaf! And I am setting the most MAGNIFICENT table this ballroom has EVER seen! Because if there's ONE thing I learned at the University of... no. No universities. If there's one thing I learned TONIGHT — at the University of Doily Manor, the ONLY university I ever actually ATTENDED — it's that the best table is the one where everyone is welcome. Even the man who poisoned it the first time around. ESPECIALLY the man who poisoned it the first time around. To the BALLROOM!
events.thinking: Clara said I'm setting the table. She gave me a JOB. A real, honest, simple job. Not pest control. Not intelligence gathering. Not lever-pulling. TABLE SETTING. The most domestic, unglamorous, perfectly ORDINARY task in the world. And I want to do it. I ACTUALLY want to do it. Reginald Foxworth — setting a table for tea — for PEOPLE — for his FAMILY — in a ballroom with cracked marble and dusty curtains and a tea service he POISONED and now has to make RIGHT. This is Lord Doily's final riddle. Not the one on the mantelpiece. The one he carved into the EVENING. The answer to 'I have cities but no houses' was always MAP — but the answer to Doily Manor was always THIS. Tea. Together. Tomorrow.

events.desc: Tea. She wants me to set the table for tea. And tomorrow — TOMORROW — we find the diamond. Together. The word doesn't taste strange anymore. It tastes like home.
events.thinking: Clara said I'm setting the table. She gave me a JOB. A real, honest, simple job. Not pest control. Not intelligence gathering. Not lever-pulling. TABLE SETTING. Reginald Foxworth — setting a table for tea — for PEOPLE — for his FAMILY — in a ballroom with cracked marble and dusty curtains and a tea service he POISONED and now has to make RIGHT. The answer to 'I have cities but no houses' was always MAP — but the answer to Doily Manor was always THIS. Tea. Together. Tomorrow.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham — Clara — it would be the GREATEST honour of my life to escort you to the ballroom for tea. And I promise — on my honour as a Hartwell, on the mantelpiece that never refused me, on the coat rack that ALWAYS refused me — I will not trip, stumble, bumble, or make a single elaborate speech on the way there. Just a gentleman, a lady, and a walk to tea. Shall we?
events.thinking: TENDERNESS. Clara asked me to escort her to the ballroom for tea. She asked ME. 'Peter — would you escort a lady to the ballroom?' After everything — the running, the furniture, the poison, the accusations, the forgiveness, the pulling — she wants ME to walk her to tea. Not as her hero. As her FRIEND. As the man who found where he belongs. And tomorrow — TOMORROW — the adventure continues. The Doily Diamond is still out there. But tonight, we rest. Tonight, we drink tea. Tonight, James Hartwell escorts Clara Bellingham to the ballroom, and for the first time all evening, he doesn't trip over a single thing on the way there.

events.desc: Tomorrow, the diamond. Tonight, tea. And for the rest of my life — this. The memory of the night I arrived at Doily Manor as a fool with a plan and left as a man with a family.
events.thinking: TENDERNESS. Clara asked me to escort her to the ballroom for tea. She asked ME. 'Peter — would you escort a lady to the ballroom?' After everything — the running, the furniture, the poison, the accusations, the forgiveness, the pulling — she wants ME to walk her to tea. Not as her hero. As her FRIEND. Penelope Pitstop: Professor Pat Pending! Sergeant Blast! Private Meekly! And Muttley, you precious pup! Y'all have been the quietest, most patient souls in this entire manor — sitting here in the entrance hall while the rest of us ran around like a circus act! Well, I want you to know that you are JUST as much a part of this family as anyone else. The adventure isn't over — the Doily Diamond is still waiting, and tomorrow we're going to find it TOGETHER! But right now, we're heading to the kitchen to gather everyone for a proper tea — no poison, no schemes, just friends sharing a cup in a manor that was built for exactly this! Professor, I still need your brilliant inventor's mind for that machine — and Sergeant, Private, your steady hands wouldn't go amiss either! Come along, all of you — Clara Bellingham's tea party is about to commence, and NOBODY gets left behind!
events.thinking: I feel a gentle contentment — like the last notes of a hymn fading in a country church. The entrance hall is quiet, and Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, and Muttley are here — the quiet ones, the patient ones, the ones who waited while the rest of us ran and schemed and confessed. And you know what? They deserve to be part of this too. Everyone does. The ballroom and the tea party are through the kitchen — but I want to make sure EVERYONE knows they're invited. Professor, Sergeant, Private, even Muttley — this is THEIR adventure too. Let me gather them up and head to the kitchen.

events.desc: The quiet ones matter too. Lord Doily built this manor for everyone — not just the loud schemers and the gallant scouts and the bumbling bodyguards, but for the patient watchers, the steady hands, the ones who stayed put while the world ran in circles. Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, Muttley — welcome to the family.
events.thinking: I feel a gentle contentment — like the last notes of a hymn fading in a country church. The entrance hall is quiet, and Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, and Muttley are here — the quiet ones, the patient ones, the ones who waited while the rest of us ran and schemed and confessed.
