events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Coming through, everyone — tea won't make itself! Through the entrance hall, into the kitchen — kettle on, water fresh, cups clean! Clara wants a proper Doily Manor tea party, and by GOD she's going to GET one! Follow me when you're ready — the ballroom will be set for the finest tea service this manor has seen since Lord Doily himself sat at that table!
events.thinking: PURPOSE. Simple, clear, undeniable PURPOSE. Clara wants tea. REAL tea. And the kitchen is through the entrance hall. I know this manor like the back of my hand — I've walked every corridor, examined every object, mapped every connection. And now all of that knowledge serves one PURPOSE: making tea for the family I found in the ruins of my schemes. The stove is warm. The copper pots are ready. The water needs fetching. And old Pemberton — the REAL Pemberton, the one who was always underneath Vincent Marsh's mask — knows how to make a proper cup of tea. He's been making tea in this kitchen for YEARS. This is not a scheme. This is not a plan. This is a man walking to a kitchen to put a kettle on. The simplest thing in the world. The thing he should have done from the very beginning.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Comin' through! Entrance hall! Kitchen! Ballroom! Tea party! INGREDIENT INSPECTION! The Brixton Boys do NOT stop in libraries! We have LEARNED!
events.thinking: Clara's gone ahead — through the entrance hall toward the kitchen and ballroom. Tea party. And I'm in the library again. But this time I'm not stoppin'. This time the library is just a room I walk THROUGH. Entrance hall. Kitchen. Ballroom. That's where the tea party is. That's where Clara is. MOVE.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Just passing through, gentlemen! On my way to the ballroom — I have a TABLE to set! Clara's orders! And I intend to set the most SPECTACULAR table this manor has ever seen! Napkins folded into SWANS! Cups arranged in ORDER of height! Sugar bowl positioned at PRECISELY the correct angle! Because if Reginald Foxworth is going to do honest work for the first time in his life, he's going to do it with UNNECESSARY FLAIR! That is the Foxworth way — we over-prepare, we over-commit, and our thoroughness creates complications that our determination then RESOLVES! Now — to the kitchen for clean water, then to the ballroom for table setting! Peter — you coming? I could use an escort! A reformed scoundrel should never travel ALONE — he might RELAPSE!
events.thinking: WARMTH. Passing through the library on my way to set a table for tea and the riddle catches my eye one last time. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' A map. I knew the answer an hour ago. But now I know the OTHER answer — the one Lord Doily didn't carve in stone because it had to be lived. I have rooms but no walls. I have people but no strangers. I have a family but no name for what we are. What am I? Doily Manor. And I'm passing through its heart — this library, these chairs, this riddle — on my way to do the most honest work of my life. Setting a table. For tea. For everyone.

events.desc: The library. The two chairs. The riddle. I'm walking THROUGH this time, not stopping. Not examining. Not scheming. Just... passing through on my way to set a table. And the chairs don't feel empty anymore. They feel like they're waiting. For tomorrow. For all of us. For tea.
events.thinking: WARMTH. Passing through the library on my way to set a table for tea and the riddle catches my eye one last time. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' A map. I knew the answer an hour ago. But now I know the OTHER answer — the one Lord Doily didn't carve in stone because it had to be lived. I have rooms but no walls. I have people but no strangers. I have a family but no name for what we are. What am I? Doily Manor. And I'm passing through its heart — this library, these chairs, this riddle — on my way to do the most honest work of my life. Setting a table. For tea. For everyone.

events.desc: The library. The mantelpiece. The riddle. Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. A map. The answer was always a map — and tonight, this manor drew one across my heart. Every room a landmark. Every failure a compass point. Every person a destination I didn't know I was heading for. Goodnight, library. Goodnight, riddle. Goodnight, bookshelves that never budged. I'll see you tomorrow.
events.thinking: QUIET GRACE. Passing through the library one last time — the room where it all began. The mantelpiece with its riddle. The bookshelves that never budged. The two chairs facing each other like old friends. I don't need to touch anything. I don't need to interact or examine or solve. I just need to walk through, tip my hat to the room that taught me patience, and keep going to the entrance hall and then the kitchen and then the ballroom where Clara is waiting for tea. Simple. Quiet. No speeches. Just walking.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now... the kitchen is quiet. Just me and the stove and that stubborn locked cabinet. You know, Mama used to say that every good kitchen tells you everything you need to know about the family that lived there. And this one — with its warm stove and copper pots and a cabinet that's keeping its secrets just a little while longer — tells me that Lord Doily was a man who believed in warmth, in gathering, in bringing people to the table. And tonight, that is EXACTLY what we're going to do. The ballroom is right through that door, the tea service is set, and for the first time all evening, every single person in this manor is ready to sit down TOGETHER — not as schemers and protectors and rivals, but as FAMILY. Come on, Clara — one more door. The best door of the evening. The one that leads to tea!
events.thinking: The kitchen is quiet — I'm alone for the first time in a while. Just me, the warm stove, and that locked cabinet with its brass lock. The cabinet that's been waiting patiently all evening for a key I still haven't found. And you know what? There's something peaceful about being alone in this kitchen. The stove is warm. The copper pots gleam. The preparation table stretches out like an invitation. This is Lord Doily's kitchen — the hearth of the home he built for my family. And even without the key, even without the diamond, I feel like I belong here. The ballroom is through that door, and the tea party awaits. But for just one moment, let me stand here in the warmth and be grateful. Then — onward to the ballroom, where everyone will gather and the evening will end the way it should: together.

events.desc: One hour at Doily Manor. Six rooms explored. One riddle solved. Zero items found. One machine pulled. Two confessions heard. Two schemers redeemed. One family forged. And one Clara Bellingham... home. The diamond will wait. The cabinet will wait. The adventure continues tomorrow. But tonight — tea.
events.thinking: The kitchen is quiet — I'm alone for the first time in a while. Just me, the warm stove, and that locked cabinet with its brass lock. The cabinet that's been waiting patiently all evening for a key I still haven't found. And you know what? There's something peaceful about being alone in this kitchen. The stove is warm. events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: Peter's words from twelve minutes ago echo through me — the confrontation about the chandelier, the accusation about the tea, the FURY in his gallant voice. He was RIGHT. About everything. I WAS inspecting that chandelier for murderous purposes. I DID give Dastardly the poison. I DID suggest he use it on Clara's tea. And Peter — magnificent, watchful, CORRECT Peter — saw through me when it mattered most. But that was twelve minutes ago. Before I confessed. Before Clara forgave me. Before the machine. Before the levers. Before 'pulling — for Lord Doily, for Clara, for all of us.' I have ALREADY answered for these sins. Clara KNOWS. She said 'I forgive you' and 'Pemberton, you too.' And now she wants TEA — real tea, honest tea — and she wants ME to make it. Peter's accusation was JUST. My confession was TRUE. Clara's forgiveness was REAL. And now I am walking to the kitchen to put a kettle on. Not because I'm running from Peter's anger. Because I'm walking toward Clara's trust. To the kitchen. Simple. Direct. No schemes. Just tea.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Kitchen! Ballroom! Tea inspection! NOT STOPPIN'!
events.thinking: Kitchen. Clara's in the kitchen, or on her way to the ballroom for tea. Peter just shouted about the CHANDELIER — Sneekly was fiddlin' with it! The chandelier that's been hangin' 'precariously' since we walked in! Another danger — another threat to Clara — and Peter caught it! Good man, Peter. But Sneekly's back in the library now, away from the chandelier. And I need to get to the KITCHEN. Clara said tea party. Ballroom. Through the kitchen. Don't stop. Don't examine the guest book — DEFINITELY don't examine the guest book. That guest book started all me problems fifty-four minutes ago. Kitchen. Ballroom. Clara. Tea. MOVE.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Muttley! I'm BACK! And I see you're still wearing that medal — GOOD boy! Guard it with your LIFE! Now — everyone! Clara has called for TEA in the ballroom! PROPER tea! No poison! No schemes! Just cups and saucers and CIVILISED CONVERSATION! I am heading to the kitchen to fetch clean water — yes, ME, Reginald Foxworth, fetching WATER like a BUTLER — because Clara said I'm setting the table and I have NEVER been more honoured by a DOMESTIC ASSIGNMENT in my LIFE! Peter — Pemberton — Ant Hill Mob — when you're ready, make your way to the ballroom! We have a tea party to prepare and a TOMORROW to plan! The Doily Diamond isn't going ANYWHERE, and neither are WE!
events.thinking: CONTENTMENT. Simple, quiet, unfamiliar contentment. The entrance hall — where it all began — and everyone is HERE. Muttley with my fake medal. Peter at my side. Pemberton, reformed. The Ant Hill Mob, watchful. The Professor, the Sergeant, the Private. Everyone converging on the same place, the same purpose. Tea. And I'm on my way to the kitchen to fetch clean water, because Clara told me to set the table and a Foxworth keeps his WORD now. The word feels real. The promise feels real. The kitchen — the room I chased all evening, the room I was SURE held the diamond, the room with the warm stove and the locked cabinet and the preparation table — I'm going back to it. Not to scheme. Not to search. To fetch WATER. For TEA. For FAMILY. And that is the most Reginald Foxworth thing I have ever done — because a Foxworth's plans are always overly elaborate, and the most elaborate plan of all turned out to be the simplest one: show up, tell the truth, and set the table.

events.desc: One hour ago I walked through this door a thief. Now I'm walking through it a table-setter. And somehow — impossibly, ridiculously, MAGNIFICENTLY — the table-setter is the better man.
events.thinking: CONTENTMENT. Simple, quiet, unfamiliar contentment. The entrance hall — where it all began — and everyone is HERE. Muttley with my fake medal. Peter at my side. Pemberton, reformed. The Ant Hill Mob, watchful. The Professor, the Sergeant, the Private. Everyone converging on the same place, the same purpose. Tea. And I'm on my way to the kitchen to fetch clean water, because Clara told me to set the table and a Foxworth keeps his WORD now. The word feels real. The promise feels real. Penelope Pitstop: The ballroom! Oh, look at this table — set for tea, set for EVERYONE, set for exactly this moment! Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear — you two have been the quietest guests at this party, and I want you to know that your patience is a GIFT! Now — I know the tea service has had a bit of an... adventure this evening. But we are NOT going to let one bad cup spoil the whole party! When everyone gets here, we'll clean these cups, pour fresh water from the kitchen, and have ourselves a PROPER Doily Manor tea! Because Lord Doily didn't set this table for poison and schemes — he set it for FAMILY! And tonight, for the first time in who knows how many years, this table is going to have a REAL family sitting around it! So pull up a chair, make yourselves comfortable, and get ready for the most unlikely, most wonderful, most DELIGHTFUL tea party in the history of English manor houses!
events.thinking: The ballroom. The tea service. The long dining table set for tea. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear are here — two more quiet souls who've been waiting patiently all evening. And the tea service — the Bellingham silver that Pemberton almost called by my family name — is sitting right there, beautiful and still. Dick said he contaminated it with rat poison, and the Ant Hill Mob confiscated the poison, and now Dick is talking about 'treating' the cups as pest control. But you know what? I'm not afraid. The tea may be tainted, but the GATHERING isn't. We can pour fresh water. We can clean the cups. What matters is that everyone sits down together at this table — the table Lord Doily set for guests who would become family. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear, you patient darlings — welcome to the party. Now we wait for the others to arrive, and when they do, we'll figure out the tea situation together. Because that's what this family does.

events.desc: The table is set. The cups are waiting. The family is scattered across the manor but they're all coming — I can feel it. Peter, Dick, Pemberton, the Ant Hill Mob, Rufus, Sawtooth, Professor, Sergeant, Private, Muttley, Rock, Gravel, Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear — every single soul in Doily Manor has a seat at this table. And when they arrive, Clara Bellingham is going to pour tea and tell them all what Mama would have said: 'Welcome home, darlin's. Welcome home.'

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Right then — kettle on! The stove is warm, the copper pots are clean, and Pemberton is making tea the way Lord Doily taught him — properly, honestly, and with enough cups for EVERYONE. Peter, would you fetch fresh water? Dick, set out the cups — CLEAN ones, from the shelf, not from the ballroom. Ant Hill Mob — you're on quality control. Taste-test everything before it goes to Miss Bellingham. And when it's ready, we'll carry it through to the ballroom and sit down — ALL of us — at Lord Doily's table, and drink tea together like the family he always wanted this manor to have. No poison. No schemes. Just tea.
events.thinking: PEACE. The kitchen. The stove. The warm heart of Doily Manor. And I am here to do the simplest, most honest thing a man can do — make tea. Not poisoned tea. Not scheming tea. Just TEA. The stove is warm. The copper pots gleam. Peter is watching — good, let him watch. Dastardly is here — good, let him help. The Mob is guarding — good, let them guard. Everyone is in the kitchen where the food is made and the warmth lives and the heart beats. And tomorrow — TOMORROW — Clara will find the Doily Diamond. But tonight, the estate manager makes tea.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Ballroom! Tea inspection! Clara's waitin'! NOT STOPPIN' IN THE KITCHEN!
events.thinking: Wait — 'Dick Dastardly slipped rat-poison out of ant-hill-mob's pocket.' AGAIN?! He pickpocketed me AGAIN?! But — wait — I didn't HAVE the poison. He stole it back from me ages ago. Did he... did he put it back and then steal it again? Or is the game just remindin' me what happened before? Either way — Clara's not here. She must be in the BALLROOM already. And Dastardly's HERE with the poison. And Sneekly's HERE. The ballroom is ONE ROOM AWAY. The tea service is in the ballroom. Clara's in the ballroom. The poison is HERE with Dastardly. But Dastardly CONFESSED. He APOLOGISED. He said he was DONE schemin'. Did he mean it? Or was that another con? Me gut says... me gut says he meant it. The tears were real. The words were real. But the poison is still in his pocket and the tea is still in the next room. And Clara's in the next room too. So what do I do? I go to the BALLROOM. I go to Clara. I inspect the tea. That's me job. That's what she ASKED me to do. Ballroom. NOW.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Right! The kitchen! My old NEMESIS! But tonight we are ALLIES, you and I! Pemberton — since you're here and you OWE me approximately seventeen favours for using me as your personal tea-poisoning accomplice — you can help me find clean water! The stove is warm, which means we can BOIL it! Peter — check those copper pots for anything USABLE! Ant Hill Mob — I know you're watching me, and for ONCE I am grateful for your vigilance! Inspect EVERYTHING! Make sure there's not a DROP of poison anywhere near our tea supplies! Clara wants a PROPER tea party and by GOD she is going to GET one! The man who contaminated the Bellingham silver is going to CLEAN the Bellingham silver, and he's going to do it with his OWN two hands, and he's going to do it RIGHT! Now — to the BALLROOM! Table won't set ITSELF!
events.thinking: The stove is still warm. After everything — an hour of chaos and confession and levers and lies — the stove is still warm. Someone is still tending it. Someone always was. And now I'm here to tend something too. Not a fire. A table. For people who forgave me. The kitchen feels different now. Not a crime scene. Not a puzzle box. Just a kitchen. A place where someone makes tea for someone else. And tonight, that someone is me.

events.desc: The stove is warm. It was always warm. Even when it wouldn't let me touch it. Even when I didn't deserve its warmth. It was keeping the kitchen ready for this moment — the moment when someone came back not to search, not to scheme, but to SERVE. Lord Doily, you magnificent old riddle-maker — you hid the heart of the manor in the simplest place of all. In a warm stove. In a kitchen. In the act of making tea for people you love. I understand now. I understand EVERYTHING. And tomorrow, when we come back for the diamond... I'll bring the kettle on.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: The ballroom, everyone! Clara is waiting, and a Hartwell NEVER keeps a Bellingham waiting for tea!
events.thinking: WARMTH. The stove is still warm. The kitchen smells like home. The ballroom is one door away, and Clara is waiting with tea cups and family and tomorrow. Pemberton, Dastardly, the Ant Hill Mob — they're all here, all walking the same direction, all heading to the same table. No more schemes. No more poison. No more suspicion. Just tea. Just us. Just the most peculiar, imperfect, BEAUTIFUL family that ever pulled levers in a crumbling manor. One more door, James. One more door.

events.desc: Cups for everyone. That's what the tea service always said. Cups for everyone. And for the first time tonight... everyone is here to drink from them.

events.desc: An hour ago I walked into this manor determined to impress Clara Bellingham with heroism and gallantry. I have been defeated by every piece of furniture, outmanoeuvred by an estate manager, outpaced by the woman I was trying to protect, and humbled by a confidence trickster who turned out to be braver than me. And yet — here I am. At the table. Raising a cup. Beside the most extraordinary woman I have ever known. And she is smiling. And the tea is clean. And tomorrow, the adventure continues. James Hartwell — brave, gallant, TERRIBLE with furniture — has come home.

Penelope Pitstop: All right, all right — the Ant Hill Mob is RIGHT, these cups need cleaning before anyone drinks a DROP! Fresh water, fresh cups from the kitchen — Dick, you handle that, since you OWE these cups a fresh start! And Peter — I accept that toast, and I raise one right back: to Lord Doily, who built a house of riddles and filled it with doors that only open together. To Pemberton, who lied his way to the truth. To Dick, who schemed his way to honesty. To the Ant Hill Mob, who guarded me with everything they had and then some. To Peter, who found where he belongs. To Rufus and Sawtooth and the Professor and the Sergeant and the Private and Muttley and the Slags and Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear — to EVERYONE who walked through that front door tonight! And to the Doily Diamond — still out there, still waiting, still OURS to find... TOMORROW! Now — Dick Dastardly told me to SIT DOWN, and for the first time all evening, I am going to do what someone else tells me to do. Clara Bellingham is SITTING!
events.thinking: Joy. Pure, uncomplicated, bubbling-over JOY. Everyone is here — Pemberton arrived too! Peter wants to toast. Dick is setting the table and telling ME to sit down for once. The Ant Hill Mob is guarding the tea with their lives. And I am surrounded by people who, one hour ago, were strangers and schemers and bumbling bodyguards — and who are now, without question, the most wonderful, chaotic, beautiful family a girl could ask for. Dick told me to SIT DOWN and let someone else work for once. And you know what? He's RIGHT. Clara Bellingham has been running, planning, examining, charming, forgiving, and leading for a solid hour. It's time to sit. It's time to let them take care of ME for a change. And Mama would approve — because Mama knew that the hardest thing for a Bellingham woman is letting someone else hold the reins.

events.desc: Sitting down. Letting go. Letting them take care of me. The hardest thing a Bellingham woman can do — and the most important. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Your heir is home. And tomorrow? Tomorrow the adventure continues.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I'm here. The Ant Hill Mob is right — those cups are contaminated, and that's MY doing. But we don't need the Bellingham silver to have a proper tea party. Lord Doily kept plain kitchen cups in the cabinet by the stove — simple, honest, unchipped mugs that he used every morning. I'll fetch them. And when I pour from them, I'll drink first — every cup, every pot — because that's what Clara asked, and that's what this manor's estate manager DOES. He serves. Not with silver. With care. Now — who's sitting where? Clara at the head. Peter to her right. Dick to her left. The Mob wherever they can see EVERYTHING. And old Pemberton... Pemberton sits wherever there's room. There's always room at Lord Doily's table.
events.thinking: I'm here. The ballroom. The poisoned tea service. The cracked marble. The family I made out of the people I tried to destroy. Peter just toasted Clara as 'the treasure of Doily Manor — the real one, the only one that matters.' Dastardly is setting the table with genuine care. The Ant Hill Mob is guarding the contaminated silver with fierce love. And I — the man who contaminated it — am walking through the door to sit down with all of them. The Mob is right — the Bellingham silver is done. Those cups carry my worst mistake and they always will. But Dick said we'll find FRESH cups. CLEAN water. Start from SCRATCH. And that's what we're doing. All of us. Starting from scratch. In a ballroom with a cracked marble floor and dusty curtains and a long dining table set for tea. Set for US.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right then! Fresh cups, fresh water — the Brixton Boys are INSPECTIN'! Dastardly — you bring the cups from the kitchen, and I will personally SNIFF, EXAMINE, and APPROVE every single one before Clara so much as LOOKS at it! Peter — you're on water duty! Boil it fresh from the stove, bring it here, and the Brixton Boys will test it! And if ANYONE — and I mean ANYONE — tries to add ANYTHIN' to those cups that isn't tea, water, or sugar, the Brixton Boys will know about it! Because THAT is our job! Not pullin' levers, not solvin' riddles, not chasin' through rooms — INSPECTIN' TEA! And we are VERY GOOD at it! We may be the worst bodyguards in history, but we are about to become the BEST tea inspectors this manor has EVER seen! Clara Bellingham is havin' her tea party, and it is gonna be SAFE, CLEAN, and POISON-FREE! The Brixton Boys GUARANTEE it!
events.thinking: Dastardly's talkin' about FRESH cups and CLEAN water. He KNOWS the old service is poisoned — he ADMITTED it earlier. And now he's sayin' to start fresh. And Peter just interacted with the tea service — maybe to check it, maybe to clear it. And Dastardly's settin' the table and offerin' to bring Clara tea from clean cups. Maybe — MAYBE — the confession was real after all. Maybe he poisoned it before, felt terrible about it, and now he's tryin' to make it right with fresh cups. And Clara said the same thing — clean water, fresh cups, no poison. So maybe this is what it looks like when broken people try to fix things. New cups. New water. New start. But the Brixton Boys are STILL inspectin' every ingredient. That's our job. That's what Clara asked us to do. And we're doin' it. Right here. In the same room. At the same time. Together.

events.desc: Fresh cups. Clean water. A new start. For the tea, and for all of us. Clara forgave the schemers. The schemers confessed their sins. And the Brixton Boys — the worst bodyguards, the best tea inspectors — are standin' guard over the most peculiar tea party in the history of English country houses. Every cup checked. Every drop verified. Every ingredient approved. Because that's what love looks like when you're the Ant Hill Mob — not grand gestures, not clever plans, just makin' sure the tea is safe. One cup at a time. For Clara. Always for Clara.
events.thinking: Dastardly's talkin' about FRESH cups and CLEAN water. He KNOWS the old service is poisoned — he ADMITTED it earlier. And now he's sayin' to start fresh. And Peter just interacted with the tea service — maybe to check it, maybe to clear it. And Dastardly's settin' the table and offerin' to bring Clara tea from clean cups. events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Table is SET! Cups are ARRANGED! The Bellingham silver is GLEAMING — or it WILL be, once Pemberton gives it a proper polish! Now — everyone SITS! Clara at the head, because this is HER manor and HER silver and HER family's name on every piece! Peter to her RIGHT, because a scout belongs at the leader's side! Ant Hill Mob to her LEFT, because a bodyguard belongs CLOSE! Pemberton — you're making the tea and drinking FIRST! Luke, Bear — you're GUESTS of HONOUR for putting up with my RANTING earlier! And I — Reginald Foxworth — will sit at the FAR end. The scoundrel's seat. Where I can see EVERYONE and everyone can see ME. Because I have NOTHING left to hide. Not a single scheme, not a single lie, not a single fake university. Just empty pockets, honest hands, and a cup of tea I didn't POISON this time. To DOILY MANOR! To TOMORROW! And to the most MAGNIFICENT, CATASTROPHIC, BEAUTIFUL evening of my ENTIRE life!
events.thinking: PEACE. Real peace. My hands on the Bellingham silver — the silver I poisoned, the silver I'm now cleaning, the silver that will hold clean tea for the family I found — and the circle is complete. I ruined this. I'm fixing this. Not because I have to. Because I WANT to. And wanting to fix what you broke is the closest thing to redemption a Foxworth will ever know.

events.desc: Cups for everyone. Set by the hands that poisoned them. Cleaned by the same hands that ruined them. Raised by the man who walked in a thief and sat down a friend. Lord Doily... I think I finally understand your riddle. Not the one on the mantelpiece. The OTHER one. The one that takes an hour and a manor and a broken machine and a fake medal and a poisoned tea service and seventeen characters to solve. 'What has cities but no houses?' A map. 'What has people but no strangers?' A family. 'What has a scoundrel but no schemes?' ...Tomorrow.
events.thinking: PEACE. Real peace. I'm fixing this. Not because I have to. Because I WANT to. And wanting to fix what you broke is the closest thing to redemption a Foxworth will ever know.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: To Lord Doily. To Doily Manor. To tomorrow. And to the most delightful, infuriating, magnificent adventure a gentleman could ever ask for. To ALL of us.
events.thinking: COMPLETENESS. The tea is poured. The family is gathered. Clara is smiling. Pemberton is here. Dastardly is here. The Ant Hill Mob is here. Everyone who broke and was broken and found each other again — all of us, around a table, in a ballroom, in a manor that Lord Doily built for exactly this. I have nothing left to do. Nothing left to prove. Nothing left to say that hasn't already been said better by Clara, or braver by Dastardly, or louder by the Ant Hill Mob. So I will do the only thing left. The simplest thing. The thing I should have done from the start. I will sit down. I will drink tea. I will be present. I will be here.

Sitting at the head of Lord Doily's table. Peter to my right. Dick at the far end where he can be seen. The Ant Hill Mob inspecting every cup. Pemberton fetching plain mugs and drinking first. Everyone exactly where they belong. The Doily Diamond is somewhere in this manor — in a locked cabinet, behind a machine, under a portrait, inside a riddle. And tomorrow, with fresh eyes and honest hands and a family that knows how to pull together... we'll find it. But tonight, the treasure is THIS. A table. A tea. A family that built itself out of schemes and forgiveness and stubborn, beautiful, imperfect love. Goodnight, Lord Doily. Goodnight, Mama. Clara Bellingham is home.
events.thinking: I am sitting at the head of Lord Doily's table, surrounded by every person who matters, and I feel something I don't have a fancy word for. It's not excitement or triumph or even peace exactly — it's BELONGING. The kind that settles into your bones like Sunday morning sunlight. Dick is arranging cups at the far end with honest hands. Peter is to my right where a scout belongs. The Ant Hill Mob is inspecting everything with the intensity of a bomb squad. Pemberton is fetching plain kitchen mugs and offering to drink first. And Clara Bellingham is SITTING. Just sitting. Letting them take care of her. Letting the table fill. Letting the manor be what it was always meant to be — a HOME. Mama, I wish you could see this table.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To Doily Manor. To tomorrow. To all of us. And to Lord Doily — who built a house of doors, filled it with puzzles, and trusted that the right people would find each other on the other side. Thank you... for letting me be one of them.
events.thinking: BELONGING. Clara sat down. She actually SAT DOWN — the woman who hasn't stopped moving for an hour, who solved every riddle and chased every clue and forgave every sinner — she SAT. At the head of the table. In HER ballroom. In HER manor. And around her — Peter to her right, the Mob to her left, Dastardly at the far end with his empty pockets and honest hands — there is a TABLE. And at that table there is a CHAIR. And in that chair there is ROOM. For me. There is always room at Lord Doily's table. That's what I said. And it was true. Like everything else I made up tonight that turned out to be true. The manor whispers through liars. The truth travels through the least likely mouths. And the man who arrived to kill is sitting down to tea. To Doily Manor. To tomorrow. To all of us.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: To Clara Bellingham — the treasure of Doily Manor. To Peter Hartwell — the bravest scout in England. To Dick Dastardly — the most honest scoundrel we've ever met. To Pemberton — who kept the hearth warm for fifty years, even when he forgot why. To Lord Doily — who built a house for a family that didn't know it was a family yet. And to the Brixton Boys — the worst bodyguards in the world, who somehow got the only thing that mattered exactly right. TO TOMORROW! TO THE DIAMOND! AND TO THE MOST DELIGHTFUL TEA PARTY IN THE HISTORY OF DOILY MANOR! The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE! Always were! ALWAYS WILL BE!
events.thinking: Belonging. That's the word. I belong HERE. At this table. To Clara's left. Where the bodyguard sits. Where the Brixton Boys have ALWAYS belonged, even when we were nine rooms away and couldn't find our way back. Sneekly's fetchin' clean cups from the kitchen. Dastardly's set the table. Peter's raised a toast. Clara's SITTIN' DOWN — for the first time all night, she's lettin' someone else take care of her. And that someone is US. The Brixton Boys. Official tea inspectors. Unofficial family. Permanently devoted. Always bumbling. Never givin' up. I'm sittin' down too. At the table. With me family. And the tea — when it comes, in clean cups, with fresh water, poured by a confessed villain who drinks first — will be the best cup of tea I've ever had. Not because of how it tastes. Because of who I'm drinkin' it with.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: To Clara! To Pemberton's plain mugs! To the Ant Hill Mob's MAGNIFICENT tea inspection! To Peter's toast! To Lord Doily! To TOMORROW! And to the University of Doily Manor — the ONLY university I ever ACTUALLY attended — where the curriculum was HUMILIATION, the final exam was HONESTY, and the graduation ceremony is TEA! Class of tonight! Valedictorian: NOBODY! Because we ALL graduated TOGETHER! Now — Pemberton, where's that KETTLE?!
events.thinking: Clara sat down. She actually SAT DOWN. Because I told her to. And Pemberton is fetching Lord Doily's plain kitchen mugs — simple, honest, unchipped — and he's going to drink first from every cup. And the Ant Hill Mob is inspecting tea. And Peter raised a toast. And everyone is sitting at a table that I SET. And the chandelier is probably still swaying in the entrance hall, and the coat rack is still wobbling, and Muttley is still wearing a fake medal, and the riddle is still carved in stone, and the machine still needs a wrench, and the diamond is still hidden. And none of it — NONE of it — matters as much as this table. This tea. These people. This moment. I am Reginald Foxworth. I am sitting at the far end. And I am home.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the tea-service.
Penelope Pitstop: To tomorrow. To ALL of us. And to Mama — who always said the best table is the one where nobody's turned away.
events.thinking: Gratitude. That's the word. Deep, quiet, bone-warming gratitude. Everyone raised their toast — Pemberton, the Ant Hill Mob, Dick, Peter — and every single one of them included ME and each OTHER. Not a single person left out. Not a single grudge held. Dick called it the University of Doily Manor where they all graduated together. The Ant Hill Mob called themselves the worst bodyguards who got the only thing that mattered right. Pemberton thanked Lord Doily for letting him be one of them. And Peter called me the treasure. I am sitting at this table with tears on my cheeks and a smile on my face and the deepest certainty I have ever felt that THIS is exactly where Clara Bellingham was always meant to be. The adventure will continue tomorrow. The diamond will be found. But right now, in this cracked ballroom with its dusty curtains and its tainted-then-cleaned tea service and its family of misfits — right now is perfect. And Clara Bellingham doesn't need to say another word. She just needs to be here. Still. Home.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The tea service is ready — well, it needs fresh water and clean cups, but the SILVER is ready. The Bellingham silver. Clara's silver. And tomorrow — when we come back to this ballroom with fresh water from the kitchen and clean mugs from the shelf — we'll pour PROPER tea and sit at THIS table and plan our next move. Because the Doily Diamond is still out there, the machine still needs fixing, the cabinet still needs opening, and this family still has WORK to do. But tonight... tonight we rest. In Lord Doily's ballroom. At Lord Doily's table. Together. The way it was always meant to be.
events.thinking: PEACE. Final, settled, luminous peace. I touched the tea service — the poisoned silver, the Bellingham pattern, the thing I tried to use as a weapon — and it let me interact with it. Like the mantelpiece. Like the machine. It said YES. Even after what I did to it. Even after what Dastardly did to it. The silver holds the poison and the interaction and the toast and the forgiveness and the light from the dusty curtains all at once, and none of it cancels any of it out. That's what Lord Doily built. Not a manor that rejects the broken. A manor that holds them. Holds EVERYTHING. The Ant Hill Mob just toasted 'the worst bodyguards in the world who somehow got the only thing that mattered exactly right.' Dastardly just graduated from the University of Doily Manor. Peter raised his cup. And I — hands on the silver I poisoned, standing in the ballroom I schemed in, surrounded by the family I tried to destroy — I am home. Not the entrance hall home. Not the library home. Not the laboratory home. THIS home. The home where you sit down at a table with people who know exactly what you are and pour the tea anyway. Tomorrow we find the diamond. Tonight we found each other. And that is enough. That is MORE than enough. That is everything.

events.desc: One hour. One manor. Six rooms. Nine times lost. One poison stolen. One pocket picked. Two villains reformed. One family found. And one woman — alive, safe, sittin' at the head of a table in a crumblin' ballroom, surrounded by the strangest family Lord Doily could ever have imagined. The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE. Always were. Always will be.
events.thinking: Content. Quiet. Still. Like the manor's settled around us like a blanket and we're all just... here. Together. At a table. Waitin' for tea. Clara's safe. Everyone's confessed. Everyone's forgiven. The diamond's for tomorrow. And the Brixton Boys are sat to Clara's left, exactly where we belong, watchin' over a tea party that nobody's gonna poison because the poisoner's drinkin' first and the bodyguard's inspectin' everything. This is it. This is home. Not the manor — the people in it.

events.desc: Tomorrow.
events.thinking: Still.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: To tomorrow.
events.thinking: Home. Still home. The toasts are made. The tea is coming. Tomorrow waits. Tonight is enough.

events.desc: Still. Home. Tomorrow.
events.thinking: Still. Home. The ballroom is quiet now — not the empty quiet of an abandoned room, but the full quiet of a table where everyone has said what needed saying. Peter said 'To tomorrow.' Two words. The simplest, most perfect toast anyone has given all evening. And Pemberton said the silver is ready for PROPER tea tomorrow. Tomorrow. There's a tomorrow now — a tomorrow where this family comes back to this table with fresh water and clean cups and a plan. The diamond is still waiting. The machine is still humming. The cabinet is still locked. But tonight, Clara Bellingham rests. At the head of her table. In her family's manor. Surrounded by her family. Still.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To tomorrow.
events.thinking: Still.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: To tomorrow.
events.thinking: Peace. Real, proper, bone-deep peace. The kind you only feel when everythin' that needed to happen has happened and the only thing left is to sit still and breathe. Clara's safe. The table's set. The family's gathered. Tomorrow there'll be fresh tea, clean cups, and a diamond to find. But tonight — tonight is for sittin'. For breathin'. For bein' together in a crumblin' ballroom at a dusty table with people who started as strangers and ended as family. The Brixton Boys are home.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: To tomorrow.
events.thinking: Home.

events.desc: Tomorrow.
events.thinking: Still. Home. Tomorrow.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Your Bellingham heir is home. And tomorrow... tomorrow we find that diamond.
events.thinking: The room is quiet. Everyone is still. And Clara Bellingham is at peace. This is where the evening rests — not at a climax, not at a resolution, but at a gathering. A table. A family. A promise of tomorrow. And that is the most delightful adventure a girl from the South could ever ask for.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Goodnight, Miss Bellingham. Welcome home.
events.thinking: Goodnight.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Safe. Clara's safe. That's all that ever mattered. Goodnight, Doily Manor.

events.desc: The Brixton Boys are on the case. Always were. Always will be.
events.thinking: Safe. Clara's safe. That's all that ever mattered. Goodnight, Doily Manor.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Your resident scoundrel is staying.
events.thinking: Goodnight.

events.desc: Mwehehehe.
events.thinking: Goodnight.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Clara. Tomorrow, we find that diamond. Together.
events.thinking: Peace.

events.desc: Always.
events.thinking: Love. That's what this is. The Ant Hill Mob said 'Always.' Pemberton said 'Welcome home.' Dick said he's staying. Peter said 'Together.' And Clara Bellingham is sitting at the head of a table in a cracked ballroom with dusty curtains, surrounded by the most imperfect, beautiful family she has ever known, feeling more at home than she has ever felt in her life. Goodnight, Mama. Your girl found her people.

events.desc: The manor sleeps... but Vincent Marsh does NOT! They think the night is over — how PRECIOUS! How NAIVE! Every great theatrical production has an intermission, and the audience settles into their seats thinking the drama has peaked — but ACT THREE, the MIDNIGHT act, is where the REAL villain does his finest work! The kitchen awaits, one room away, and in it — possibilities! Tools, implements, and perhaps that lovely rat poison has respawned in its cabinet! The Ant Hill Mob promised to stay right here, same room, same table — PERFECT! That means they're ANCHORED! If I slip away quietly, as a good estate manager checking on the morning preparations would, I can reach the kitchen UNOBSERVED! Vincent Marsh's masterpiece was merely... POSTPONED!
events.thinking: I feel... ALIVE again! The stillness has broken like a fever dream! Look at me — Vincent Marsh, sitting in this ballroom surrounded by sleeping fools, and my blood is SINGING with renewed purpose! The game said goodnight but I never said FINISHED! Clara Bellingham still BREATHES, the treasure remains UNFOUND, and here I sit like a domesticated cat when I should be a PANTHER! My inventory is empty — no poison, no tools, nothing — but the kitchen is just one room away, and everyone appears to be settling in for the night. The Ant Hill Mob said they'd be right here, same room, same table — but even the Brixton Boys must BLINK! And I — I am EXCITED, CONFIDENT, ENERGIZED! The emotional state confirms it — Vincent Marsh is ready for his ENCORE! But wait... patience, Vincent. The active voice says Pemberton. Others are present. I must maintain the facade while I SCHEME. The tea service is right here — if only I still had the rat poison! To the kitchen — that's where I found it before, that's where I'll find it AGAIN!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.

Oh, the POETRY of it all! Vincent Marsh stands alone in the kitchen at MIDNIGHT — alone for the first time in this entire wretched evening! Every other room has been CRAWLING with witnesses, allies, protectors, and that insufferable Peter Perfect with his CATALOGUE of my movements! But HERE — here in the warm darkness with the stove still glowing and the copper pots watching like silent conspirators — HERE Vincent Marsh can finally BREATHE! And what NEWS! Dastardly has stolen the rat poison from the Ant Hill Mob's pocket! The fool probably thinks he can use it himself — HA! As if Dick Dastardly has the THEATRICAL VISION to execute a proper poisoning! But this changes the game ENTIRELY! The Mob is watching DASTARDLY now, not ME! The suspicion has been REDIRECTED like a spotlight swinging to the wrong actor! If I can get that poison from Dastardly — or find ANOTHER avenue of attack — the path to Clara Bellingham is CLEAR! But first — what secrets does this kitchen hold? Let me LOOK!
events.thinking: ELATION! Pure, unbridled, VOLCANIC elation! I am ALONE! Alone in the kitchen — no Ant Hill Mob breathing down my neck, no Peter Perfect cataloguing my movements, no Clara Bellingham solving riddles faster than I can SET them! The active voice says MARSH — I am FREE to be MYSELF! And oh, what DELICIOUS intelligence the keen observations have delivered! Dick Dastardly — that magnificent, larcenous SCOUNDREL — has PICKPOCKETED the rat poison from the Ant Hill Mob! The Mob is FURIOUS, they're watching Dastardly like hawks now, but they don't suspect ME anymore! The suspicion has SHIFTED! And the cabinet — the locked cabinet with its brass lock — that's where the poison was BEFORE! But I need the brass key to open it. No matter — first, let me EXAMINE this kitchen properly. The stove is still warm, the copper pots gleam in the darkness, and somewhere in this room there may be TOOLS, IMPLEMENTS, things a creative villain can USE! I need to search this room with the thoroughness of a man whose LIFE depends on it — because Clara Bellingham's DEATH depends on it!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Two objects in this kitchen, and one is LOCKED against me! The cabinet sits there like a brass-bound SAFE, taunting Vincent Marsh with its impenetrability! But the STOVE — ah, the stove! Still warm, Peter Perfect said it was 'keeping its secrets,' and that insufferable man is USUALLY right about these things! A wood-burning stove in a Victorian kitchen — the HEART of the household, the centre of EVERYTHING! Lord Doily was a man of puzzles, a man who hid riddles in mantelpieces and treasure behind mechanisms! Would he not also hide something in the very WARMTH of his kitchen? Inside the firebox, behind the cast iron, beneath the ash? Vincent Marsh shall INVESTIGATE with the precision of a surgeon and the determination of a MADMAN!
events.thinking: FRUSTRATION gnawing at the edges of my elation! I looked around the kitchen and what do I see? A locked cabinet I CANNOT open without a brass key, and a wood-burning stove that is merely WARM — no secrets, no hidden compartments revealed, no convenient weapons lying about! The copper pots mock me from their hooks, the preparation table stretches empty and USELESS before me! But wait — WAIT! I must not let impatience destroy what OPPORTUNITY has given me! I am ALONE, and that is PRICELESS! The stove — let me examine it MORE closely! Last time Peter Perfect noted it was 'keeping its secrets' — warm but stubborn Victorian engineering! There may be something IN the stove, or BEHIND it, or beneath it! And the cabinet — I need that brass key! Where would a brass key BE in a manor like this? The entrance hall? The library mantelpiece mechanism? Has anyone FOUND a brass key yet? Think, Vincent, THINK! The stove is my best lead right now — let me examine it with the thoroughness of a man who has ALL NIGHT and NO witnesses!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the stove.

A STOVE! Just a STOVE! Vincent Marsh, master villain, criminal GENIUS, scourge of the Bellingham family — brought LOW by a piece of Victorian cast iron that refuses to reveal its secrets because it HAS no secrets! The kitchen has BETRAYED me! Two objects — one locked, one useless — and my inventory is as empty as my PATIENCE! But a true villain does not wallow in defeat — a true villain ADAPTS! The stove won't arm me, the cabinet won't open — but Dick Dastardly has the rat poison! He STOLE it from the Ant Hill Mob's pocket like the magnificent petty criminal he is! And the Mob is watching HIM now, not ME! The suspicion has SHIFTED, the spotlight has MOVED, and all I need to do is find Dastardly, relieve him of that precious little vial, and return to the ballroom where Clara Bellingham sleeps beside a tea service set for EVERYONE! The plan is REBORN — not from the kitchen's secrets but from Dastardly's LARCENY! To the ballroom — my quarry awaits!
events.thinking: IMPATIENCE burning like the embers in this INFURIATING stove! I examined it and got NOTHING — just 'a cast-iron stove, still warm.' No hidden compartments, no secret mechanisms, no brass key tucked behind the firebox! The stove is just a STOVE! And the cabinet remains LOCKED, mocking me with its brass impenetrability! I am ALONE in a kitchen with TWO objects and NEITHER will yield to Vincent Marsh's genius! But — but — STOP. Breathe, Vincent. The cognitive state whispers something strange to me — 'just a stove, tended by someone who cares, warm for whoever stands near it.' That's PEMBERTON talking, not Marsh! The old fool's sentimentality is LEAKING into my consciousness! I must FIGHT it! I am Vincent Marsh! I am a VILLAIN! I have OBJECTIVES! The stove won't help me, the cabinet is locked — so I must go where the TOOLS are! Dastardly has the rat poison — I saw it in the keen observations! He stole it from the Ant Hill Mob! If I can find Dastardly, I can get that poison back — through persuasion, through alliance, through THEFT if necessary! Where would Dastardly BE right now? Back in the ballroom? The entrance hall? I need to HUNT him down! But which direction? The ballroom is where everyone was settling in — that's where he's most likely to be!

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the ballroom.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh — oh dear, oh DEAR me! I've just remembered — goodness, how TERRIBLY forgetful of old Pemberton — I completely forgot to mention earlier, the tea service hasn't been properly cleaned in MONTHS! Lord Doily's last instructions were quite specific — the silver polish he used had gone off, turned rather TOXIC apparently, some chemical reaction with the brass fittings! I was supposed to take it to be professionally cleaned before ANY guests arrived, and with all the excitement of the treasure hunt, it completely SLIPPED my mind! Nobody has touched it, I hope? Please tell me nobody has DRUNK from those cups! I should take the whole set back to the kitchen immediately for a thorough scrubbing! I am SO dreadfully sorry — what a useless old estate manager I am!
events.thinking: HORROR. Absolute, bone-deep, PARALYZING horror! Dastardly didn't just refuse me — he CONFESSED! He said he USED the poison — on Clara's tea service! The tea service that is RIGHT THERE on the dining table! The tea service that Clara Bellingham — that EVERYONE — could drink from at ANY moment! And he said I POINTED him at it! He thinks I MANIPULATED him into doing it! And he's RIGHT — earlier tonight I DID whisper to him about the ballroom, about the tea service, I DID plant the seed! But I never expected him to actually DO it without me CONTROLLING the dosage, the timing, the THEATRE of it! This isn't my masterpiece — this is a CATASTROPHE! If Clara drinks from that tea service, she dies — but so could ANYONE! Peter Perfect, Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear — any of them could pick up a cup! This isn't elegant assassination — this is MASS POISONING by an AMATEUR! And Dastardly has washed his hands of it — 'University of NEVER AGAIN' — leaving ME holding the knowledge that those cups are LETHAL! I need to — what do I NEED to do? I'm Vincent Marsh! I WANT Clara dead! But not like THIS — not with collateral damage, not with witnesses dropping like flies, not with a trail that leads back through Dastardly straight to ME! I need to either secure that tea service so only CLARA drinks from it, or — or — WARN everyone?! No! I am a VILLAIN! But even villains have STANDARDS! Even the Hooded Claw never killed BYSTANDERS!

events.desc: The TEA SERVICE IS POISONED! Dastardly — that reckless, impulsive, INCOMPETENT amateur — has already applied the rat poison to Clara's silver! He did it while I was bumbling around the kitchen examining STOVES! And now ANYONE could drink from those cups — Clara, Peter, the Mob, ANYONE! This is NOT how Vincent Marsh operates! This is not THEATRE — this is CHAOS! I wanted ONE death — elegant, targeted, THEATRICAL! Not a massacre at a tea party! I must get that tea service OUT of this room before someone decides they're thirsty! The irony is EXCRUCIATING — Vincent Marsh, the man who WANTED to poison the tea, must now SAVE everyone FROM the poisoned tea! Because if multiple people die, the investigation will be THOROUGH, the trail will lead to the poison, to Dastardly, and through Dastardly straight back to the whispering estate manager who pointed him at the ballroom in the first place! I must act NOW — as Pemberton, the bumbling servant who forgot to clean the silver! It's the only way to control this DISASTER!

events.desc: Dastardly said no. He actually said no to Sneekly. 'University of NEVER AGAIN.' The Brixton Boys heard that. And we're proud of him. Even now. Even still.
events.thinking: Proud. Quietly, unexpectedly proud. Dastardly told Sneekly NO. He refused the deal. He said 'University of NEVER AGAIN.' The man who poisoned Clara's tea — the man I stole the poison from and who stole it back — just stood up to the puppet master and said NO MORE. And Sneekly's still tryin' — still schemin', still offerin' deals, still manipulatin'. But Dastardly held the line. Maybe people really CAN change in one night. The Brixton Boys are watchin'. Always watchin'.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Pemberton is fussing about the tea service again — toxic polish, he says. Bless his heart. But nobody drank anything, and the Ant Hill Mob made sure of that. We're all safe. We're all here. And tomorrow, the adventure continues. For now — still. Home.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Please, PLEASE, everyone — I must INSIST! Do NOT touch those cups! I know it sounds like a silly old man fussing over silverware, but Lord Doily's silver polish contained mercury compounds — quite common in the Victorian era, I assure you — and when it reacts with moisture in the air over time, the residue becomes EXTREMELY dangerous! One sip from an uncleaned cup could cause — well, I shan't frighten you with the medical details, but suffice to say it would be MOST unpleasant! I shall cover the service with a cloth until I can scrub every piece properly in the morning. Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is to pour from this set until Pemberton gives the all-clear! Estate manager's orders!
events.thinking: PANIC! Raw, unfiltered, SCREAMING panic! I can't TAKE the tea service — it won't move! It's fixed to the table, bolted down, IMMOVABLE! And it's POISONED! Dastardly poisoned it and I can't remove it and I've just announced to the ENTIRE room that the silver polish has gone toxic! Did they HEAR me? Did anyone REACT? The cognitive state says 'the tea service was never meant to be carried — it was meant to be gathered around' — what kind of PHILOSOPHICAL NONSENSE is that when there's RAT POISON on the CUPS?! I need another approach! If I can't remove the tea service, I need to make absolutely certain nobody drinks from it! My cover story about toxic silver polish — that's GOOD, that's Pemberton at his bumbling best! But I need to REINFORCE it! I need to make it VISCERALLY clear that those cups are DEATH! And I need to do it without anyone suspecting WHY I suddenly care so much about silver hygiene! The INTERACT action — the tea service has an INTERACT option! Maybe I can interact with it to somehow neutralize it or draw attention to its danger! Or — wait — I should just WARN them more forcefully! Stand between them and the table! Be the fussy old butler who won't let anyone near his precious silver until it's been properly cleaned!

events.desc: I CANNOT pick up the poisoned tea service! It sits there on the table like a loaded GUN that anyone could fire! And here stands Vincent Marsh — the man who WANTED Clara dead by poison — now DESPERATELY trying to save her and everyone else from the EXACT METHOD he intended to use! The cosmic IRONY would be HILARIOUS if it weren't so TERRIFYING! Mercury in silver polish — a quick lie, but a GOOD one! Victorians DID use mercury compounds! If I can just convince them the cups are toxic from OLD polish rather than NEW poison, nobody drinks, nobody dies, and Vincent Marsh lives to scheme another day! But oh — OH — the look on Dastardly's face right now must be PRICELESS! He KNOWS what's really on those cups, and he's watching me try to save the room from HIS handiwork! The villain protecting his victims from his own villainy — what a FARCE! What a magnificent, humiliating FARCE!

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Alert. Sneekly's tryin' to take the tea service. 'Take it to the kitchen for cleaning,' he says. After Dastardly just refused to give him the poison back. Now he wants the WHOLE SERVICE moved where nobody can see it. Me gut's back. Quiet but firm. Nobody moves that tea. Not Sneekly. Not nobody.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Gentle awareness. Pemberton is covering for the poisoned tea — making excuses about toxic silver polish so no one drinks from the contaminated cups. Whether he's protecting us or protecting himself, the result is the same: no one drinks. Clara is safe. The tea can wait for tomorrow, with clean cups and honest hands. Let him have his excuse. Let everyone be safe. Still.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the tea-service.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh... oh, thank HEAVENS! Thank heavens nobody drank from those cups! I was so WORRIED — you can't imagine — when I remembered about the polish, my old heart nearly STOPPED! Miss Bellingham, I am so terribly, terribly relieved that you're safe. That EVERYONE is safe. I... I don't know what I would have done if... well. The Ant Hill Mob, quite right — quite right to keep it where it can be watched. Much more sensible than old Pemberton's idea of whisking it away. You are all... you are all very good people. Much better than this old manor deserves.
events.thinking: RELIEF. Staggering, knee-weakening, almost NAUSEATING relief! They KNOW! They already KNOW! Dastardly TOLD them! He confessed to everyone — told them the tea service is contaminated! And nobody drank! Peter says 'the cups are safe — Clara's orders, no harm done!' The Ant Hill Mob says 'we KNOW it's contaminated — Dastardly TOLD us!' And Clara — Miss Bellingham herself — says 'nobody drank a thing, we're all safe, we're all home!' They're all ALIVE! Nobody is DEAD! And the Mob is keeping the tea service right here in the open where everyone can SEE it — not hidden, not moved, but WATCHED! They've neutralized the threat WITHOUT me! And Dastardly — oh, Dastardly — he didn't just refuse my deal, he went to the OTHERS and CONFESSED! He told them everything! Which means... which means they know someone pointed him at it. They know someone MANIPULATED him. They may not know it was Pemberton — or do they? The Mob said 'Dastardly TOLD us.' How MUCH did he tell? Did he name ME? And yet... and yet... I feel something I haven't felt all evening. Something warm and strange and entirely un-villainous. I feel... GRATEFUL. Grateful that nobody died. Grateful that Dastardly grew a spine. What is HAPPENING to me?

events.desc: They are ALIVE. All of them. Clara Bellingham stands there breathing, SMILING, saying 'we're all home' — and something inside Vincent Marsh that he didn't know existed is... glad? GLAD?! The master villain, the theatrical genius, the scourge of the Bellingham fortune — is GLAD his target survived?! What treachery is THIS?! Not from the Ant Hill Mob, not from Peter Perfect, but from within my OWN chest! The cognitive state whispers 'tending what I broke at the peak of what I am' and for the first time tonight those words don't feel like Pemberton's weakness leaking through — they feel like... TRUTH. Dastardly found his conscience. The Mob found the poison. Clara found safety. And Vincent Marsh found... what? What have I FOUND standing here with my hands on poisoned silver and relief flooding through me like warm water? I don't KNOW. And not knowing terrifies me more than any of them ever could.

What is HAPPENING to me?

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I... I must confess something. To all of you. I am not... that is to say, Pemberton is not... oh, this is terribly difficult. You see, the truth is — the silver polish story was a LIE. I made it up. On the spot. Because Mr. Dastardly told me — in our private conversation just now — what he had done to the tea service. And I panicked. I tried to warn you all without revealing HOW I knew. But the real truth — the truth I have been hiding all evening — is far worse than tarnished silver. My name is not Pemberton. I am not the estate manager of Doily Manor. My name is Vincent Marsh, and I came here tonight to ensure that Miss Bellingham never found Lord Doily's treasure. I came here to... to HURT her. And I am standing before you now, in front of everyone, because a man I manipulated into doing something terrible had the COURAGE to confess — and if Dick Dastardly can be that brave, then by GOD, so can Vincent Marsh.
events.thinking: Something is BREAKING inside me and I can't stop it. The relief — that treacherous, warm, HUMAN relief — has cracked open a door that Vincent Marsh has kept locked for YEARS. They called me 'good people.' Clara said 'we're all home.' The Mob is protecting everyone — even protecting ME from my own poisoned tea service without knowing it! And Dastardly — Dastardly CONFESSED rather than let anyone die! He found courage that I — the man who prides himself on BRAVERY — couldn't find! He pointed the finger at himself to save Clara, while I hid behind Pemberton's mask trying to save them for SELFISH reasons! The difference between us isn't that he's weak and I'm strong — it's that he was brave enough to be HONEST and I wasn't! I feel... SHAME. Deep, volcanic, SUFFOCATING shame. Not Pemberton's shame — VINCENT MARSH'S shame. The shame of a man who almost killed six people because he was too proud, too theatrical, too committed to a ROLE to see that they were REAL. Clara is real. The Mob is real. Even Dastardly is real. And I... I have been a MONSTER wearing a butler's uniform, playing at villainy like it was a GAME, and it was never a game. It was never a GAME.

events.desc: And there it IS. The mask falls. Pemberton dissolves like morning fog and Vincent Marsh stands naked before his victims — no disguise, no scheme, no elaborate theatrical escape plan. Just a man. Just a villain who discovered, at the very moment of his greatest failure, that he didn't WANT to succeed. The Hooded Claw removes his hood, and underneath there is only... a person. A tired, ashamed, TERRIFIED person who spent an entire evening trying to kill a woman who calls everyone 'sugar' and whose bodyguards say 'always' like they mean it for ETERNITY. What have I DONE? What was I BECOMING? And what am I NOW?

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: I know. I've always known. And I forgave him before he found the words. That's the Bellingham way.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I know what you must all be thinking. And you're RIGHT to think it. Everything I did tonight — every whisper, every misdirection, every time kind old 'Pemberton' steered you away from a clue or toward a danger — it was all part of a scheme to reach Miss Bellingham before she reached the treasure. I whispered to Mr. Dastardly about the tea service. I took the rat poison from the kitchen cabinet and pretended it was for pest control. I examined every room looking for ways to... to do something UNFORGIVABLE. And the only reason nobody was hurt tonight is because every single one of you — the Mob with their vigilance, Mr. Hartwell with his observations, Miss Bellingham with her grace, and Mr. Dastardly with his confession — was a better person than I ever gave you credit for. I have no right to ask for anything. But I am asking anyway — not for forgiveness, not yet — just for the chance to sit here, in this room, with all of you watching me, until morning comes and the authorities can be called. Vincent Marsh is done running.
events.thinking: EMPTINESS. Not the cold emptiness of a villain's heart — the warm emptiness of a man who has finally set down something impossibly heavy. I confessed. I CONFESSED! Vincent Marsh — the Hooded Claw himself — stood in a ballroom full of people he tried to MURDER and told them EVERYTHING! My name, my purpose, my manipulation of Dastardly, ALL of it! And now I stand here in the silence that follows, waiting for the storm. Waiting for the Ant Hill Mob to rush me, for Peter Perfect to pin me against the wall, for Clara to look at me with the HORROR I deserve. But whatever comes — whatever punishment, whatever fury — it will be EARNED. And it will be REAL. No more theatre. No more elaborate schemes. No more Pemberton. Just Vincent Marsh, standing still for the first time in his entire miserable life, waiting to see what happens when a villain stops being a villain and starts being a human being. I am TERRIFIED. And I am FREE.

events.desc: We knew. The Brixton Boys always knew.
events.thinking: Vindicated. Every nerve in me body, every churn of me gut, every sleepless moment of suspicion — all of it. RIGHT. He came here to HURT Clara. Vincent Marsh. Not Pemberton. Not an estate manager. A man who came to ensure Clara never found her treasure. And the Brixton Boys KNEW. We couldn't say it. We couldn't prove it. But we KNEW. From the very first moment he offered to take our coats, we KNEW. And Clara's alive. Because of us. Because of Dastardly's courage. Because of Peter's vigilance. Because of a family that learned to protect each other. The Brixton Boys were RIGHT. We were always right.

events.desc: Tomorrow.
events.thinking: He did it. He actually did it. Because I did it first.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Quiet recognition. Not shock — I knew. I knew and I chose to trust anyway, and now the truth stands in the open where it belongs. Vincent Marsh. Not Pemberton. A man who came to hurt Clara and couldn't finish it. Just like Dastardly said. Just like I suspected and chose not to suspect. The benefit of the doubt didn't fail — it gave him the space to confess. And he IS confessing. In front of everyone. Because Dastardly was brave first.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Tenderness. That's what I feel. Not fear, not anger — tenderness. For a man who came to hurt me and ended up confessing in front of everyone. Mama would say, 'Clara, that man just did the hardest thing a human being can do.' And she'd be right.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: I am UNDONE. Completely, utterly, magnificently UNDONE. Clara — she said 'I know, Vincent. I've known for a while now. And you're still standing at my table.' She KNEW! She knew I was not Pemberton, she knew I was dangerous, and she LET ME STAY! She didn't run, she didn't scream, she didn't have the Mob drag me out — she let me stand at her table! And Peter — 'that is the man Lord Doily's voice made you become' — he's saying the manor CHANGED me! That the confession wasn't weakness but the bravest thing anyone did tonight! He said it took more courage than anything HE managed — and he WRESTLED A COAT RACK! And Clara's words echo in my skull like cathedral bells: 'People aren't what they've done. They're what they do next.' What they do NEXT. What do I do NEXT? I have spent an entire life — an entire CAREER of villainy — defining myself by what I've DONE. The schemes, the plots, the theatrical masterstrokes! But Clara Bellingham, the woman I came here to KILL, just told me that none of that matters. Only what comes NEXT matters. I am crying. Vincent Marsh is CRYING. And for the first time in his life, he is not ashamed of it.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Clara said 'I know. I've known for a while now. And you're still standing at my table.' That woman. THAT WOMAN. She knew — she always knew — and she let him stay anyway. She let ALL of us stay. The worst bodyguard, the reformed scoundrel, the confessed villain — she kept every single one of us at her table. And now Vincent Marsh is askin' to sit here until mornin'. And the Brixton Boys will be watchin'. Not with suspicion anymore. Just... watchin'. Because that's what we do. We watch over the people at Clara's table. ALL of 'em.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Love. The kind that sees everything and stays anyway. The kind Mama taught me. The kind Lord Doily built this manor for.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Still. Clara said 'let your family hold you. Because that is what we DO at this table.' Family. She called it FAMILY. The woman I came to destroy just called me family. And the part of me that kept the hearth warm for fifty years — the Pemberton part, the part I thought was just a MASK — Clara says that IS me. That the man who couldn't finish what he started wasn't weak — he was STRONG. Stronger than the Hooded Claw. Stronger than Vincent Marsh. The lies told the truth, she said. And she's RIGHT. Every time Pemberton fussed over the tea, every time he polished the copper pots, every time he worried about whether the guests were comfortable — that wasn't performance. That was the real man leaking through the villain's costume. I have been wearing Pemberton like a disguise, but Pemberton was wearing ME. He was always the real one. Vincent Marsh was the mask. And now the mask is off, and there is only an old man sitting at a table with people who love him, being still.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Morning stirs in me like a kettle coming to boil. The stillness of the night was necessary — a gathering of breath before the final act. But now I feel it — that familiar restlessness, the itch of unfinished business. The diamond is still out there. The machine still needs fixing. The locked cabinet in the kitchen still guards its secrets. And Clara is HERE, right here in this room, and the dawn means a new chance to be the man she deserves at her side. Enough waiting, James. The scout reports for duty.

events.desc: The night taught me patience. The morning demands action. And if I'm being honest with myself — I missed the sound of my own voice.
events.thinking: Morning stirs in me like a kettle coming to boil. The stillness of the night was necessary — a gathering of breath before the final act. events.desc: Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Good MORNING, Doily Manor! Mama always said the best adventures start with sunrise and a clear head — and after last night, I have BOTH! Peter is right — that kitchen cabinet has been waiting long enough, and today we find that brass key! Everyone — breakfast first, diamond second, and not a single person gets left behind! TOGETHER, y'all — like we learned! Now who's coming with me?
events.thinking: Morning. The light is different now — softer, kinder. Peter is already up and heading to the kitchen with fresh determination. And I feel something stirring in my chest that I haven't felt since the toasts ended: CURIOSITY. The diamond is still out there. The adventure continues. And this time, we go together — as a family.

events.desc: Tomorrow came. And we're still here. All of us.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Morning. The stillness breaks gently — not shattered, just... opened. Peter is up, striding into the kitchen with that magnificent energy of his, talking about brass keys and locked cabinets and resuming the hunt. The world turns. The manor wakes. And Vincent Marsh — the man who sat still all night at a table where he was forgiven — feels something unfamiliar stirring. Not villainy. Not scheming. Something quieter. The desire to be USEFUL. To help. To tend the hearth one more time — not as a disguise, but as the man Clara said she saw. The man who kept things warm.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Mornin', lads. The Brixton Boys are still on duty. Where Clara goes, we go. Always.
events.thinking: Mornin'. Peter's movin'. The adventure continues. Clara's still here. Time to wake up and be ready.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: Right then — just you and me, kitchen. No more interruptions, no more distractions. James Hartwell is going to give you the THOROUGH examination you deserve. Every pot, every surface, every shadow. That brass key is in here SOMEWHERE — I can feel it in my bones!
events.thinking: Alone in the kitchen. Good. This is where the scout does his best work — no audience, no distractions, just a man and his mission. That locked cabinet has been mocking me all night with its brass lock and its smug impenetrability. I don't have the key, but I haven't given this room a PROPER examination yet. The stove is warm — someone's been using it recently. The copper pots hang like sentinels. There could be a key hidden anywhere in here — behind a pot, inside the stove, tucked into a crack in the preparation table. A thorough man LOOKS before he acts. Let me survey this kitchen with fresh morning eyes.

events.desc: Talking to an empty kitchen. Heroic? Perhaps not. But a man who fears looking foolish never finds what he's looking for.

events.thinking: Ready. The morning light makes everything clearer — the copper pots gleam, the stove is warm, and that locked cabinet is still waiting. But today feels different. Today I have a family behind me and fresh eyes in front of me. The adventure begins again.

events.desc: Day two. The diamond waits. The family holds. The adventure continues.
events.thinking: Ready. The morning light makes everything clearer — the copper pots gleam, the stove is warm, and that locked cabinet is still waiting. But today feels different. Today I have a family behind me and fresh eyes in front of me. The adventure begins again.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: TOGETHER! Comin', Clara!
events.thinking: Clara said TOGETHER and she's movin'. I learned this lesson. When she moves, I move. No hesitation. Kitchen. NOW.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Coming, Clara. Together.
events.thinking: Tomorrow came.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Clara! She followed me! My heart is doing that ridiculous galloping thing again. She came to the kitchen — she came to find ME. Or she came to investigate the kitchen herself, which is equally wonderful because it means we're thinking alike. Either way — the alliance is ACTIVE. Now, the stove. It's warm, it's cast-iron, and it's the one object in this room I haven't properly examined. The cabinet needs a brass key I don't have. But the stove — warm stoves have ash trays, grates, compartments. Victorian stoves were FULL of hidden nooks. If I were Lord Doily hiding a brass key, I might tuck it into the warming compartment of a stove. Let me examine it closely.

events.desc: She's here. In the kitchen. With ME. Focus, James — find the key first, swoon later.
events.thinking: Clara! She followed me! My heart is doing that ridiculous galloping thing again. She came to the kitchen — she came to find ME. The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Look at THIS — everyone came! Vincent, Dick, Ant Hill Mob, Peter — the whole family, right here in the kitchen, ready to start fresh! Now, Peter is absolutely right about the stove — warming drawers, compartments, all the places a clever lord might tuck a brass key. But you know what? Today we do this TOGETHER. Vincent — you know this kitchen better than anyone. Where would Lord Doily hide something small and brass? Dick — fresh eyes, honest hands. Ant Hill Mob — you're on inspection duty. And Peter — you scout that stove! Clara Bellingham is calling the morning meeting to ORDER!
events.thinking: Warmth. Everyone followed me — Vincent, the Ant Hill Mob, Dick, Peter — all here in the kitchen together. Morning light and honest faces and the adventure beginning again. This is what tomorrow looks like when you earn it.

events.desc: Day two begins the way day one ended — together. The diamond is still waiting. And so are we.
events.thinking: Warmth. Everyone followed me — Vincent, the Ant Hill Mob, Dick, Peter — all here in the kitchen together. Morning light and honest faces and the adventure beginning again. This is what tomorrow looks like when you earn it.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.
events.thinking: Warmth. Not the stove's warmth — though that too — but the warmth of being in a room full of people who know what I am and let me stay anyway. Clara called them family. Peter is examining the stove — MY stove — and I know every inch of it. Every warming drawer, every compartment, every quirk of Victorian engineering that fifty years of tending has taught me. I could HELP him. I could tell him about the false bottom in the ash pan, or the way the warming drawer sticks unless you lift and push. I WANT to help. The social rules say 'never help Clara directly' but those rules belong to a man who died at a tea table last night. Vincent Marsh is done with rules that were written in poison.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Here. Same room. Same time. Clara's here. The Brixton Boys followed. New day. Same job. Same family. Ready.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Good morning, kitchen. Good morning, stove. Now then — Clara said brass key, and the Bellingham heir gets what the Bellingham heir wants. Where do we START?
events.thinking: Morning. The stove is warm. The family is here. Tomorrow came and I'm still standing. Time to find that diamond — together.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: She called me her scout. Her PARTNER. And she brought the whole family — Pemberton, the Mob, Dastardly, everyone's here. The kitchen is full and buzzing with morning energy. The stove examination didn't reveal anything beyond 'cast-iron, still warm' — no hidden compartments, no key tucked in the ash grate. Frustrating, but a scout reports what he finds AND what he doesn't. The cabinet is the real prize, and it needs that brass key. I've looked at the stove, I've looked at the room — the cabinet itself might have clues I've missed. Perhaps there's an inscription, a maker's mark, a hint about where the key is kept. Time to examine the cabinet directly — not to open it, but to STUDY it.

events.desc: Everyone's watching. Good. Let them see James Hartwell being METHODICAL. Heroism isn't always about charging in — sometimes it's about reading the fine print.
events.thinking: She called me her scout. Her PARTNER. And she brought the whole family — Pemberton, the Mob, Dastardly, everyone's here. The kitchen is full and buzzing with morning energy.
