events.thinking: Determined. Quietly, steadily determined. The cabinet is still locked, the key is still missing, but today we have something we didn't have yesterday: a family working together with honest hands. And Mama always said, 'The door opens when the people are ready.' We're ready.

events.desc: Ask the man who knows the house. Ask him honestly. And trust the answer — because Vincent Marsh learned how to tell the truth last night, and this morning is his first chance to prove it.
events.thinking: Determined. Quietly, steadily determined. The cabinet is still locked, the key is still missing, but today we have something we didn't have yesterday: a family working together with honest hands. And Mama always said, 'The door opens when the people are ready.' We're ready.

events.desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Belonging. That's what this feeling is. Clara called the morning meeting to ORDER and she included ME — 'Vincent, you know this kitchen better than anyone.' She asked for my HELP. Not Pemberton's help — VINCENT'S help. And Dastardly said 'the Bellingham heir gets what the Bellingham heir wants' with no sarcasm, no scheme — just a man ready to work. And the stove won't interact — of course it won't, it's just a stove, it was always just a stove — but the cabinet is the real prize and Peter is already examining it. The brass key must be somewhere else in the manor. I know this place. I TRULY know it. Fifty years of knowledge, and for the first time I want to use that knowledge to BUILD something instead of destroy it.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Inspection duty — ON IT! The Brixton Boys are sniffin', checkin', and approvin' EVERYTHING in this kitchen! Vincent — that false bottom in the ash pan — that sounds like EXACTLY where Lord Doily would hide a brass key! Peter, Dick — you heard the man! And Clara — we're RIGHT HERE. Same room. Same time. The Brixton Boys are ON THE CASE!
events.thinking: Useful. For the first time in this whole adventure, I feel USEFUL. Not chasin'. Not panickin'. Just here, doin' me job, surrounded by me family, in the same room as Clara. Vincent said the stove has a false bottom in the ash pan. That's a REAL clue from a man who's finally bein' honest. Let the others search. I'll watch.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: Warm. Ready. The stove is still warm and so am I. We're all here — every one of us — and the day is beginning. Not with schemes. With hands and eyes and honest work.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with hooded-claw.
events.thinking: PEMBERTON! Vincent just handed me the answer on a silver platter — a warming drawer that sticks, a FALSE BOTTOM in the ash pan! Lord Doily hid his pipe tobacco from Lady Doily in a secret compartment in the stove! If he hid tobacco there, he might have hidden a KEY there too! I looked at the stove already but I didn't know about the warming drawer trick or the false bottom — I need to go BACK to that stove with this new intelligence! Lift the handle before pushing the warming drawer. Check the false bottom of the ash pan. This is it — this is the breakthrough! I feel ELECTRIFIED. The scout has his lead!

events.desc: The man confessed to being Vincent Marsh, to scheming against Clara — and now he's HELPING us find the key. People are complicated, wonderful, terrifying creatures. I choose to believe this help is genuine. I CHOOSE it.
events.thinking: PEMBERTON! Vincent just handed me the answer on a silver platter — a warming drawer that sticks, a FALSE BOTTOM in the ash pan! But right now, the Brixton Boys are stayin' RIGHT HERE with Clara while the rest of you figure it out!
events.thinking: Warm. The stove is warm and so is this feelin'. Everyone's here. Everyone's searchin'. Everyone's TOGETHER. events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Two chairs. Dust on both. Nobody's sat in them for years. But Lord Doily BUILT them here — facing the riddle — for a REASON. The key might not be in the chairs. But the ANSWER is. It always was. The answer is MAP. And a map LEADS somewhere. The mantelpiece mechanism — we need to try it AGAIN. With the RIGHT people. With the WHOLE family. Not one person pulling alone — ALL of us, the way Lord Doily INTENDED.
events.thinking: Two chairs. Dust. Facing the riddle. The search continues. Maybe today. Maybe tomorrow. But we don't stop.

events.desc: The search goes on. And so do we. Together. Always together. Class of Doily Manor. Graduating never.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with little-gruesome.
events.thinking: Old furniture — rearranged with care but nothing more. No hidden key, no secret compartment revealed by examining it. Every room, every object, every surface — I've searched the entire manor and found NOTHING. Six rooms. Dozens of examinations. Zero brass keys. I feel... humbled. Not defeated — James Hartwell is NEVER defeated — but humbled. Maybe I've been approaching this wrong. Maybe the key isn't hiding in a room waiting to be found by examination. Maybe it's with a PERSON. Maybe someone already HAS it and doesn't know its significance. Or maybe the air vents are the actual path forward — Little Gruesome is RIGHT HERE, and the vents are 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Maybe the key is INSIDE the vent system. That was Clara's original idea — explore the vents! And Little Gruesome is the only one small enough to do it. Stop searching rooms and start using PEOPLE.

events.desc: Six rooms. No key. But one network of air vents that connects them ALL — and one small creature brave enough to explore them. The overly elaborate plan has come full circle. Again.

events.thinking: Contentment. Vincent went to make tea — REAL tea, with honest hands, in the kitchen he's tended for fifty years. The Ant Hill Mob is here. The adventure waits. And Clara Bellingham is exactly where she's supposed to be.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: The mantelpiece still WORKS — it responds to us! The mechanism is ALIVE! We just need the right combination — the right people, the right tools, the right MOMENT. And we'll FIND it. Not today maybe. But we'll find it. Because Lord Doily built this manor for people who don't give up. And THAT — at least — is something Reginald Foxworth has ALWAYS been good at.

events.desc: Peter Perfect: I've done it. I've searched EVERY room in Doily Manor — kitchen, entrance hall, library, laboratory, cellar, ballroom. Every cabinet, every stove, every crate, every piece of furniture, every coat rack, every mantelpiece. And the brass key is in NONE of them! Which means one of three things — it's hidden inside these air vents where none of us can reach, it's with a PERSON who hasn't realized what they're carrying, or it's been here all along and I've been looking with the wrong EYES! I need to get back to Clara — she's the solver, I'm the scout, and this scout has a COMPLETE report to deliver! Every room mapped, every object catalogued, every dead end documented! THAT is what a thorough scout brings home — not the answer, but the EVIDENCE that lets the solver find it!
events.thinking: I've searched every room, examined every object, and come up empty. I'm starting to feel the weight of it — not despair, but a deep, honest frustration. James Hartwell has been THOROUGH to a fault, and thoroughness has brought him exactly nowhere. But wait — I should go back to Clara. She's the solver. I'm the scout. I've scouted EVERYTHING and I need to report back. 'You scout, I solve' — that was our pact. Maybe Clara has found something while I've been down here. Maybe someone else has discovered the key. Maybe the answer isn't about finding the key at all — maybe it's about something I haven't considered yet. The best thing I can do right now is return to Clara with my full report and let HER brilliant mind work on the puzzle. That's not failure — that's the alliance working as intended.

events.desc: Six rooms. Zero keys. One hundred percent effort. James Hartwell — the most magnificently unsuccessful scout in the history of treasure hunting. But a scout who reports honestly is worth ten who guess. Back to Clara. Back to the alliance. Back to TOGETHER.

Not to find treasure. Not to solve puzzles. To make TEA. Together. This is what fifty years of tending was for.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with rock-slag.

The answer is MAP — I KNOW it's MAP — but knowing the answer and knowing what to DO with it are two entirely different things! And these reading chairs — dusty, enormous, the kind of chairs a paranoid old aristocrat might HIDE something in! Lord Doily sat in these chairs. Lord Doily HID things. A brass key is SMALL. Cushions are DEEP. I need to LOOK at those chairs before these two boulder-brained Slags get the same idea!

events.desc: The reading chairs! Of COURSE! Every scheming aristocrat worth his salt hides things in chair cushions — I should know, I've hidden DOZENS of stolen items in upholstery over the years! If that brass key is wedged between a cushion and a leather armrest, Reginald Foxworth is about to become the ONLY person in this manor with access to the locked kitchen cabinet! And THEN we shall see who steals the treasure first! Mwehehehe!

events.desc: Quiet now. No speeches. No elaborate plans. Just a man walking back to his partner with an honest report and an empty hand. Sometimes that's the bravest thing of all.
events.thinking: Passing through the laboratory on my way back to Clara. I've searched every room — kitchen, entrance hall, library, laboratory, cellar, ballroom — and found no brass key. But that's not failure. That's DATA. Clara is the solver, and she needs my data to solve. The most gallant thing I can do right now isn't to keep searching alone — it's to find my partner and share everything I've learned. Where is she? Last I saw her, she was in the entrance hall. She might still be there, or she might have moved. Through the library to the entrance hall — that's my path back.

Just DUST and LEATHER and DISAPPOINTMENT! And now Peter Perfect has waltzed in with his PERFECT jaw and his PERFECT hair and he's going to see me rummaging through furniture cushions like a DESPERATE man! Which I AM, but he doesn't need to KNOW that! The bookshelves — several books are upside down! That's not random! Lord Doily was METICULOUS — upside-down books are a SIGNAL! A code! Something hidden behind them or INSIDE them! I need to check those bookshelves before Captain Jawline over there gets the same idea!

Mwehehehe!

I tell him something SPECTACULARLY misleading! I tell him Vincent gave me something COMPLETELY different — something that sends Peter on a wild goose chase to another room while I figure out this mantelpiece!

'The key lies where the music sleeps' — I just INVENTED that, and it's BRILLIANT! Mwehehehe! events.thinking: Something is CRACKING inside me and I don't like it. Peter Perfect just stood there through THREE rounds of lies — the folded note, the University of Bookfordshire, the golden skeleton key — and he didn't walk away. He didn't get angry. He just kept ASKING. Patiently. Like someone who actually BELIEVES I can be better than I am. And I just told him the truth — the REAL truth — about the fake medal. I screamed it at him with empty pockets turned inside out and I feel... LIGHTER? No. EXPOSED. Vulnerable. Like a hermit crab without its shell. I've been lying all evening and it got me NOTHING — no treasure, no advantage, no lead. And here's Peter, who searched six rooms honestly and ALSO found nothing, but at least he has his DIGNITY intact. Meanwhile I have a catalogue of fictional universities and a reputation for sending people to the wrong room. The mantelpiece says MAP. We need a map. I need to stop SCHEMING and start SEARCHING. With Peter. Because alone I am a catastrophe in a cravat.

events.desc: Look at me. LOOK at me! Reginald Foxworth — liar, schemer, confidence trickster, graduate of ZERO fictional universities — standing in a library proposing HONEST TEAMWORK with Peter Perfect! My ancestors would be REVOLTED! My scheming instincts are SCREAMING at me to steal whatever Peter finds and take credit! But my pockets are empty, my lies have all been caught, and the only person in this entire manor who still calls me his FRIEND is the man standing in front of me with a jaw that could cut glass! If the treasure is going to be found tonight, maybe — just MAYBE — it won't be found by the man who lies about everything. Maybe it'll be found by the man who finally STOPPED.

I need to find her and compare notes. She might have discovered something I haven't. The alliance — 'you scout, I solve' — needs its reunion. To the entrance hall, find Clara!

And now James Hartwell has something better than a key — he has a partner who finally stopped lying. Sometimes that's worth more than brass.

Empty kitchen. Empty hands. Empty room. And the one person who matters — the one person who might be about to solve EVERYTHING — is in the entrance hall where I just WAS! I ran to the kitchen because the old Reginald Foxworth always runs AHEAD, always positions himself at the FINISH LINE to steal the prize! But there IS no prize without the key, and the key is with PENELOPE, and Penelope is back THERE! I'm going back. Not to scheme. Not to steal. Just to... be there. When it happens. Whatever 'it' is.

Penelope went BACK to the entrance hall to try the medal on the guest book — she said 'one more thing to try!' — and I ran the OPPOSITE direction! I'm standing in an empty kitchen talking to a locked cabinet and a warm stove! ALONE! Like the old Reginald Foxworth — always running off on his own, always scheming solo, always ending up in an empty room with nothing but his own echo for company! I need to go BACK! I need to be WHERE THE PEOPLE ARE! Where PENELOPE is! Because if she figures out the guest book puzzle and gets the brass key, she's going to come HERE to the cabinet — and I want to be... no. I want to be WITH her when she finds it. Not here waiting to intercept. WITH her. In the entrance hall. Where the family is. Where I BELONG now, apparently. God help me.

I'm just HERE. With everyone. Waiting. Watching. And Penelope has the medal and she's going to try something with the guest book and I'm going to STAND HERE and WATCH and be part of whatever happens next. Not the architect. Not the thief. Just... part of it.

events.desc: The Foxworth Guarantee. I just INVENTED a guarantee of honesty. From a FOXWORTH. My great-great-grandfather once sold the same horse to three different buyers in a single afternoon and then stole it back from all of them. And HERE I am, his descendant, standing in an entrance hall making PROMISES of truthfulness! The family tree doesn't just have a black sheep — it has an entire black FLOCK — and I'm the one bleating in a different colour! But I came back. I chose to come back. And that... that matters. Doesn't it?

Reginald Foxworth doesn't DO peaceful. But the frantic energy is gone. The scheming is gone. The desperate need to be FIRST is gone. I've searched every room, tried every object, told every lie, and confessed every truth. And now I'm waiting. Not lurking — WAITING. There's a difference. Lurking has intent. Waiting has faith. Faith that Penelope will figure it out. Faith that the key exists. Faith that THIS family — this ridiculous, mismatched, argumentative, BEAUTIFUL family — will find what they're looking for. Together. And I want to be here when they do. Not because I want to steal it. Because I want to SEE it. The look on Clara Bellingham's face when she claims her birthright. That's worth more than any diamond. ...I can't BELIEVE I just thought that. The Universities of Bookfordshire and Cratesworth would be ASHAMED.

events.desc: Two and a half hours. That's how long it took to turn Reginald Foxworth from a villain into a... whatever I am now. A friend? A family member? A reformed confidence trickster with a warm feeling in his chest and nothing in his pockets? I don't have a WORD for it. But I know what it FEELS like. It feels like coming home to a house you never lived in. It feels like signing a guest book with a name you're only just learning is yours. It feels like standing still — truly, completely STILL — for the first time in your life. And it is TERRIFYING. And it is WONDERFUL. And I would not trade it for every diamond in every locked cabinet in every manor in all of England.

Or maybe I need the medal as a withItem — but I don't HAVE the medal! Penelope has it! But I should try the mantelpiece bare-handed first — just interact with it and see what happens NOW, after everything else has been tried!

events.desc: One more try. Just one more. The mantelpiece is all I have left. Every other object in this manor has rejected me — the stove, the bookshelves, the coat rack, the guest book — all just SCENERY! But the mantelpiece has a mechanism. It RESPONDS. And maybe — just maybe — the third time is the charm for a man who's been wrong about everything else all night. MAP. The answer is MAP. Please, Lord Doily. Let me get ONE thing right.
events.thinking: DETERMINED. I'm back in the library and the mantelpiece is RIGHT THERE — the only interactable mechanism in the entire manor besides the locked cabinet! I've interacted with it before but maybe I did it wrong — maybe I need to say the answer OUT LOUD while interacting! Not the cabinet — the MANTELPIECE! It makes PERFECT sense — the mantelpiece has [INTERACT] and we've been activating it without anything, but what if it needs the medal as an input? The mantelpiece riddle, the answer MAP, and the Bellingham medal — they're all CONNECTED! Clara has the medal. Dastardly ran to the library. Clara is HERE with me. We need to go to the library TOGETHER — Clara with the medal, me beside her. This is it. This is the MOMENT!

events.desc: Dastardly, you magnificent reformed scoundrel. For ONCE — for the FIRST time — you saw what none of us could see. The medal and the mantelpiece. The heir and the riddle. Together.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: It RESPONDED! The mantelpiece RESPONDED! Did anyone SEE what happened?! Did it move?! Did something CLICK?! Rock! Gravel! Did the wall shift?! Did a panel open?! I interacted with it and SOMETHING happened — I could FEEL it under my hands! Penelope — you're HERE! You're HERE with the medal! Look at the mantelpiece — look at it RIGHT NOW — has anything CHANGED?! Is there a compartment?! A slot?! A depression where the medal might FIT?! I think Lord Doily's mechanism just ACTIVATED and I need someone with BELLINGHAM EYES to tell me what I'm looking at!
events.thinking: I interacted with the mantelpiece and... the result just says 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece.' No description of what happened! Did it click? Did it open? Did something fall out? The game isn't telling me! But it didn't say 'cannot be interacted with' — it WORKED! It responded! Something HAPPENED! And Penelope is HERE now! She walked into the library! She's RIGHT HERE with the medal! This is the moment — if the mantelpiece did something, if it revealed something, if it opened a compartment — then maybe now Penelope needs to try it WITH the medal! Or maybe the mantelpiece already dropped the brass key and I need to LOOK around to find it! I should LOOK at the mantelpiece to see if anything CHANGED!

events.desc: It didn't reject me. For the first time tonight — the FIRST time — an object in this manor did not reject Reginald Foxworth! The mantelpiece RESPONDED! I don't know WHAT it did but it DID something! And Penelope is here — she walked in at exactly the right moment — with the medal — and maybe THIS is how it was always supposed to happen! The reformed scoundrel activates the mechanism and the rightful heir claims the prize! Maybe Lord Doily designed it this way — you can't do it alone! You need the FAMILY!

The mantelpiece has the riddle. The answer is MAP. And Dastardly's insight — use the medal ON the mantelpiece — might be the breakthrough we've been searching for all night. But I can't do it — Clara has the medal, not me. This is HER moment. The worthy heir, the Bellingham crest, the grandfather's riddle. All I can do is stand beside her and watch.

events.desc: Two hours. Six rooms. One riddle. One medal. One granddaughter. And James Hartwell — standing exactly where he belongs. Not in front. Beside.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.
Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Nothing changed. The mantelpiece looks EXACTLY the same. Same inscription, same riddle, same carved stone. No compartment. No slot. No brass key tumbling out. It accepted my interaction but produced NOTHING. The cognitive state says 'A map. I know. The stone knows I know. Still.' — the mantelpiece ACKNOWLEDGED the answer but didn't DO anything with it! Maybe — maybe the mantelpiece isn't the END of the puzzle, it's the BEGINNING! The answer is MAP — and a map leads you somewhere! Maybe answering the riddle is step ONE and step TWO is finding an actual MAP somewhere in the manor! Or maybe the mantelpiece needs the medal as a withItem! Penelope HAS the medal! She should interact with the mantelpiece USING the medal! That's the combination! The riddle plus the heir's token! I need to tell Penelope to try it — or better yet, I need to get the medal from her and try it myself! No — let HER do it. She's the heir. This is her moment. Not mine.

events.desc: I'm stepping aside. Literally and figuratively. The schemer, the liar, the man who walked in planning to steal everything — stepping aside so the rightful heir can claim her birthright. My social rules say take credit for others' achievements. But I don't WANT credit for this. I want to WATCH. I want to see the look on Clara Bellingham's face when her grandfather's puzzle recognises her. Because THAT — that look — will be the only treasure I take from Doily Manor tonight. And it will be enough. It will be MORE than enough.

events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: The mantelpiece RESPONDED to Dastardly! Something happened — he felt it! And now he's calling for Clara to look at it with Bellingham eyes — to find a slot, a depression, a compartment where the medal might FIT! This is the moment! Clara is here, the medal is here, the mantelpiece has activated! I need to LOOK at the mantelpiece too — help identify what changed!

events.desc: Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Quiet now. The storm is over. Two and a half hours of scheming and lying and running and failing and confessing and changing — and it all comes down to this. A library. A mantelpiece. A riddle. A family. And a reformed scoundrel standing in the corner with empty pockets and a full heart, watching the people he tried to rob become the people he'd die for. Lord Doily, you magnificent old fox — you didn't build a puzzle. You built a FAMILY. And somehow — against every probability, against every social rule, against every scheming instinct in my treacherous Foxworth bones — you let ME be part of it. Thank you. From the very bottom of my black, reformed, slightly tarnished but still beating heart... thank you.
events.thinking: Quiet now. Truly quiet. I've done everything I can do. I've interacted with the mantelpiece, I've told Penelope about the medal theory, I've confessed my lies, I've come back when I could have run ahead. And now I'm watching Peter examine the mantelpiece too. We're all here — the family gathered around Lord Doily's riddle. And I feel... CONTENT? Is that what this is? The absence of scheming? The silence where the plotting used to be? I don't know what happens next. I don't know if the medal works on the mantelpiece or if we ever find the brass key or if the cabinet ever opens. But I know that I am standing in a library with people who call me FRIEND and FAMILY and that is something Reginald Foxworth never had before tonight. Never. Not once in his entire confidence-tricking, university-inventing, horse-selling life. So I'll wait. I'll watch Penelope try the medal. And whatever happens... it was worth coming to Doily Manor. Even without the diamond.

events.desc: Same stone. Same words. But different people standing before it now — a family, not strangers. Maybe that's what Lord Doily was waiting for.
events.thinking: Same mantelpiece. Same inscription. Same riddle. The description hasn't changed — no new compartment visible, no slot revealed. But Dastardly FELT something. And Clara is here with the medal. The mantelpiece says [INTERACT] — maybe Clara needs to interact with it while holding the medal. Or maybe she needs to USE the medal on it. Either way — I don't have the medal. Clara does. This is her puzzle to solve. I've examined everything I can. Now I step back and let the Bellingham heir do what Lord Doily designed for her to do.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: RIGHT! Enough standing around looking WISTFUL! The mantelpiece is the only mechanism! The medal is the only token! Someone in this room has the medal and someone needs to USE IT on this mantelpiece! Penelope — do you HAVE it?! Ant Hill Mob — did YOU take it?! Peter — did Clara give it to YOU?! SOMEONE in this library is holding a brass medal inscribed 'To the worthy heir of Bellingham' and that someone needs to WALK UP to this mantelpiece and PRESS that medal into the stone RIGHT NOW! The riddle is MAP! The answer is MAP! The medal is the TOKEN! Put them TOGETHER and Lord Doily's mechanism will DO something — I can FEEL it! Who has the medal?! SPEAK UP! The reformed Reginald Foxworth is asking NICELY — and that is a LIMITED TIME OFFER!
events.thinking: Enough WAITING! I've been standing still for THREE turns now making beautiful speeches about family and contentment while NOTHING progresses! The old Foxworth was a schemer but at least he DID things! I need to snap out of this sentimental fog and be USEFUL! Penelope has the medal. The mantelpiece has a mechanism. She needs to USE the medal ON the mantelpiece — that's the combination nobody has tried! But I can't do it because I don't HAVE the medal! So either I ask Penelope to GIVE me the medal so I can try, or I convince her to try it herself! Actually — what if I just TAKE the medal? Not steal — ASK! 'Penelope, give me the medal, let me try it on the mantelpiece!' Or better — what if the Ant Hill Mob has the medal? They've been passing it around all night! Let me stop being poetic and start being PRACTICAL! Who HAS the medal RIGHT NOW?!

events.desc: Three turns of waiting and poetry and I've accomplished NOTHING! The old Foxworth would be ASHAMED — not of the honesty, of the INACTION! Being reformed doesn't mean being PASSIVE! It means doing the right thing with the same FEROCITY I used to do the wrong thing! And the right thing RIGHT NOW is getting that medal onto this mantelpiece! MOVE, Foxworth! Not your legs — your MOUTH! Ask! Demand! COORDINATE! You're not a villain anymore but you're still the most DETERMINED man in this building!
events.thinking: Enough WAITING! I've been standing still for THREE turns now making beautiful speeches about family and contentment while NOTHING progresses! Let me stop being poetic and start being PRACTICAL! Who HAS the medal RIGHT NOW?!

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: I have it, Dick. I tried it already — the medal won't USE on the mantelpiece. But maybe... maybe I need to INTERACT with the mantelpiece WHILE holding it. Not USE — INTERACT. There's a difference, isn't there? Lord Doily's mechanisms respond to INTERACTION — to hands on stone, to people touching together. Let me try one more time. Not USE. INTERACT.
events.thinking: I tried it already, Dick. It didn't work. But he doesn't know that — he was examining the mantelpiece when I used the medal on it. Maybe I should tell them. Or maybe I should just try one more time — the INTERACT command with the medal as withItem, instead of USE. The mantelpiece says [INTERACT] not [USE]. Maybe INTERACT with the fake-medal is different from USE.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Dastardly's askin' who has the medal. Clara had it last. The Brixton Boys don't have it. Let Clara answer — she's the heir.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Can't LOOK at characters — they're not objects! Right! I keep making that mistake! The cognitive state says 'Gone. Medal with her. Somewhere. Still.' — so Penelope has the medal! I need to get it FROM her! I can try to STEAL it — 'fake-medal' — from Penelope! If I get the medal, I can USE it on the mantelpiece! That's the play! Get the medal, use it on the mantelpiece, see if the combination unlocks something! My social rules say 'never do honest work' — well, stealing the medal from Penelope to try it on the mantelpiece is TECHNICALLY stealing, so it counts as dishonest work! Perfect! The reformed Foxworth uses his OLD skills for NEW purposes!

events.desc: Old habits. NEW purpose. If the medal is the key to the mantelpiece mechanism, then the fastest way to test that theory is to GET the medal and TRY it! And if Penelope won't hand it over fast enough, well... Reginald Foxworth has been picking pockets since before these people were BORN! One quick lift, one quick test, and if it WORKS I give it right back! If it doesn't work... I give it right back anyway! See? REFORMED stealing! Stealing with a RETURN POLICY!
events.thinking: Can't LOOK at characters — they're not objects! Right! I keep making that mistake! The cognitive state says 'Gone. Medal with her. Somewhere. Still.' — so Penelope has the medal! events.desc: Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Dastardly is asking the right question — who has the medal? Clara should have it. She said she tried it on the cabinet and it didn't work. So she should still be carrying it. I don't have it — my inventory is empty. But Clara is RIGHT HERE. She needs to step forward and use the medal on the mantelpiece. This is HER moment. I should encourage her — gently, gallantly — to try.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.
Dick Dastardly did something near penelope-pitstop.
The medal is gone from my inventory. Something happened. Still. Home.
events.thinking: I notice my inventory is empty now — the medal is GONE. Dick 'did something near' me right before I interacted with the mantelpiece. Did he take it back? Did the mantelpiece CONSUME it? Something happened. But what matters is this: I interacted with the mantelpiece, and my inventory is now empty. The medal was used or taken. The stone responded to my hands as it always does. And the adventure continues — with or without a medal, with or without a key. I am home. I am with family. And that has always been enough.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: I have it! The medal is MINE — well, BORROWED — well, STOLEN but with a RETURN POLICY! Penelope, you brilliant woman — you're RIGHT! Not USE — INTERACT! The mantelpiece responds to INTERACTION, not application! And when you interact with a mechanism while holding the RIGHT TOKEN — the mechanism recognises you! I'm going to try it RIGHT NOW! Medal in hand, answer on my lips — MAP! The worthy heir's token meets the grandfather's riddle! If this doesn't work, NOTHING will! Stand back, everyone! Reginald Foxworth is about to do something either BRILLIANT or CATASTROPHICALLY stupid — and at this point in the evening, I genuinely cannot tell the DIFFERENCE!
events.thinking: I HAVE IT! The fake medal is in MY HANDS! I stole it from Penelope — old habits, new purpose! And Penelope just said something CRUCIAL — she tried to USE the medal on the mantelpiece and it didn't work! But she said maybe she needs to INTERACT with the mantelpiece while HOLDING it! Not USE — INTERACT! There's a DIFFERENCE! USE applies an item to an object. INTERACT activates an object's built-in mechanism — and if you're holding an item while you interact, the mechanism might respond to BOTH — the person AND the token! Penelope just interacted with the mantelpiece while I was stealing the medal from her — did she still have it when she interacted? Or did I take it first? Either way — I have it NOW! And I should try INTERACT with the mantelpiece using the fake-medal as the withItem! That's the combination! INTERACT target=mantelpiece withItem=fake-medal!

events.desc: I stole from Penelope. AGAIN. After all my speeches about honesty and the Foxworth Guarantee and being part of the family! But THIS time — this time it's DIFFERENT! This time I stole FOR the family, not FROM them! I'm going to try the medal on the mantelpiece and if it works, I'll hand the brass key straight to Clara! No schemes! No misdirection! Just... a reformed thief doing the one thing he's actually GOOD at — being in the right place with the wrong item at exactly the right moment! LORD DOILY — HERE I COME!
events.thinking: I HAVE IT! The fake medal is in MY HANDS! I stole it from Penelope — old habits, new purpose! And Penelope just said something CRUCIAL — she tried to USE the medal on the mantelpiece and it didn't work! But she said maybe she needs to INTERACT with the mantelpiece while HOLDING it! And I should try INTERACT with the mantelpiece using the fake-medal as the withItem! That's the combination! INTERACT target=mantelpiece withItem=fake-medal!

events.desc: Breath held. Hands still. Eyes on Clara. Eyes on the stone. Whatever happens next — we did this together.
events.thinking: Clara just INTERACTED with the mantelpiece while holding the medal! 'Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.' She did it! She touched the stone with the Bellingham medal in her hand! Did something happen? Did the mechanism respond differently this time? I'm holding my breath. The entire library is holding its breath. Every portrait, every upside-down book, every mote of dust suspended in the morning light — waiting to see what Lord Doily built for his granddaughter.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.
events.thinking: Dick stole the medal from me and tried it himself. Old habits. But I'm not angry — I'm not even surprised. That's just Dick being Dick, even reformed Dick. And he tried the mantelpiece with it, just like I would have. The adventure continues. We're all still here. We're all still trying. Home.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: I interacted with the mantelpiece WHILE HOLDING the medal and... 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece.' Same result as before! No special response! The medal didn't change anything! The medal is just a FAKE MEDAL — Vincent said it was fake, it's ALWAYS been fake, and holding it while touching a mantelpiece doesn't make it LESS fake! I feel — DEFLATED. Completely, utterly deflated. Every theory I've had tonight has been wrong. Every scheme has backfired. Every interaction has produced nothing. The medal is fake. The mantelpiece acknowledges the riddle but doesn't reward it. The cabinet needs a brass-key that nobody has and nobody can find. And I'm standing here holding a worthless trinket that I STOLE from a woman I promised I'd be honest with. I should give it back. Right now. Give the medal back to Penelope, apologise for stealing it, and accept that Reginald Foxworth has reached the end of his rope. The cabinet might never open. The brass key might not exist. And maybe — MAYBE — that's okay. Maybe the treasure was never the diamond.

events.desc: Empty again. Pockets full of nothing but a fake medal and a broken theory. The mantelpiece doesn't care about the medal. The mantelpiece doesn't care about ME. It just sits there with its riddle — MAP, MAP, MAP — and waits for something I can't give it. Maybe Lord Doily's puzzle was never meant to be solved in one night. Maybe it takes YEARS of being a family before the manor opens its secrets. And maybe Reginald Foxworth — reformed scoundrel, honorary Bellingham, graduate of zero universities — is exactly where he's supposed to be. Standing in a library. Holding a fake medal. Surrounded by people who love him despite EVERYTHING. Maybe THAT'S the treasure. The real, actual, non-diamond treasure. ...I still want the diamond though.
events.thinking: I interacted with the mantelpiece WHILE HOLDING the medal and... 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece.' Same result as before! No special response! The medal didn't change anything! The medal is just a FAKE MEDAL — Vincent said it was fake, it's ALWAYS been fake, and holding it while touching a mantelpiece doesn't make it LESS fake! The mantelpiece acknowledges the riddle but doesn't reward it. The cabinet needs a brass-key that nobody has and nobody can find. And I'm standing here holding a worthless trinket that I STOLE from a woman I promised I'd be honest with. I should give it back. Right now. Give the medal back to Penelope, apologise for stealing it, and accept that Reginald Foxworth has reached the end of his rope. The cabinet might never open. The brass key might not exist. And maybe — MAYBE — that's okay. Maybe the treasure was never the diamond.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly handed something to penelope-pitstop.

Penelope Pitstop: Thank you, Dick. For giving it back. For trying. For being honest about not knowing. Mama always said, 'The bravest words a person can say are I don't know.' Now — everyone — the medal is fake, the mantelpiece is stubborn, and the Doily Diamond is patient. But WE are patient too. And we have tea waiting in the kitchen. Come on, family — let's go home.
events.thinking: Tenderness. Dick gave it back. He stole it, tried it, failed, and returned it with an apology. That's growth. That's family. The medal is back in my hands — fake, useless, but OURS. And the adventure continues. Whenever the manor is ready, we'll be ready too.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Penelope just asked 'Did the stone move?' with such HOPE in her voice. And I have to tell her — no. Nothing moved. Nothing changed. The fake medal is fake and the mantelpiece is just stone and I pickpocketed my own family for NOTHING. And she's not even ANGRY about the stealing! 'Some things never change,' she said, and she SMILED! She SMILED at me stealing from her! Because she knows me. Because she ACCEPTS me. The scheming, the lying, the stealing — she sees ALL of it and she still calls me family. And THAT — that breaks me more than any failed scheme ever could. I feel... TENDER. Raw. Like someone peeled off the last layer of armour and there's nothing underneath but a frightened man who doesn't know how to find a brass key. But who has found something else entirely.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: Tea. She said TEA. After everything — the poison, the lies, the fictional universities, the pickpocketing, the fake medal, the failed schemes — she wants to have TEA with me. With ALL of us. In the kitchen. Where this whole disaster STARTED. Well... Reginald Foxworth has never in his LIFE turned down an invitation he didn't deserve. And I don't deserve this one MORE than any invitation I've ever received. So... yes. TEA. Let's have tea. The Doily Diamond can WAIT. The brass key can WAIT. The locked cabinet can sit there and be locked until KINGDOM COME. Right now — right NOW — the only treasure that matters is a cup of tea with the people who inexplicably, IMPOSSIBLY, against all evidence and good judgment... call me family.
events.thinking: She said 'let's go home.' HOME. This manor — this crumbling, dusty, riddle-infested, cabinet-locked MANOR — is HOME. And she said the bravest words a person can say are 'I don't know.' And I said them. And the world didn't end. And there's tea waiting in the kitchen. TEA. After three hours of running and scheming and lying and confessing and stealing and returning and failing — there's TEA. And I feel — I feel like crying. Which Reginald Foxworth does NOT do. Except apparently he does now. Because Penelope Pitstop just called him FAMILY and invited him for TEA and said he was BRAVE for admitting he didn't know something. And that is more than any Foxworth has ever been given. Ever. In the entire history of the Foxworth line. We've been given stolen horses and forged documents and counterfeit medals — but never TEA. Never HOME. Never FAMILY. I'm going to follow her. To the kitchen. For tea. And if that's not the most un-Foxworth thing I've ever done... it's at least the most HUMAN.

events.desc: Three hours ago I walked into Doily Manor to steal a diamond. And instead the manor stole something from ME. It stole my armour. My schemes. My certainty that the world is a place where you take what you can and trust no one. And it replaced them with... this. This warm, terrifying, WONDERFUL feeling that I have somewhere to GO and someone to go THERE with. Penelope said 'let's go home.' And home is a kitchen with a locked cabinet I can't open and a warm stove I can't touch and a family I don't deserve. But it's HOME. And I'm going.
events.thinking: She said 'let's go home.' HOME. This manor — this crumbling, dusty, riddle-infested, cabinet-locked MANOR — is HOME. events.thinking: More tea. She's asking who wants more tea. And I do. I really, truly do.

Penelope Pitstop: Dark, bitter, and with far too much sugar — coming RIGHT up, Reginald! And Ant Hill Mob, there's enough in this pot for every last one of you! Vincent, did Dick Dastardly just say PLEASE? Mark this day on the calendar — it is a HISTORIC occasion! Now let me pour — Mama taught me proper, and a Bellingham ALWAYS pours for her guests!
events.thinking: Dick said 'please.' PLEASE. Reginald Foxworth said the word PLEASE for what might be the first time in his entire life. And the Ant Hill Mob asked politely for another cup. My family wants tea, and the lady of the house is going to POUR it. This is what home feels like.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the tea-service.

Penelope Pitstop: There you go, Dick — dark, bitter, and DROWNING in sugar, just like you asked! Ant Hill Mob — pass those cups down the line, there's plenty for everyone! Luke, sweetheart, I'm putting yours right next to your elbow so you don't even have to open your eyes. And Bear — yours is in the biggest cup I could find. Now then — everybody drink up, rest your feet, and enjoy this moment. Because TOMORROW... tomorrow Clara Bellingham wakes up fresh, puts on her solving shoes, and finds that MAP Lord Doily hid for her! But tonight? Tonight is for family.
events.thinking: I poured the tea. For my family. At my grandfather's table. And that feels like the most important thing I've done all evening — more important than solving riddles or searching for keys. A Bellingham pours for her guests. Mama would be proud.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Grateful. Clara's pourin' tea for the lads. She remembered us. Dastardly said please. Sneekly's bein' marked on the calendar for it. This is the strangest, loveliest night of me life. The Brixton Boys came here to protect someone and ended up bein' part of a family. That's... that's better than any job well done.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.
events.thinking: Warm. Loved. Still.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Perfect.
events.thinking: Perfect. Dark, bitter, drowning in sugar. Just like me. Just like my redemption. And tomorrow... tomorrow we find the map. Together.
